title: An interpretable machine learning model for MRI-based morphological classification of lumbar disc herniation using functional biomechanical features.
abstract: Introduction Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) is commonly assessed using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), although disc morphology does not necessarily correspond to pain intensity, functional impairment, neurological findings, or prognosis. This retrospective single-center exploratory study examined whether functional biomechanical indicators were associated with MRI-based morphological classification of LDH. Methods A total of 58 patients were included, comprising 15 patients with disc bulging and 43 with disc protrusion or extrusion. Five predictors-lumbar extension, straight-leg-raising asymmetry, side-flexion asymmetry, gluteus medius asymmetry, and right Jiaji regional surface electromyography root mean square-were used to construct an interpretable L2-regularized logistic regression model. Model performance was evaluated using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times, with participant-level out-of-fold probabilities averaged across repetitions. Predictors were selected before cross-validation; therefore, the reported performance may include selection-induced optimism. Results The model achieved a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.705 (95% confidence interval: 0.537-0.851), a precision-recall area under the curve of 0.844, and a Brier score of 0.218. At the exploratory Youden threshold of 0.566, balanced accuracy was 0.714, sensitivity was 0.628, specificity was 0.800, positive predictive value was 0.900, and negative predictive value was 0.429. A prespecified threshold of 0.500 yielded a balanced accuracy of 0.692, sensitivity of 0.651, and specificity of 0.733. Calibration was suboptimal, with an intercept of 0.999 and a slope of 0.752. In a separate exploratory bootstrap analysis, coefficient sign stability ranged from 97.0% to 99.9%, although the intervals remained wide. Discussion These findings suggest preliminary associations between selected functional biomechanical indicators and MRI-based disc morphology. Given the small and imbalanced sample, predictor-selection optimism, limited negative predictive performance, suboptimal calibration, and absence of external validation, the model should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than as a standalone clinical decision-support tool.

title: An interpretable multimodal morphomolecular model refines progression-risk stratification in early-stage endometrioid endometrial carcinoma.
abstract: Background Risk stratification remains incomplete for patients with FIGO stage I-II endometrioid endometrial carcinoma (EEC) despite clinicopathological assessment and molecular subtyping. Interpretable integration of diagnostic tissue morphology with molecular programmes may provide complementary information for progression-risk assessment. Methods We developed a prototype-resolved interpretable survival model (PRISM), a multimodal framework integrating haematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images with RNA-seq-derived pathway programmes for progression-free survival risk assessment. PRISM was developed in 287 eligible TCGA-UCEC patients with EEC, comprising a training cohort (n = 229) and a held-out internal validation cohort (n = 58). After model specification was fixed, PRISM was retrained on all 287 cases and evaluated without further tuning in an independent CPTAC-UCEC cohort of 63 patients with EEC. Prototype-pathway alignment provided tissue- and pathway-level interpretation of model predictions. Results Among 350 patients with EEC and matched multimodal data, PRISM achieved C-indices of 0.770, 0.751 and 0.745 in the TCGA training, internal validation and CPTAC external validation cohorts, respectively. In CPTAC-UCEC, the 36-month time-dependent AUC was 0.727, compared with 0.685 for the clinicopathological and molecular subtype baseline model. In a complementary fixed-horizon analysis, adding PRISM to the clinicopathological model increased the 36-month AUC in CPTAC-UCEC from 0.609 to 0.719. The PRISM risk score remained associated with progression-free survival after multivariable adjustment. Prototype-resolved analyses linked higher-risk predictions to localised histomorphological patterns and pathway programmes related to proliferation, cell-cycle activity, glycolysis, hypoxia, focal adhesion and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Conclusion PRISM showed prognostic discrimination in an exploratory independent external evaluation and provided a biologically interpretable framework for integrating histopathology and transcriptomics to refine progression-risk assessment in early-stage EEC. Further validation in larger, prospective, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish its generalisability and clinical utility.

title: Noninvasive diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease: a review of emerging biomarkers and multimodal approaches.
abstract: Noninvasive biomarkers are expanding access to biological assessment of Alzheimer's disease (AD). This review evaluates blood-based, neuroimaging, retinal, electrophysiological, digital, and behavioral measures alongside structured cognitive and functional assessment, and examines multimodal and machine-learning approaches for detection, differential diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. Plasma phosphorylated tau, particularly p-tau217, currently offers the strongest scalable evidence for identifying amyloid and advanced tau pathology, whereas PET and MRI retain complementary roles in pathological confirmation, regional staging, exclusion of alternative causes, and characterization of atypical phenotypes. Retinal, electrophysiological, speech, sleep, and eye-tracking measures remain promising but require greater standardization and external validation. Across modalities, biomarker trajectories are temporally staggered, assay and platform differences affect interpretation, and pathology-phenotype mapping is modified by disease stage, cognitive reserve, copathology, vascular factors, and population characteristics. We therefore propose a phenotype-anchored, stepped pathway that begins with patient and informant history, objective cognitive and functional assessment, structural imaging, and routine laboratory evaluation; adds validated blood biomarkers when they resolve a defined uncertainty; and reserves CSF or PET for unresolved, atypical, or treatment-relevant cases. Discordant findings should prompt reassessment rather than automatic reclassification. We describe the literature-search and descriptive evidence-categorization approach used to select and categorize the evidence reviewed, and we place the findings within the emerging regulatory context of blood-based testing. Clinical translation will depend on harmonized thresholds, representative prospective cohorts, calibration, independent validation, and evidence that multimodal systems improve decisions and patient outcomes rather than benchmark accuracy alone.

title: Differential diagnosis of pulmonary Talaromyces marneffei infection and pulmonary tuberculosis in HIV/AIDS patients using a CT-based multimodal 2.5D deep learning approach.
abstract: To investigate the diagnostic value of a computed tomography (CT)-based multimodal 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) deep learning model for differentiating Talaromyces marneffei (TSM) from pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) in patients with human immunodeficiency virus infection/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (HIV/AIDS). A total of 380 HIV/AIDS patients with pulmonary infections who were admitted to the Fourth People's Hospital of Nanning from January 2018 to August 2025 were retrospectively enrolled, including 203 patients with PTB, 177 with TSM. The cohort was randomly divided into a training set and a test set at a ratio of 7:3. A clinical model, a radiomics model, and a 2.5D deep learning model were constructed separately. In the clinical feature model, Random Forest achieved the optimal performance, with a test set AUC of 0.856. In the radiomics model, XGBoost attained the highest AUC of 0.866. In the 2.5D deep learning model, ResNet18 performed best at the slice level with an AUC of 0.865, and the patient-level support vector machine (SVM) model based on MIL achieved an AUC of 0.885. The multimodal combined model integrating clinical, radiomics, and deep learning features achieved the highest AUC of 0.931 and a specificity of 0.981. It significantly outperformed the clinical model (P = 0.020) and the radiomics model (P = 0.008), but the improvement over DL25D was not statistically significant (ΔAUC = 0.046; P = 0.116). The high specificity of the combined model should be interpreted alongside its sensitivity (0.717) and the selected decision threshold. The CT-based multimodal 2.5D deep learning model effectively integrates clinical indicators, radiomics features, and deep learning representations, and substantially improves the differentiation of TSM from PTB in HIV/AIDS patients.

title: Circulating CARMN for acute myocardial infarction prognosis and its incremental effect when combined with conventional biomarkers.
abstract: Background This study aims to explore the clinical value of lncRNA CARMN in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients. Methods The study subjects included 156 AMI patients and 59 healthy controls. The serum CARMN levels were detected by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). The correlation between CARMN and myocardial injury markers, as well as cardiac ultrasound indicators by Pearson analysis. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression were employed to screen out the independent influencing factors for MACE in AMI patients, and a nomogram was constructed. Results In patients with AMI, the serum CARMN level is decreased. CARMN level correlated with cTnI, CK-MB, Myo, LVEF. A total of 156 patients with AMI were enrolled and followed up for 6 months, among whom 60 patients experienced MACE. Lower CARMN levels were associated with a higher incidence of MACE. The AUC of the combined model for predicting MACE reaches 0.867, and the nomogram has good calibration and high clinical net benefit. Conclusion Serum CARMN combined with myocardial injury markers and ultrasound indicators, may help predict MACE risk in patients with AMI.

title: CTA-based morphological parameters predict adverse prognosis in stanford type B aortic dissection: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Objective To investigate the prognostic value of computed tomography angiography (CTA)-based morphological parameters for adverse aortic events in patients with acute Stanford type B aortic dissection (TBAD) and to develop an internally validated prediction model. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 292 consecutive patients with CTA-confirmed acute TBAD. Baseline clinical and CTA-derived morphological variables were collected, and the primary endpoint was a composite of adverse aortic events. Candidate predictors were evaluated using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, precision-recall analysis, and decision curve analysis, with internal validation based on 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Results During a median follow-up of 13.20 months (interquartile range, 8.15-19.52 months), 78 patients (26.7%) experienced adverse aortic events. The final LASSO-selected model included age, symptom onset-to-admission time, white blood cell count, D-dimer, maximum aortic diameter, TL/FL ratio, and false lumen status. In multivariable analysis, older age (adjusted OR = 1.043), higher white blood cell count (OR = 1.164), higher D-dimer (OR = 1.056), and larger maximum aortic diameter (OR = 1.110) were associated with higher odds of adverse events, whereas a higher TL/FL ratio was inversely associated with the outcome (OR = 0.060). Compared with partial false-lumen thrombosis, patent false lumen was associated with higher odds (OR = 3.718), whereas complete thrombosis was associated with lower odds (OR = 0.253). The apparent AUC was 0.849 (95% CI: 0.800-0.898), and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.828 after 1,000 bootstrap resamples. The optimism-corrected calibration slope and Brier score were 0.893 and 0.143, respectively. The AUPRC was 0.708 vs. a no-skill baseline of 0.267, and decision curve analysis showed positive net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. Conclusion A model integrating baseline clinical and CTA-derived morphological characteristics demonstrated good internally validated discrimination and reasonable calibration for short- to medium-term adverse aortic events in acute TBAD. Independent external validation is required before broader clinical application.

In multivariable analysis, older age (adjusted OR = 1.043), higher white blood cell count (OR = 1.164), higher D-dimer (OR = 1.056), and larger maximum aortic diameter (OR = 1.110) were associated with higher odds of adverse events, whereas a higher TL/FL ratio was inversely associated with the outcome (OR = 0.060). Compared with partial false-lumen thrombosis, patent false lumen was associated with higher odds (OR = 3.718), whereas complete thrombosis was associated with lower odds (OR = 0.253). The apparent AUC was 0.849 (95% CI: 0.800-0.898), and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.828 after 1,000 bootstrap resamples. The optimism-corrected calibration slope and Brier score were 0.893 and 0.143, respectively. The AUPRC was 0.708 vs. a no-skill baseline of 0.267, and decision curve analysis showed positive net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities.

Conclusion

A model integrating baseline clinical and CTA-derived morphological characteristics demonstrated good internally validated discrimination and reasonable calibration for short- to medium-term adverse aortic events in acute TBAD. Independent external validation is required before broader clinical application.

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived hemodynamics predict adverse outcomes after Fontan palliation.
abstract: Background Long-term outcomes following the Fontan procedure remain heterogeneous, and robust imaging-based predictors of adverse events are limited. Patients residing at moderate-altitude may experience additional pulmonary vascular stress; however, the prognostic value of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived flow parameters in this population are not well defined. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of Fontan patients followed at a single moderate-altitude center who were ≥5 years post-Fontan and had undergone comprehensive CMR exams. Demographic, anatomic, and surgical data were collected. CMR-derived variables included indexed ventricular volumes and function, systemic arterial dimensions, and flow indices in the ascending and descending aorta, superior vena cava (SVC), inferior vena cava, and branch pulmonary arteries.The primary composite outcome was death or referral/listing for heart transplantation. Time-to-event analyses from the time of CMR were performed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox proportional hazards regression. Results A total of 182 Fontan patients were included (median age at Fontan 3.2 years [interquartile range (IQR) 2.6-3.9]; median time from Fontan to CMR 10.9 years [IQR 7.7-14.2]). Over a median follow-up of 4.7 years following CMR (IQR 3.1-6.6), 14 patients (7.7%) experienced the primary outcome. In univariable Cox regression, a higher SVC flow index was significantly associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome [hazard ratio [HR] 0.70 per 0.1 L/min/m 2 increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.50-0.92; p = 0.008]. Conclusions In this moderate-altitude Fontan cohort, reduced CMR-derived SVC flow index was significantly associated with the primary outcome. This finding suggests that systemic venous flow merits further investigation as a prognostic marker in the Fontan population.

title: Synthetic preimplantation factor ameliorates the severity of radiotherapy-induced heart disease in a rat model.
abstract: Background Radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD) is a potential side effect of radiotherapy (RT) for thoracic tumors and breast cancers, often causing diastolic dysfunction, left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), and fibrosis. Preimplantation factor (PIF), an embryonic immunomodulatory peptide, has shown protective effects against acute radiation syndrome. We investigated whether synthetic PIF (sPIF) could mitigate RIHD development in rats and tumor cell proliferation in human breast cancer cell lines. Methods Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats were allocated into three experimental groups: vehicle-treated control, vehicle-treated RT (50 Gy, focused on the heart), and RT treated with sPIF, monitored at 1, 3, and 15 weeks. Endpoint assessments included transthoracic echocardiography, histopathology, qPCR, Western blotting, and UHPLC-MS/MS in the left ventricular (LV) samples. The effects of sPIF on hypertrophy, fibrosis, and proliferation were investigated in H9c2 cardiomyoblasts, human ventricular cardiac fibroblasts (HVCFs), and human breast carcinoma cells, respectively. Results sPIF decreased LV expression of inflammatory markers at week 3 and attenuated RT-induced LVH and fibrosis, with reduced nitrotyrosine accumulation at week 15. sPIF suppressed angiotensin II-induced hypertrophy in H9c2 cells, inhibited transforming growth factor- β 1 (TGF β 1)-induced collagen-1 expression in HVCFs, and enhanced the anti-proliferative response to RT in human breast carcinoma cells. Conclusions These findings suggest the potential of sPIF as a cardioprotective agent for the management of RIHD and warrant further mechanistic investigations.

title: Perivascular fat attenuation index improves the identification of functional myocardial ischemia beyond traditional risk factors: a coronary CT angiography-derived fractional flow reserve study.
abstract: Background Perivascular fat attenuation index (FAI) derived from coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a novel imaging biomarker of coronary inflammation. However, its incremental value in predicting functional myocardial ischemia, defined by CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR), beyond traditional cardiovascular risk factors and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume remains unclear. Methods A total of 380 consecutive patients who underwent clinically indicated CCTA with CT-FFR evaluation were retrospectively analyzed. Functional ischemia was defined as CT-FFR ≤0.80. Patients were stratified into low and high FAI groups based on the optimal cutoff value of -81.32 Hounsfield Units (HU). Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of ischemia. The incremental diagnostic performance of adding FAI to a baseline clinical model was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Despite comparable baseline profiles for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, body mass index, and glycemic status ( P > 0.05), patients in the high FAI group exhibited significantly lower CT-FFR values (0.75 ± 0.13 vs. 0.79 ± 0.12, P = 0.0017). After adjusting for age, gender, traditional cardiovascular risk factors, and EAT volume, average FAI remained a robust independent predictor of functional ischemia [Adjusted Odds Ratio [OR]: 1.056 per 1 HU increase; 95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 1.019-1.096; P = 0.004]. Notably, EAT volume did not reach statistical significance in the multivariate model ( P = 0.584). The addition of FAI to the clinical model resulted in a modest, non-significant improvement in AUC (0.731 vs. 0.707, P = 0.087), but yielded significant improvement in risk reclassification (continuous NRI: 0.339, P = 0.001; IDI: 0.024, P = 0.002). Subgroup analysis demonstrated a consistent risk trend across varying degrees of stenosis, age, and body mass index categories (OR range: 1.03-1.07). DCA confirmed superior net clinical benefit for the FAI-integrated model across a wide threshold probability range (25%-75%). Conclusions Coronary perivascular FAI is an independent imaging marker for CT-FFR-defined functional ischemia and provides incremental value beyond traditional risk factors and EAT volume. These findings support FAI as a non-invasive marker of coronary inflammation that may refine risk stratification for functionally significant coronary artery disease. However, as CT-FFR mainly reflects epicardial physiology, the association between FAI and microvascular dysfunction remains to be determined.

title: Differential sparse attention framework for accurate ovarian cancer subtype classification using DenseNet121.
abstract: Ovarian cancer is the most fatal gynecologic cancer, contributing to approximately 207,000 deaths per year worldwide, largely due to late-stage diagnosis and considerable histopathological diversity across subtypes. Accurate subtype classification is clinically important for prognosis and treatment planning, but remains challenging due to high inter-class morphological similarity and the scarcity of adequately labeled histopathological datasets. This study presents a novel attention module, Deep Differential Sparse Attention (DDSA), designed for multi-class classification of ovarian cancer subtypes in histopathology images. The module selectively amplifies discriminative tumor regions while suppressing irrelevant background features, thereby improving both feature representation and model interpretability. A dataset of 3,082 images spanning five subtypes i.e., Clear Cell Carcinoma, Endometrioid Carcinoma, High-Grade Serous Carcinoma, Low-Grade Serous Carcinoma, and Mucinous Carcinoma--was obtained from Kaggle. The training set was balanced to 5,940 images (1,188 per subtype) using RandomOverSampler, with on-the-fly data augmentation applied during training. DDSA was integrated into a DenseNet-based architecture, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using standard classification metrics, including precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, and ROC curves. The proposed model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 92.53%, with a macro-average recall of 91.54% and a macro-average F1-score of 0.90. AUC values ranged from 0.92 to 0.99 across all five subtypes, indicating strong and consistent classification performance on the test set. These results suggest that attention-guided DenseNet architectures can enhance discriminative feature extraction and improve diagnostic accuracy for ovarian cancer subtype classification. The DDSA module's ability to highlight tumor-relevant regions also supports improved model interpretability, an important consideration for clinical adoption. While these findings are promising, further validation on larger, multi-institutional datasets is needed to confirm robustness and generalizability, and to assess the framework's readiness for clinical deployment.

title: A robust lightweight deep learning network with deformable convolutions for efficient segmentation of optical coherence tomography images.
abstract: Introduction Manual segmentation and evaluation of optical coherence tomography (OCT) images are difficult and rely on specialist training, which limits the output in a busy clinic. While automatic segmentation can ease this burden, the deep models that currently lead the field tend to be too heavy for routine deployment on standard clinical hardware. A further obstacle is the unusual geometry of OCT data: instead of compact objects on a background, the structures of interest form long, undulating tissue strata that extend horizontally across the whole frame, and this layout is poorly matched to convolutional kernels designed for ordinary photographs. Methods We address both issues with LiDeOCTNet, a compact segmentation backbone tailored to the layered nature of OCT. Within a reduced UNet, we introduce learnable sampling offsets so that each kernel can reshape itself locally and trace the curved, irregular interfaces between tissues. To assess the design, we evaluate the network on three OCT collections covering retinal as well as endoscopic acquisitions. Results Across all three, LiDeOCTNet surpasses a parameter-matched UNet baseline and approaches the accuracy of much heavier benchmarks such as TransUNet, despite using about 750× fewer parameters and running roughly 7.4× faster at inference. Discussion Together these properties point to LiDeOCTNet as a practical option for real-time OCT analysis pipelines, including embedded and resource-limited devices.

title: Automated voxel-based prostate volumetry improves PSA density-based detection of clinically significant prostate cancer in the PSA gray zone: comparison with manual segmentation and the ellipsoid formula.
abstract: Purpose To investigate whether voxel-based prostate volume can improve the diagnostic performance of prostate-specific antigen density (PSAD) for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) in patients within the prostate-specific antigen (PSA) gray zone (4-10 ng/mL), and to compare it with conventional formula-based estimation. Methods In this retrospective study, 489 patients with PSA levels of 4-10 ng/mL who underwent prostate MRI were included. Prostate volumes were calculated using three methods ellipsoid formula ( PV formula ), manual voxel-based segmentation ( PV mask ), and automated voxel-based segmentation ( PV auto_seg ) based on nnU-Net. Agreement between volumetric measurements was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, and PSAD was calculated according to three prostate volume estimations. Diagnostic performance for the detection of csPCa was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results PV formula systematically overestimated prostate volume compared with PV mask , with mean volumes of 58.8 ± 28.1 mL and 54.5 ± 26.6 mL (bias 4.4 mL); whereas PV auto_seg (55.8 ± 20.8 mL) showed close agreement with PV mask and reduced bias of 1.4 mL. In ROC analysis, voxel-based PSAD mask (AUC 0.762, 95% CI 0.717-0.808) outperformed the formula-based PSAD formula (AUC 0.719, 95% CI 0.671-0.767; P = 0.01). PSAD auto_seg calculated from PV auto_seg yielded an AUC similar (0.754, 95% CI 0.707-0.800) to that of with PSAD mask , and also outperformed PSAD formula ( P = 0.02). Conclusion Voxel-based prostate volumetry provides more accurate and consistent volume estimation than the conventional ellipsoid formula, leading to improved PSAD performance for detecting csPCa in the PSA gray zone. Moreover, automated segmentation enables reliable and scalable PSAD calculation with diagnostic performance comparable to manual delineation, supporting its potential for clinical implementation in risk stratification of PCa.

title: Augmentation or erosion? Artificial intelligence and the transformation of clinical reasoning: a critical narrative review.
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are used to support diagnosis, but a model's accuracy does not establish that clinicians reason more accurately when they use it. This review appraises how AI decision support and large language models affect physicians' diagnostic performance and the risks of relying on them. Methods This critical narrative review follows the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles. Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO and LILACS were searched in July and August 2026 in English, Spanish and Portuguese. Eligible studies, published from 2015 onward, compared AI-assisted with unassisted clinicians, measured reliance on AI or unassisted performance after exposure to it, or externally validated deployed models. A single author selected sources purposively. Nine primary studies were appraised with an adapted Critical Appraisal Skills Programme framework. Results In randomized trials of perceptual tasks, AI support improved detection. In the MASAI mammography screening trial, cancer detection rose from 5.0 to 6.4 per 1,000 women, reading workload fell by 44%, and the interval-cancer rate was non-inferior. In colonoscopy, computer-aided detection raised the adenoma detection rate from 40.4% to 54.8%. In the only randomized trial of open-ended diagnostic reasoning, access to GPT-4 did not improve physicians' scores (76% vs. 74%; P=.60 ), although the model alone scored 92%. Evidence of harm came from smaller or non-randomized studies: reader accuracy fell sharply when AI suggestions were incorrect or the AI missed a cancer; physicians trained in AI literacy were still misled by erroneous model advice; unassisted adenoma detection fell from 28.4% to 22.4% after routine AI use in one pre-post study; and a deployed sepsis model discriminated poorly on external validation (area under the curve 0.63). No eligible study from Latin America was identified. Conclusions In the studies reviewed, AI assistance improved clinician performance in bounded detection tasks but not in open-ended diagnostic reasoning, where evidence is limited to one vignette-based trial. The evidence that reliance on AI can impair performance comes from single or design-limited studies and does not establish how large or lasting such effects are. Benefit therefore cannot be inferred from model accuracy alone; assisted and unassisted clinician performance should be measured directly.

title: Enhanced vision language framework for medical report generation using agent-based retrieval.
abstract: Introduction Automated chest X-ray report generation has the potential to reduce the workload of radiologists by combining deep learning and natural language processing. However, existing vision-language models (VLMs), including R2Gen, may generate incorrect or unsupported statements when relevant contextual information is insufficiently captured. This study proposes a modular framework to improve automated report generation through inference-time retrieval and language model-based refinement. Methods Given an input chest X-ray image, R2Gen generates a preliminary report. Relevant contextual information is retrieved using image-derived and textual representations through a FAISS-based similarity retrieval mechanism. The retrieved textual information is combined with the preliminary report and provided to the Zephyr 7B language model to generate the final report. The framework is evaluated on the IU X-Ray and CheXpert Plus datasets using BLEU, ROUGE-L, METEOR, and token-overlap-based precision, recall, and F1-score. The retrieval and refinement stages operate at inference time without requiring additional retraining or fine-tuning of the underlying R2Gen model. Results Experimental results demonstrate improved performance over the R2Gen baseline across the reported evaluation metrics on the evaluated datasets, indicating greater similarity between the generated reports and the reference reports. Discussion The findings suggest that integrating similarity-based retrieval with language model-based refinement can improve the reported text-generation performance of automated chest X-ray reporting systems. The modular framework offers an inference-time approach that avoids additional training of the underlying report generation model.

title: When intact mucosa hides a malignancy: solid-type primary intraosseous carcinoma (PIOC, NOS) of the mandible: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Introduction Primary intraosseous carcinoma, not otherwise specified (PIOC, NOS) is a rare odontogenic carcinoma that arises within the jawbone from odontogenic epithelial remnants, with no initial connection to the oral mucosa. Its non-specific clinical and radiographic features overlap with benign odontogenic and inflammatory lesions, so diagnosis is often delayed and rests on histopathology. The 2017 and 2022 World Health Organization (WHO) classifications recognize PIOC, NOS without formal subtypes; earlier schemes described a solid ( de novo ) type arising without a cystic or tumorous precursor. Case A 53-year-old man with no tobacco or alcohol history presented with painful right mandibular and cheek swelling, purulent discharge through a cutaneous fistula and mobile right mandibular molars, persisting despite management as an odontogenic abscess. The oral mucosa was intact and there was no sensory disturbance. Cone-beam computed tomography showed a destructive radiolucent lesion from the right mandibular first molar to an impacted third molar, with buccolingual expansion, cortical thinning and probable lingual perforation. After extraction of the molars, incisional biopsy showed invasive well-differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma with keratin pearls and bone trabeculae encased by tumor nests, without a cystic or odontogenic tumor component. Staging CT identified no suspicious primary tumor within the imaged regions. The diagnosis was PIOC, NOS under WHO 2022; the tumor was well differentiated (Grade I) and corresponded to the historically described solid ( de novo ) type. Segmental mandibulectomy with right neck dissection revealed a 7-cm tumor with perineural and lymphovascular invasion and four positive level I lymph nodes; margins were clear. Postoperative radiotherapy (40 Gy in 20 fractions) with concurrent cisplatin followed. In August 2026, CT showed an operative-bed mass suspicious for locoregional recurrence, and paclitaxel-carboplatin chemotherapy began in September 2026. Conclusion Solid-type PIOC, NOS can mimic benign odontogenic and inflammatory lesions beneath an intact mucosa. A destructive jaw lesion that fails to respond to treatment for infection should be biopsied without delay. Keratin pearls, infiltrative epithelial nests and bone invasion without mucosal continuity are decisive for diagnosis, and the nodal metastasis and suspected recurrence in this case underline the need for continued oncologic surveillance.

title: Case Report: Intracranial germ cell tumors in girls presenting with peripheral precocious puberty and arginine vasopressin deficiency.
abstract: Objective This report summarizes the clinical characteristics of three female children with clinically diagnosed β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)-secreting intracranial germ cell tumors (iGCTs) who presented with peripheral precocious puberty (PPP) and arginine vasopressin deficiency (AVP-D), with the aim of facilitating earlier diagnosis and treatment. Methods Clinical data of the 3 female patients with iGCTs with initial symptoms of PPP and AVP-D were retrospectively analyzed, and the relevant literature was reviewed. Results All the 3 female children first had polydipsia and polyuria, but their parents paid no attention or sought no medical help until the girls developed thelarche. The children were diagnosed with PPP and AVP-D. Moreover, their β-hCG levels were elevated in the peripheral blood (PB) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and pituitary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed space-occupying lesions in the sellar region. Initial serum β-hCG concentrations in the 3 children were 5010.0, 314.3, and 202.8 mIU/mL, respectively. After regular chemotherapy and radiotherapy, β-hCG levels in the PB and CSF returned to normal, MRI scans revealed tumor reduction, Tanner stages regressed to stage I, and estradiol and testosterone levels decreased. Seven months after the treatment was completed, Patient 1 developed rapidly progressive central precocious puberty. Conclusion In children of either sex presenting with precocious puberty accompanied by multiple pituitary dysfunctions, including AVP-D, or mass effect manifestations, such as decreased visual acuity, routine serum β-hCG and AFP testing and contrast-enhanced sellar MRI are recommended to exclude organic lesions, including iGCTs.

title: Long term (over five-year) outcomes of thermal ablation vs surgical resection for T1N0M0 papillary thyroid carcinoma in danger triangle: a propensity-matched dual-center study.
abstract: Objective To evaluate long-term efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided Thermal Ablation(TA) versus Surgical Resection(SR) for T1N0M0 papillary thyroid carcinoma in the thyroid danger triangle. Materials and methods This dual-center retrospective study included patients treated with TA or SR between September 2016 and April 2020. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Outcomes included overall disease progression (Regional lymph node metastasis, local tumor progression (LTP), residual tumor, distant metastasis), disease-free survival (DFS), complication rates, hospital stay duration, procedure time, blood loss. Results After PSM, 84 patients (age 46.06 ± 10.64; 16 males) in the SR group and 84 patients(age 44.25 ± 12.67; 14 males) in the TA group were observed for a median of 67 months (range, 60-83months) and 68 months (range, 60-105 months), respectively. No significant differences were observed in overall disease progression (6.0% vs 4.8%, P = 0.732), Regional lymph node metastasis (1.2% vs 3.6%, P = 0.306),local tumor progression (LTP) (3.6% vs 1.2%, P = 0.173), or DFS (94% vs 95.2%, P = 0.898). Compared with SR, the TA group had significantly lower complication rates (6.0% vs 16.7%, P = 0.049), shorter hospital stays (median 1 vs 3.3 days, P<0.001), reduced procedure time (23 vs 82 min, P<0.001), less blood loss (1.94 vs 19.76 mL, P<0.001). Conclusion Thermal ablation demonstrated no statistically significant difference in long-term oncologic outcomes compared with surgery for T1N0M0 PTC in the thyroid danger triangle, while offering fewer complications and faster recovery.

title: Long-term endocrine and reproductive outcomes in female adolescent and young adult survivors after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for hematological malignancies during childhood or adolescence.
abstract: Background Cancer treatment during childhood and adolescence, particularly hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), may adversely affect long-term reproductive and endocrine health in female adolescent and young adult (AYA) survivors, leading to premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), which may be associated with impaired pubertal development, low bone mass, and reproductive complications. Methods This study included 34 female survivors treated with HSCT for hematological malignancies during childhood or adolescence (median age 10.8 years). The median follow-up from HSCT to the last gynecological assessment was 8.5 years. Hormonal assessment, pelvic ultrasound, and bone mineral density (BMD) evaluation were performed. Patients were classified as having normal ovarian function, transient ovarian insufficiency (TOI), or persistent POI. Results At the last follow-up, normal ovarian function was observed in 15 patients (44.1%), TOI in 7 (20.6%), and persistent POI in 12 (35.3%). Patients with normal ovarian function were significantly older at HSCT (p = 0.0432), whereas premenarchal status was associated with impaired ovarian outcome (p = 0.0066). In multivariable analysis including cyclophosphamide equivalent dose (CED), radiotherapy, and menarchal status at HSCT, postmenarchal status was associated with markedly lower odds of ovarian insufficiency (adjusted OR 0.056, 95% CI 0.005-0.566; p = 0.0147). All postmenarchal patients received GnRHa, precluding separation of the effects of menarchal status and GnRHa exposure; GnRHa-treated survivors had higher AMH concentrations (p =0.0032). AMH and FSH concentrations differed significantly between groups (both p < 0.01). Uterine and mean ovarian volumes, antral follicle count (AFC), and BMD were significantly lower in patients with TOI and POI (all p < 0.05). Radiotherapy exposure was associated with both lower uterine and ovarian volumes, while puberty induction was also associated with lower uterine volume (all p <0.05). Two patients diagnosed with POI achieved spontaneous pregnancies during follow-up, one resulting in a live birth. Conclusions Ovarian dysfunction is highly prevalent after childhood HSCT, although partial recovery of ovarian function may occur even in patients with a diagnosis of POI. Persistent POI is associated with impaired uterine development and lower BMD despite ongoing hormone replacement therapy, underscoring the need for timely and long-lasting individualized endocrine and reproductive care in AYA survivors.

title: Computed tomography multi-phase radiomics models for differentiating benign and malignant thyroid nodules.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate an integrated model combining multiphase CT radiomics features, clinical data, and conventional morphological CT signs for the preoperative differentiation of benign and malignant thyroid nodules. Methods We retrospectively enrolled patients with surgically confirmed thyroid nodules who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced thyroid CT examination at two centers. Patients from center 1 were randomly allocated to a training cohort and an internal validation cohort at an 8:2 ratio; patients from center 2 served as an external validation cohort. Clinical characteristics and morphological features of nodules were assessed. Radiomics features were extracted from all three CT phases, and four categories of models were constructed: clinical model, single-phase CT radiomics models, multiphase CT radiomics model, and combined clinical-radiomics model. Model performance and interpretability were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results The multiphase CT radiomics model yielded areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) of 0.919, 0.836, and 0.787 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Among the single-phase models, the venous-phase model achieved the best external validation performance (AUC = 0.815). The combined model, integrating clinical and morphological features with multiphase radiomics features, achieved the highest overall diagnostic performance, with an external validation AUC of 0.865 (sensitivity = 74.0%, specificity = 84.5%), significantly outperforming both the clinical model (AUC = 0.800) and the multiphase radiomics model (AUC = 0.787). It also demonstrated favorable calibration and greater clinical net benefit. Conclusion Multiphase CT radiomics enables effective differentiation of benign and malignant thyroid nodules. Integration of clinical and morphological information further improves diagnostic performance, providing an objective, noninvasive tool for preoperative risk stratification of incidentally detected thyroid nodules on CT.

title: Diagnostic performance of next-generation sequencing in thyroid nodules and molecular correlates of tumor aggressiveness in papillary thyroid carcinoma.
abstract: Background Genetic alterations play a crucial role in the pathogenesis and progression of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). However, the diagnostic and prognostic significance of specific genetic alterations in PTC remains to be elucidated. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based genetic testing and to examine associations between genetic alteration subtypes and adverse clinicopathological features in PTC. Methods A total of 279 thyroid specimens with NGS-based genetic testing and pathological diagnoses were enrolled, of which 201 specimens with histopathologically confirmed PTC constituted the primary analytical cohort. Diagnostic performance-sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV)-for predicting malignancy was assessed using postoperative histopathology as the reference standard, with a positive result defined as detection of a pathogenic or likely pathogenic mutation. Alterations were categorized as BRAF -like, RAS -like, or Fusion, and their associations with lymph node metastasis (LNM) and tumor size (cutoffs: 0.5 cm, 1 cm) were evaluated using Pearson's chi-squared test or Fisher's exact test. Results Among the 279 thyroid specimens, 219 had postoperative pathology, of which 203 were malignant, 6 borderline, and 10 benign. BRAF V600E was the most frequent genetic alteration (68.10% overall; 79.10% in PTC). Genetic testing demonstrated high sensitivity (86.21%), specificity (90.00%), and PPV (99.43%), but low NPV (24.32%). The Fusion subtype showed a trend toward association with LNM (OR = 7.23, 95% CI 0.85-61.17, P = 0.048). BRAF -like and RAS -like subtypes showed no significant associations with LNM. For tumor size, BRAF -like alterations were significantly enriched in tumors > 0.5 cm (OR = 2.60, 95% CI 1.24-5.46, P = 0.0098); no significant associations were observed at the 1 cm cutoff. RAS -like and Fusion subtypes showed no significant associations with tumor size. Conclusion Genetic testing demonstrated high PPV (99.43%) but a low NPV (24.32%), indicating that a positive result identifies malignancy while a negative result cannot exclude cancer. Gene fusions showed a trend toward association with LNM in PTC. BRAF -like mutations appeared more often in tumors > 0.5 cm, whereas RAS -like alterations bore no clear link to adverse pathological features. These results suggest that genetic profiling may improve diagnosis and risk assessment of PTC.

title: Case Report: Neurosurgery, octreotide, cabergoline, radiotherapy, pasireotide and pegvisomant - a multimodal strategy for adolescent acrogigantism.
abstract: Growth hormone (GH)-secreting pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are rare in the pediatric population. They often present as large, invasive tumors and are frequently associated with an underlying genetic predisposition, making their management particularly challenging. Optimal treatment requires an individualized multidisciplinary approach, which often involves a combination of surgery and adjuvant medical therapy or radiotherapy when necessary. We present a challenging case of an adolescent female with acrogigantism. The patient was diagnosed at the age of 13 years and 10 months during the evaluation of chronic headaches. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed an invasive PitNET measuring 38 × 23 × 32 mm, while biochemical assessment confirmed marked GH hypersecretion. The disease followed an aggressive course, and biochemical control could not be achieved despite optimal multimodal therapy. Sequential treatment included neurosurgical resection, octreotide LAR, cabergoline, pasireotide LAR, proton beam radiotherapy, and pegvisomant. Combination therapy with pegvisomant and octreotide LAR ultimately normalized insulin-like growth factor 1 concentrations while maintaining long-term radiological tumor stability. This case underscores the complexity of managing aggressive GH-secreting PitNETs in adolescents and emphasizes the need for individualized, multidisciplinary care and long-term follow-up. Combined medical therapy with pegvisomant and octreotide LAR may provide effective biochemical control when surgery, radiotherapy, and standard medical treatment are insufficient.

title: Peritoneal neuroendocrine carcinoma of unknown primary with markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein: a case report.
abstract: Background Peritoneal neuroendocrine carcinoma(NEC) is primarily metastatic, with primary cases being exceedingly rare. The relationship between alpha-fetoprotein(AFP) and neuroendocrine carcinoma remains unclear. In this report, we present a patient with peritoneal neuroendocrine carcinoma who exhibited significantly elevated AFP levels. Extensive evaluation revealed no obvious primary site outside the peritoneum; however, occult gastrointestinal origin could not be entirely excluded. The tumor was thus classified as NEC of unknown primary, with a presumed primary peritoneal origin. The findings from this case suggest that markedly elevated AFP may be associated with aggressive tumor behavior and could serve as a potential marker for monitoring disease activity in peritoneal NECs, a hypothesis that warrants further investigation. Case presentation A 51-year-old man with massive ascites and elevated AFP levels was admitted to the hospital. Liver enhanced magnetic resonance imaging and gastrointestinal endoscopy did not reveal any space-occupying lesions, while abdominal puncture did not detect tumor cells. The patient's whole-body PET-CT revealed extensive peritoneal thickening and increased FDG metabolism. Subsequent laparoscopic exploration revealed numerous nodules and masses of varying sizes with a firm texture in the greater omentum, small intestine surface, mesentery, and parietal peritoneum. Immunohistochemistry of the omentum demonstrated positive results for AE1/AE3, Syn, CgA, and AFP, leading to a final diagnosis of large cell NEC of unknown primary, with a presumed primary peritoneal origin. Due to the presence of multiple peritoneal nodules, radical surgery was not feasible, and EP combined with camrelizumab was initiated. AFP levels showed an overall progressive increase, peaking at 5315 ng/mL on May 25, with a slight subsequent decline to 4948.4 ng/mL on June 20. Unfortunately, the patient discontinued chemotherapy after two cycles due to severe nausea and vomiting; he subsequently succumbed to the disease. Conclusions We propose the hypothesis that dynamic changes in AFP levels could reflect tumor burden and treatment response in a subset of AFP-producing NECs. However, this hypothesis requires validation in larger cohort studies. It is also important to distinguish its potential role as a monitoring biomarker from an established prognostic biomarker.

title: Circulating and extracellular vesicle-associated non-coding RNAs in diabetic retinopathy: a stage-aware framework for network-informed biomarker panels.
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes in which prognosis and management change substantially across non-proliferative and proliferative stages. Current imaging accurately detects established structural and vascular abnormalities but provides limited insight into early molecular changes or the risk of clinically important transitions within non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR). Circulating non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs), have emerged as candidate biomarkers because they regulate pathways involved in endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, oxidative stress, and angiogenesis and can be detected in blood and extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated fractions. In this structured narrative review, we synthesize circulating and EV-associated ncRNA evidence within a stage-aware framework aligned with three clinical use cases: early screening, risk stratification within NPDR, and monitoring at the severe NPDR-early proliferative diabetic retinopathy boundary. miRNAs currently provide the most mature evidence for stage-associated expression patterns and, in selected studies, stage-discriminatory performance. By contrast, circulating lncRNA and circRNA evidence remains limited and is predominantly cross-sectional and advanced-stage associated, supporting their use mainly as complementary, network-informing components. EV association may improve RNA stability and enrich disease-relevant signals, but it does not establish retinal origin, and differences in biofluid source, EV isolation and characterization, normalization, and systemic confounders limit cross-study comparability. Importantly, direct evidence for clinically relevant adjacent-stage discrimination and longitudinal prediction remains scarce. We therefore propose that future biomarker development should prioritize stage-aware, network-informed multi-ncRNA panels, standardized pre-analytical and EV workflows, adjustment for major clinical confounders, and longitudinal imaging-integrated validation to determine whether these biomarkers add value beyond conventional retinal staging.

title: HalluciGuard-eye: knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation for hallucination detection and mitigation in ophthalmic multimodal large language models.
abstract: Background Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of preventable blindness in working-age adults, yet scalable early detection is limited by the unreliability of AI-assisted screening. Multimodal large language models can interpret fundus photographs and support DR grading, but they frequently hallucinate - fabricating lesions or misclassifying referable DR - which directly threatens timely treatment and prevention of vision loss. We developed HalluciGuard-Eye to make AI-assisted DR assessment trustworthy. Methods HalluciGuard-Eye combines knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation with hierarchical hallucination detection. An Ophthalmic Clinical Knowledge Graph containing 47,832 medical entities and 156,294 semantic relationships was constructed from clinical guidelines and published literature. A dual-stream architecture uses a Visual-Semantic Alignment Module to verify cross-modal consistency and a Clinical Factuality Grounding Network to anchor generated content to reranked evidence. The Hierarchical Factuality Score assesses anatomical, pathological, and clinical-recommendation accuracy. The framework was evaluated on four public ophthalmic imaging benchmarks. Results HalluciGuard-Eye reduced hallucination rates by 42.2% compared with state-of-the-art medical multimodal large language models and achieved 91.6% factual accuracy for clinical entity recognition on EyePACS. For diabetic retinopathy grading, sensitivity was 89.6% and specificity was 92.1%, representing improvements of 2.4% and 2.7%, respectively, over MedRAG. In the component ablation, removing knowledge-graph retrieval lowered EyePACS HFS by 9.4 percentage points. Additional analyses yielded 87.6% critical-evidence recall@20, 89.2% lesion-location accuracy, and 88.9% sensitivity in a patient-clustered cohort. Conclusions These results indicate that knowledge-grounded retrieval and hierarchical factuality assessment can reduce hallucinations while preserving diagnostic performance in ophthalmic multimodal language models.

title: Risk prediction models for macrovascular complications in type 2 diabetes mellitus: from traditional risk scores to multimodal intelligent prediction.
abstract: Macrovascular complications are the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Early risk identification and accurate risk stratification are essential for both primary and secondary cardiovascular prevention. With the rapid development of electronic health records, medical imaging, multi-omics technologies, and artificial intelligence (AI), risk prediction models for diabetic macrovascular complications have evolved from traditional statistical approaches to machine learning-, deep learning-, and multimodal AI-driven models. However, despite substantial improvements in predictive performance, current models remain limited by heterogeneous target populations, inconsistent outcome definitions, insufficient external validation, limited clinical interpretability, and inadequate real-world implementation, thereby restricting their clinical translation. This review summarizes the evolution, data sources, modeling methodologies, clinical applications, and future perspectives of risk prediction models for macrovascular complications in T2DM. We first describe the transition from conventional cardiovascular risk scores, including the Framingham Risk Score, to diabetes-specific models such as the UKPDS Risk Engine, ADVANCE, RECODe, and SCORE2-Diabetes, followed by the emergence of AI-based prediction models. We then review the major data sources used in contemporary prediction models, including clinical characteristics, laboratory biomarkers, vascular function and imaging, multi-omics profiles, and wearable device-derived data. Furthermore, we compare the strengths and limitations of traditional statistical methods, machine learning, deep learning, and multitask learning with respect to predictive performance, interpretability, and clinical applicability, and discuss the major challenges related to study design, external validation, data quality, algorithmic bias, and real-world implementation. Finally, we propose that future risk prediction models for diabetic macrovascular complications will evolve from single-source data to multimodal data integration, from static risk estimation to dynamic risk trajectories, from single outcomes to multiple interconnected cardiovascular outcomes, from prognosis prediction to individualized treatment benefit prediction, and from standalone algorithms to continuously learning clinical decision support systems. Emerging technologies, including foundation models, large language models, digital twins, causal inference, and continuous learning frameworks, are expected to drive the transition from Risk Prediction to Clinical Decision and ultimately Patient Benefit, thereby advancing precision prevention and individualized management of diabetes.

title: Mucormycosis beyond the classic host: a case series and narrative literature review from a tertiary Greek hospital.
abstract: Mucormycosis is an aggressive, angioinvasive mold infection that progresses rapidly and carries high mortality. Disease in non-classical hosts is readily mistaken for bacterial superinfection or the expected course of the underlying condition and the resulting delay in tissue biopsy and antifungal therapy may adversely affect outcome. We report a retrospective case series at a tertiary referral center in northern Greece over a seven-year period. Nine patients (median age: 49 years, of whom 7 were male and 2 were female) with histopathologically confirmed mucormycosis were reviewed. Two previously healthy adolescents developed post-traumatic cutaneous disease and survived. Three patients reached craniofacial disease through the classic immunosuppressed route, one through poorly controlled type 1 diabetes, one through poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, and one through allogeneic transplantation for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). The remaining four developed infection on a background of barrier disruption or critical illness: two with major thermal burns (39% and 54% total body surface area), one with a cannulation-site eschar during high-dose corticosteroid therapy for dermatomyositis, and one intubated patient with prediabetes who developed forearm necrosis with local thrombosis. Rhizopus arrhizus predominated in the craniofacial and healthcare-associated cases, whereas the trauma and burn cases yielded a wider range of species. Liposomal amphotericin B (L-AmB) was the first-line agent in eight patients and one case with limited disease received isavuconazole monotherapy. Eight patients underwent surgery, ranging from debridement to orbital exenteration, maxillectomy, and in one case forequarter amputation. Eight of nine patients (89%) required admission to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU); among them, the median ICU stay was 37 days (IQR 7-57; range 2-123). Overall mortality was 67% (6/9). This series includes established metabolic and transplant-associated mucormycosis as well as trauma, burn, and healthcare-associated presentations. Only two patients had no documented systemic predisposition other than traumatic tissue disruption. While this small, heterogeneous patient sample cannot determine incidence, prognostic factors, or treatment effects, it may illustrate that this disease has the potential to affect patients beyond the classic host. Rapidly progressive necrosis or thrombosis should nevertheless prompt consideration of mucormycosis and tissue sampling for histopathology and culture.

title: Clinical and genetic features, surgical management, and longitudinal follow-up in two children with progressive osseous heteroplasia.
abstract: Background Progressive osseous heteroplasia (POH) is an ultrarare disorder characterized by heterotopic ossification that progresses from the skin and subcutaneous tissues into deeper connective tissues. Most affected individuals harbor heterozygous inactivating variants in GNAS , whereas postzygotic mosaic variants have rarely been described. Evidence to guide surgical management remains limited. Methods We retrospectively characterized two children with clinically diagnosed POH who underwent genetic testing and surgical treatment. Whole-exome sequencing was performed on peripheral blood and, when available, resected tissue, followed by PCR-Sanger sequencing and T-vector cloning. Case 1 underwent clinical and radiographic follow-up for 5 years; follow-up for Case 2 was limited to family-provided radiographs obtained at 2 years. Results Case 1 harbored a possible postzygotic mosaic GNAS variant, NM_000516.7:c.-1_2del, with variant allele frequencies of 14.7% in peripheral blood and 40.56% in bone lesion tissue. The predominantly localized wrist lesion was macroscopically excised. A small radiographic recurrence appeared by the second postoperative year but progressed slowly thereafter; active wrist flexion was 5-10 ° at 5 years. Case 2 harbored NM_000516.7:c.565_568del (p. (Asp189MetfsTer14)), detected as a heterozygous variant in peripheral blood. The lesion diffusely involved neurovascular structures, tendon sheaths, the joint capsule, and adjacent bones, precluding complete excision. Family-provided radiographs at 2 years showed an extent of ossification broadly similar to that before surgery; no in-person clinical assessment was available. Conclusion These cases provide additional clinical, molecular, and longitudinal information on POH and illustrate the importance of lesion distribution and resectability when interpreting surgical outcomes. The available postoperative findings cannot establish a causal relationship between variant status and prognosis because the patients differed in baseline disease extent, completeness of excision, follow-up duration, and outcome ascertainment. A possible association between mosaic burden and lesion distribution remains a hypothesis that requires evaluation in larger cohorts.

title: Chemotherapy-refractory high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma: single-cell findings, TCGA-OV transcriptomic context, and a single-case MRI-transcriptome illustration.
abstract: Background Primary chemotherapy refractoriness remains a clinical challenge in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSC) and may reflect pre-existing tumor-cell states and microenvironmental heterogeneity. We examined public single-cell and bulk transcriptomic resources, a barcode-matched MRI case, and an in vitro cisplatin-perturbation RT-qPCR experiment. Methods We reanalyzed GSE300897, comprising 19,156 annotated cells from nine treatment-naïve HGSC biopsy libraries (four chemotherapy-refractory and five chemotherapy-sensitive), with response summaries retained at the library/patient level. The Cancer Genome Atlas Ovarian Cancer (TCGA-OV) provided 421 unique primary tumors for cohort-scale transcriptomic and overall survival context. One TCGA-OV case (TCGA-24-1423) linked a multiparametric MRI examination to a tumor RNA-seq barcode. OVCAR-3 and Caov-3 cells were exposed to cisplatin (5 μM, 24 h), and IFIT1, MX1, SNAI1, and HIF1A expression was measured by RT-qPCR. Results Across the nine GSE300897 libraries, no cancer-cell program passed Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) q < 0.05. Refractory libraries showed a lower type-I interferon (IFN-I) score (-0.15 log1p(CP10k)) and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) balance (-0.16), with a small increase in hypoxia (+0.05). In TCGA-OV, none of the six displayed program scores reached BH q < 0.05 in age- and stage-adjusted Cox models; IFN-I tertiles separated nominally by Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank p = 0.029), whereas continuous IFN-I was not significant after adjustment (HR = 0.96 per SD, BH q = 0.927). In TCGA-24-1423, the paired transcriptome showed an IFN-I score at the 86.8th TCGA-OV percentile, with IFIT1 and MX1 at the 87.5th and 93.7th percentiles. RT-qPCR showed lower IFIT1/MX1 and higher SNAI1/HIF1A after acute cisplatin exposure in both cell lines (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.05). Conclusion These findings support a conservative, hypothesis-generating interpretation of chemotherapy response-associated transcriptional heterogeneity in HGSC. Reduced IFN-I and altered cell-state programs were directional features of the small refractory single-cell cohort, whereas TCGA-OV provided context rather than independent response validation. The MRI-linked case demonstrates imaging-transcriptome pairing but does not establish an imaging biomarker. The RT-qPCR experiment demonstrates cisplatin-responsive changes in selected genes but models acute drug perturbation rather than the pretreatment clinical refractory state.

title: Pathology-guided multimodal transformer predicts postoperative survival benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy in glioma: from DNA damage repair to immune characterization.
abstract: Introduction High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are aggressive primary brain tumors with high recurrence rates and poor prognosis. Survival benefit from adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) varies substantially across patients, and reliable preoperative biomarkers for treatment stratification remain limited. This study aims to develop an interpretable multimodal deep learning model integrating whole-slide histopathological images and multiparametric MRI to preoperatively predict survival benefit from adjuvant TMZ in HGG patients. Methods A Transformer-based multimodal fusion model was proposed. Key tumor regions were identified from whole-slide pathology images via weakly supervised clustering, and pathological features were extracted using attention-based multiple instance learning. Concurrently, 2.5D tumor subregional features were derived from multiparametric MRI sequences. These multimodal features were deeply fused using a Transformer encoder. The model was developed and validated on a multicenter cohort (504 patients), and its biological basis was explored through transcriptomic analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction networks, and immune deconvolution. Results The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.910, 0.861, and 0.833 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Transcriptomic analysis implicated DNA damage repair processes in high-benefit patients, suggesting that enhanced DNA repair capacity may contribute to TMZ sensitivity. Immune deconvolution showed higher M1 macrophage infiltration and lower regulatory T cell abundance in the high-benefit group, consistent with a less immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Importantly, low-benefit patients who completed TMZ chemotherapy had shorter survival than those treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy alone or surgery alone. Conclusion This model identifies patients unlikely to benefit from standard TMZ chemotherapy, providing a tool for postoperative personalized treatment stratification and optimization of therapeutic strategies in HGGs.

title: Multi-omics of tertiary lymphoid structures in breast cancer: clinical significance and biomarker potential.
abstract: Background Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are organized immune aggregates that can support local adaptive immune responses within the tumor microenvironment. In breast cancer, particularly triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), the presence and maturation of TLSs have been associated with prognosis and treatment response; however, heterogeneity in TLS definition, maturation criteria, spatial sampling, and analytical platforms currently limits standardization and routine clinical implementation. Main body Conventional histopathology provides structural information but limited molecular resolution, whereas single-cell RNA sequencing loses the spatial context that is central to TLS organization. High-resolution spatial and multi-omics technologies can partly bridge these gaps by characterizing TLS cellular composition, molecular interactions, and tissue architecture in situ . This review summarizes the biological features, histopathological classification, multi-omics characterization, clinical associations, and emerging therapeutic strategies related to TLSs in breast cancer, with particular attention to methodological limitations and translational barriers. Conclusion More precise characterization of TLSs may inform future biomarker development and therapeutic strategies in breast cancer. Prospective validation, standardized assessment, and demonstration of incremental clinical utility are required before TLS-based approaches can be incorporated into routine clinical decision-making.

title: Clinical variables and quantitative CT radiomics for mortality risk stratification after acute exacerbation of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease.
abstract: Background Acute exacerbation (AE) is the most lethal event of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD). This exploratory study compared clinical, radiomics, and combined predictor strategies across five survival-learning algorithms for survival risk stratification. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 78 patients with AE-IIM-ILD and divided them into a training cohort (n = 54; 20 deaths) and a held-out internal testing cohort (n = 24; 9 deaths), stratified by observed mortality event status. Three predictor strategies were evaluated: a clinical strategy comprising PaO 2 /FiO 2 ratio, neutrophil percentage (NEU%), and arthritis-related symptoms; a radiomics strategy comprising two selected radiomics features; and a combined strategy comprising PaO 2 /FiO 2 ratio, arthritis-related symptoms, and a composite radiomics score (Rad-score). Each strategy was evaluated using five survival-learning algorithms. Harrell's concordance index (C-index) was the primary discrimination metric, with mean time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) used as a secondary measure. Results During the 1-year follow-up, 29 deaths were observed. Performance rankings varied across predictor strategies, algorithms, and evaluation metrics. The combined-Random Survival Forest configuration demonstrated the highest training-cohort C-index among the 15 configurations. Its mean time-dependent AUC was 0.923 (95% CI: 0.860-0.970) in the training cohort and 0.915 (95% CI: 0.736-0.986) in the testing cohort, with corresponding C-indices of 0.874 (95% CI: 0.803-0.940) and 0.842 (95% CI: 0.673-0.971), respectively. The model stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with distinct observed survival trajectories. Conclusion In this exploratory cohort, integrating selected clinical variables with a quantitative CT Rad-score using RSF showed promising numerical discrimination and risk-stratification performance. These findings suggest that clinical and quantitative imaging information may provide complementary prognostic information after AE-IIM-ILD.

title: Case Report: Cholangioscopic and histopathological findings before and after treatment in immune-related cholangitis.
abstract: Immune-related cholangitis is a rare immune-related adverse event, and its diagnostic criteria and treatment strategies have not yet been established. Here, we report a case of immune-related cholangitis in which treatment response could be objectively visualized through reassessment of cholangioscopic and histopathological findings before and after treatment. A 79-year-old man with recurrent cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the scalp developed high fever and general fatigue after six courses of nivolumab, and laboratory tests revealed marked elevation of hepatobiliary enzymes. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography and endoscopic ultrasonography showed bile duct wall thickening, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography demonstrated shaggy irregularity in the distal bile duct, and peroral cholangioscopy revealed diffuse surface irregularity and granular changes of the biliary mucosa. Furthermore, cholangioscopy-guided bile duct biopsy demonstrated marked lymphocytic infiltration, particularly infiltration of CD8-positive T cells, leading to a diagnosis of immune-related cholangitis. Prednisolone and ursodeoxycholic acid were initiated, with nivolumab discontinued, after which the clinical symptoms and hepatobiliary enzyme levels gradually improved. Furthermore, on Day 28 after treatment initiation, reassessment by cholangioscopy and bile duct biopsy confirmed improvement in the cholangioscopic findings and reduction of lymphocytic infiltration, particularly CD8-positive T-cell infiltration, on bile duct biopsy. These objective findings supported tapering of steroid therapy. To our knowledge, very few cases have described reassessment of cholangioscopic and histopathological findings before and after treatment in immune-related cholangitis. We suggest that such evaluation may contribute to confirming treatment response and guiding therapeutic strategy in immune-related cholangitis.

title: Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis with psychiatric manifestations and choreiform movements: a case report and literature review.
abstract: To summarize the clinical manifestations, ancillary examination findings, treatment course, and prognosis of a patient with neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis presenting with prominent psychiatric disturbances and choreiform movements, and to review the literature on the clinical spectrum of this disease. A 52-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and biopsy-proven podocytopathy with a "full-house" immunofluorescence pattern showing diffuse positivity for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q, diagnosed in February 2026; however, a definitive diagnosis of lupus podocytopathy remained uncertain, as the patient lacked systemic lupus erythematosus manifestations. She was admitted on April 3, 2026, with a 5-day history of psychiatric disturbances and involuntary choreiform movements in all four limbs, preceded by significant psychological stress (bereavement). Neurological examination revealed slowed responses and impaired calculation. Cranial MRI showed only bilateral periventricular small ischemic foci (Fazekas grade 1) with normal SWI. Initial EEG demonstrated sharp waves and spike-and-wave complexes in the left parietal, occipital, and temporal regions. CSF analysis revealed leukocytosis (21/μl, 90% mononuclear cells), protein of 0.4 g/L, elevated IgG index of 0.76, and elevated 24-hour intrathecal IgG synthesis rate of 5.63 mg/dl. CSF mNGS detected 453 EBV sequences (RPM) with a relative abundance of 97.48%. Serum EBV VCA-IgG and EBNA-IgG were elevated with negative IgM. Autoantibody testing followed a stepwise approach: initial screening for conventional autoimmune encephalitis, paraneoplastic, and demyelinating antibodies was negative; subsequent tissue-based assay (TBA) of CSF revealed strong positive immunoreactivity, prompting expanded antibody panel testing, which ultimately detected anti-neurexin-3α antibodies in serum (titer 1:30) and CSF (titer 1:100), confirmed by both cell-based assay (CBA) and TBA. The patient's condition progressively deteriorated, requiring endotracheal intubation on April 21 and tracheostomy on April 30. She received methylprednisolone pulse therapy at 500 mg/day for 5 days followed by a stepwise taper, intravenous immunoglobulin at 0.4 g/kg for 5 days, and five sessions of plasma exchange from April 30 to May 8 due to poor initial response. Choreiform movements gradually resolved after plasma exchange. She was weaned from mechanical ventilation on May 19 and decannulated on May 27. During the ICU course, she developed pulmonary infection with carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, which was controlled after antibiotic adjustment. Repeat EEG normalized on June 1. She was discharged from rehabilitation on June 9 on oral methylprednisolone 32 mg/day. On June 26, 2026, follow-up serum TBA showed weakly positive immunoreactivity, with the serum antibody titer remaining at 1:30. She subsequently received four infusions of efgartigimod at 400 mg each for consolidation immunotherapy and was transitioned to ofatumumab for long-term maintenance. At follow-up on August 6, 2026, the patient had no residual psychiatric symptoms or choreiform movements, with muscle strength recovered to 4+ in all limbs, full independence in daily activities, ambulation without assistance, and only mild gait instability. Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis is a rare but treatable condition. Choreiform movements expand its clinical spectrum. The coexistence of podocytopathy raises a hypothesis of shared antigenicity between renal and neuronal neurexin family members, though this remains purely speculative. CSF EBV reactivation may represent a bystander phenomenon or epiphenomenon of severe immune dysregulation rather than a confirmed trigger. Tissue-based assay provides crucial diagnostic direction when conventional screening is negative. Early recognition, comprehensive immunotherapy, and meticulous ICU management are important determinants of favorable outcomes. Given the inherent limitations of a single case report, these findings warrant confirmation through larger cohort studies.
