title: Cascaded deep learning for synthesis of 18 F-FDG PET from 18 F-octreotide: model parameter optimization and performance evaluation.
abstract: Objective To investigate a cascaded conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN)-based method for synthesizing 18 F-FDG PET images from 18 F-octreotide, optimize model parameter configurations, and evaluate the quality of the synthesized images. Methods Imaging data from 71 tumor patients who underwent dual-tracer PET/CT examinations with 18 F-FDG and 18 F-octreotide between May 2022 and November 2025 were retrospectively collected. A cascaded deep learning architecture (first stage: 3D U-Net; second stage: self-attention 3D V-Net) was employed to evaluate the effects of image preprocessing, resampling size, and patch size on synthesis quality. Three preprocessing strategies (log transformation, normalization, and a combined approach) were compared. Image quality was assessed using five objective metrics (SSIM, PSNR, MSE, MAE, and NMI) and Likert 5-point ratings from three nuclear medicine physicians; liver and lesion-level SUV agreement were further evaluated. Results In the held-out test cohort ( n = 14), the combined preprocessing method (log transformation + normalization) significantly outperformed the individual methods (SSIM: 0.8454 ± 0.0328 vs. 0.7831 ± 0.0337 vs. 0.7438 ± 0.0362, P < 0.001). On the identical held-out test cohort ( n = 14), the Group 2 parameter configuration (resampling size: 256 × 256 × 512; patch size: 128 × 128 × 128) outperformed Group 1, with an SSIM of 0.8854 ± 0.0455 and a PSNR of 28.15 ± 3.35 dB, representing relative improvements of 19.1% and 83.5%, respectively, over Group 1 (paired-samples t-test, both P < 0.001). The mean Likert score was 4.53 ± 0.19. Quantitative analysis of liver SUVmean showed no significant difference between synthesized and real images ( P = 0.967, paired t-test). Lesion-level quantitative analysis demonstrated high agreement between synthetic and real 18 F-FDG images, with Pearson correlation coefficients of 1.0000, 0.9995, and 0.9991 for SUVmax and SUVmean ( n = 14) and SUVpeak ( n = 13), respectively (all P < 0.001), no significant differences on paired t-tests (all P > 0.05), and all Bland-Altman differences within the 95% limits of agreement. Conclusion The cascaded deep learning model enabled cross-tracer synthesis from 18 F-octreotide to 18 F-FDG PET images. In this exploratory, single-center pilot cohort, the optimized configuration demonstrated promising quantitative and visual performance, supporting image-synthesis feasibility and potential clinical utility of a single-injection, dual-parameter molecular imaging approach for neuroendocrine tumors. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted before any clinical application.

title: FAP-targeted [<sup>68</sup>Ga]BED003-PET compared with [<sup>18</sup>F]DOPA-PET in patients with recurrent medullary thyroid carcinoma.
abstract: Aim Molecular imaging of recurrent or advanced medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) remains clinically challenging. [ 18 F]DOPA-PET is an established reference standard, but its sensitivity is limited and dependent on tumour burden and biomarker levels. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted PET has emerged as a promising imaging approach across several malignancies. This study aimed to compare the detection rate and quantitative imaging characteristics of [ 68 Ga]BED003-PET, recently known as [ 68 Ga]OncoFAP-DOTAGA, with [ 18 F]DOPA-PET in patients with recurrent or advanced MTC. Methods Eight patients with histologically proven MTC and suspected recurrence or progression based on elevated calcitonin levels underwent both [ 18 F]DOPA-PET and an additional [ 68 Ga]BED003-PET. All patients presented with inconclusive findings in [ 18 F]DOPA-PET. Comparative analyses were performed on a patient- and lesion-based level. Quantitative parameters included maximum and mean standardized uptake values (SUV max /SUV mean ), metabolic tumour volume (MTV), and maximum tumour-to-background ratios (TBR max ). Potential theranostic suitability was explored based on lesional FAP uptake. Results The median interval between PET acquisitions was 33 days (range, 7-56 days). In total, 35 tracer-avid lesions were detected. [ 68 Ga]BED003-PET detected significantly more lesions than [ 18 F]DOPA-PET (34/35 [97%] vs. 16/35 [46%], P < 0.001). 15 lesions (43%) were positive on both modalities, 19 (54%) were only [ 68 Ga]BED003-positive, and 1 (2.9%) was only [ 18 F]DOPA-positive. Quantitative analysis demonstrated significantly higher uptake and contrast for [ 68 Ga]BED003, including higher blood-pool TBRmax than [ 18 F]DOPA (6.02 vs. 2.23, Bonferroni adjusted P < 0.001). Conclusion In this small MTC cohort, [ 68 Ga]BED003-PET demonstrated higher lesion detection and TBRs in patients with inconsistent findings in [ 18 F]DOPA-PET. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

title: From task-specific AI to multimodal foundation models in PET/CT: a readiness framework for clinical translation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence in PET/CT is evolving from narrowly optimized systems toward reusable pretrained representations and multimodal models. PET/CT is a demanding test case because clinically meaningful interpretation must preserve quantitative molecular information while integrating anatomic CT, acquisition metadata, longitudinal examinations, and free-text imaging reports. This focused narrative review synthesizes literature reported from January 2021 through July 2026, spanning PET reconstruction and enhancement, attenuation correction, segmentation, outcome modeling, pretrained representations, vision-language systems, and agentic workflows. We distinguish task-specific models, reusable pretrained representations, promptable models, vision-language systems, generalist foundation-model candidates, and agentic systems according to demonstrated capabilities, while separately considering evaluation benchmarks. Task-specific deep learning has demonstrated promising technical performance in low-count imaging and whole-body tumor analysis, but most evidence remains retrospective and restricted by radiotracer, disease, scanner, institution, or endpoint. Emerging PET-native studies demonstrate label-efficient segmentation, image-text grounding, report generation, and modular tool orchestration; however, they do not yet establish broad cross-tracer generalization or prospective clinical benefit. We therefore propose MOSAIC-PET, an author-developed heuristic six-domain evaluation framework for PET/CT foundation models encompassing Molecular fidelity, Organ and anatomic grounding, Semantic faithfulness, Adaptability, Integration and clinical impact, and Continuous governance. MOSAIC-PET has not undergone Delphi consensus or formal validation and is intended to organize PET-specific evidence requirements rather than function as a validated clinical-readiness tool. The near-term translational priority is the development of modular, auditable systems in which validated quantitative tools and evidence-linked language outputs remain under specialist oversight, with progression from external testing to silent evaluation, assisted-use studies, clinical-impact assessment, and continuous lifecycle monitoring.

title: Predictive value of multimodal models combining CT body composition and clinical variables for short-term postoperative complications in colorectal cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Malnutrition and sarcopenic obesity are prevalent in colorectal cancer (CRC) and linked to adverse surgical outcomes. Conventional screening often overlooks this occult malnutrition. Preoperative computed tomography (CT)-based body composition analysis (BCA) provides objective biomarkers for muscle depletion and fat distribution. This systematic review evaluates multimodal machine learning (ML) models integrating BCA and clinical variables to predict CRC postoperative complications and inform precision nutrition strategies. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library (inception to April 13, 2026) for ML models predicting postoperative complications in CRC using BCA. Quality was assessed using PROBAST. Pooled area under the curve (AUC) was estimated via a random-effects model, alongside subgroup analyses. Results Eight studies ( n = 7,835) were included. The pooled AUC was 0.84 (95% CI: 0.76-0.89), indicating good discriminative performance, although substantial heterogeneity was present ( I 2 = 79.7%). Nomogram-based models showed a pooled AUC of 0.87 (95% CI: 0.78-0.92). For anastomotic leakage, the pooled AUC was 0.83 (95% CI: 0.35-0.98), although this estimate was imprecise because only two studies contributed to this subgroup. Conclusion Multimodal ML models integrating BCA biomarkers offer a robust, data-driven framework for preoperative risk stratification in CRC. Identifying high-risk body composition phenotypes may facilitate tailored prehabilitation and targeted immunonutrition strategies. Future efforts must prioritize standardized BCA and multi-center external validation. Systematic review registration CRD420261364363.

title: Novel AI-derived muscle ultrasound biomarkers linking nutritional status and prognosis in cancer patients.
abstract: Introduction Malnutrition and sarcopenia worsen prognosis in patients with cancer and require accessible diagnostic methods for assessing muscle quantity and quality. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted muscle ultrasound may improve the standardization and efficiency of body-composition assessment. This study evaluated the prognostic relevance of AI-assisted rectus femoris ultrasound biomarkers within a comprehensive nutritional assessment of patients with cancer. Methods This prospective longitudinal observational cohort study included 389 patients with cancer, most of whom had tumors of digestive origin. Participants underwent longitudinal and transverse rectus femoris ultrasonography. Images were analyzed using PIIXMED™ MSK, which applies U-Net based anatomical segmentation followed by deterministic image-processing procedures. The evaluated variables included subcutaneous adipose tissue thickness (SAT), rectus femoris thickness (RFT) rectus femoris cross-sectional area (RFA), pennation angle, mean echo intensity, and the percentages of low- and medium-echogenicity pixels within the segmented region of interest, reported as the Muscle Index (Mi) and Fat Index (FATi), respectively. The muscle-area index was calculated as AreaMi = RFAxMi. Results The 389 participants had a mean age of 70.6 (10.8) years, 58.9% were men, and 53.7% ( n = 206) were classified as geriatric oncology patients (≥70 years). Malnutrition was present in 75.3% of participants, confirmed sarcopenia in 18.8% and overall mortality during follow-up was 26.5%. In univariate log-rank survival analysis, reduced muscle-area index (MiArea<1.36 cm 2 ; p = 0.014) and low muscle quality (Mi < 46%; p = 0.019) were the strongest univariate predictors of significantly shorter survival. In multivariate Cox proportional Hazards regression models adjusted for age, sex, digestive tumor location, and metastatic disease, larger rectus femoris area (RFA: HR = 0.77. 95%CI: 0.62-0.95; p < 0.05) and thickness (RFT: HR = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.19-0.99; p < 0.05) remained independent protective factors against mortality. Conversely, reduced muscle index (Mi < 47%: HR = 1.60, 95%CI: 1.05-2.06; p < 0.05) and the presence of myosteatosis (HR = 2.35, 95%CI: 1.19-4.62; p = 0.01) independently predicted an increased risk of mortality. Conclusion In cancer patients, AI-assisted rectus femoris ultrasound variables effectively predict mortality. Greater muscle area and higher muscle index (Mi > 47%) indicate a favorable prognosis. Early ultrasound assessment detects structural alterations before overt deterioration, providing a crucial window for targeted nutritional interventions to preserve muscle integrity and prevent complications.

title: Genetic risk stratification reveals distinct first-order radiomic phenotypes in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits significant morphological heterogeneity that has traditionally been attributed to etiological, environmental, and biological factors. Recent evidence suggests, however, that genetic background may influence tumor characteristics and behavior in HCC. Purpose To investigate associations between established HCC genetic risk factors and first-order radiomic features. Methods We evaluated a retrospective cohort of 210 patients with HCC who underwent contrast-enhanced MRI and genetic profiling for three established HCC risk variants (PNPLA3 rs738409-G, TM6SF2 rs58542926-T, and MAU2 rs58489806-T). We screened first-order radiomic features in the full cohort and then focused the primary analysis on 77 treatment-naive patients whose tumor morphology had not been modified by therapy. Patients were stratified into at-risk (≥1 risk allele, n=52) and wild-type (no risk alleles, n=25) groups. Eighteen first-order radiomic features were screened using the Mann-Whitney U test and AUC analysis. The leading feature, kurtosis, was then subjected to univariate and multivariate analysis for clinical and imaging features to identify any confounding effect. In addition, a 10-fold cross-validated cutpoint stability, sensitivity analysis, and Cox/Kaplan-Meier survival analysis were also conducted. Results Among 18 features, kurtosis best distinguished at-risk from wild-type genotypes in treatment-naive patients (AUC = 0.67, p=0.014), with wild-type tumors showing more uniform, sharply peaked intensity patterns. Tumor volume correlated modestly with kurtosis (Spearman's ρ=0.45, p<0.0001), but volume alone did not discriminate genotype (Mann-Whitney U, p=0.3994). The genotype-kurtosis association remained significant after adjusting for volume and shape (ANCOVA, p=0.029) and strengthened after adjusting for nine clinical/demographic covariates (p=0.003), indicating kurtosis reflects biological information beyond tumor size. The empirical cutpoint was stable across 10-fold cross-validation (mean=3.35, SD = 0.05), and results were unchanged in sensitivity analysis. Kurtosis was not associated with overall survival (Cox HR = 1.19, p=0.13). No genotype-related discrimination was observed in the pooled full cohort, consistent with treatment-related alteration of tumor texture. Conclusions In a cohort of 210 genetically profiled patients with HCC, genotype-related radiomic features were not apparent when treated and untreated tumors were analyzed together. However, restricting the analysis to the treatment-naive subgroup (n=77) revealed tumor kurtosis as a reproducible, biologically plausible first-order imaging correlate of established HCC genetic risk status.

title: Intratumoral habitat combined with peritumoral radiomics to improve the predictive performance of initial TACE efficacy: a multicenter retrospective study.
abstract: Background and purpose Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) is the primary treatment for intermediate-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, significant heterogeneity in patient response to TACE necessitates non-invasive and precise methods for evaluating treatment efficacy. This study aims to explore the predictive ability of combined intratumoral habitat imaging and peritumoral radiomics features for TACE response. Materials and methods We retrospectively enrolled HCC patients who underwent TACE treatment at four centers between January 2015 and December 2023. All patients underwent contrast-enhanced MRI. Patients from centers A and B formed the training cohort, while those from centers C and D comprised external validation cohorts. Using three-phase enhanced MRI (arterial, portal venous, and delayed phase), K-Means clustering divided intratumoral regions into three habitat subregions (Habitat 1, 2, and 3), and peritumoral features were extracted. Clinical variables were also collected. Key radiomics features were selected by LASSO regression, and clinical indicators were identified through univariable and multivariable logistic regression. The XGBoost algorithm constructed intratumoral, peritumoral, clinical, and combined models. Performance was evaluated using ROC curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and DeLong tests. Results A total of 174 HCC patients who underwent initial TACE treatment were enrolled, including 104 in training and 70 in validation cohorts. Fifteen key intratumoral features from the habitat subregions and 24 radiomics features from the peritumoral region were identified, primarily derived from wavelet transforms and texture analysis. The wavelet-LLL_glszm_ZoneVariance_ PVP feature from Cluster 2 contributed significantly to the model and had a positive impact (highest SHAP value). Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (P = 0.015) and Tumor size (P = 0.016) remained significantly associated with TACE treatment response in multivariable analysis. The combined model based on clinical, intratumoral habitat and peritumoral radiomics showed superior predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.950 (95% CI: 0.89-1.00), 0.850 (0.79-0.91) and 0.830 (0.77-0.89) in training and validation cohorts, outperforming single models (Clinic: AUC = 0.700, Tumor_Habitat: AUC = 0.880, Peritumor_Radiomics: AUC = 0.870, P<0.05). Calibration and DCA demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes and favorable net benefit across the evaluated threshold probabilities. Conclusion The combined model integrating AFP, Tumor size, intratumoral habitat imaging, and peritumoral radiomics could accurately predict initial TACE response in HCC patients. Cluster 2-derived features showed relatively greater contributions among the intratumoral habitat subregions. This non-invasive prediction tool may provide complementary information for pretreatment risk stratification. Future prospective multicenter studies are needed to verify the clinical applicability of the model.

title: The clinical value of ultrasound radiomics combined with clinical data nomogram in predicting cervical lymph node metastasis of papillary thyroid carcinoma.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the predictive value of a nomogram incorporating ultrasound and clinical features for cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with thyroid cancer. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients pathologically diagnosed with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) between April 2024 and January 2025. Radiomics features were extracted from two-dimensional thyroid ultrasound images, and feature selection was performed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO). Five classifiers were compared, and logistic regression was selected to construct the radiomics model. A clinical-radiomics model integrating the radiomics score and clinical predictors, together with a standalone clinical model, was developed using multivariable logistic regression. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated in a held-out internal validation set. Results Sex, Radscore, age, and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) levels were identified as independent predictors of CLNM in patients with PTC. Based on these variables, radiomics, clinical, and clinical radiomics models were constructed; the models achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.735, 0.792, and 0.867, respectively, in the validation set. DeLong's test and decision curve analysis (DCA) demonstrated that the clinical radiomics model outperformed the radiomics model in the validation set, offering a higher net clinical benefit. Conclusion A nomogram integrating ultrasound imaging and clinical data effectively predicts the risk of CLNM in patients with PTC and may assist clinicians in developing individualized treatment strategies.

title: Deep learning with interactive segmentation for risk stratification of cystic renal lesions on tri-phase CT: a multicenter study.
abstract: Background Accurate preoperative risk stratification of cystic renal lesions (CRLs) remains a clinical challenge, primarily due to morphological overlap which often leads to the overtreatment of indolent cysts. To address this, we developed and validated an integrated deep learning framework that combines interactive segmentation with tri-phase CT feature integration to refine malignancy prediction. Methods This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 434 patients with CRLs from four institutions, partitioned into training (n=195), validation (n=100), and external test (n=139) cohorts. The reference standard was histopathological diagnosis or ≥4 years of radiological stability. For volumetric segmentation, we implemented an interactive 'human-in-the-loop' Swin UNETR model. To integrate complementary information across the three CT phases, we then deployed a Tri-Phase-Channel (TPC) Perceiver architecture to integrate features extracted by parallel SEResNet50 backbones from unenhanced, corticomedullary, and nephrographic CT phases. Diagnostic performance was evaluated against the single-phase SEResNet50 models and the Bosniak classification version 2019 using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA). Results In the external test cohort, the interactive segmentation model yielded a Dice score of 0.890. For malignancy prediction, the TPC-Perceiver attained an AUC of 0.969 (95% CI: 0.911-1.000), significantly outperforming the Bosniak classification version 2019 (AUC 0.884; p =0.016 ). At the fixed probability threshold of 0.5, the model achieved a sensitivity of 94.4% and a specificity of 96.7%, compared with 100.0% and 76.9%, respectively, for the clinical standard. Furthermore, decision curve analysis indicated that the deep learning framework conferred greater net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. Conclusion The integrated framework showed favorable performance for cystic renal lesion risk stratification. Exploratory pairwise AUC comparisons favored the TPC Perceiver over the single-phase models and the clinical Bosniak v2019 assessment, while its AUC was comparable to that of the previous SETD model. The sensitivity-specificity profile observed at the fixed threshold suggests potential value in reducing false-positive risk stratification. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required before clinical implementation.

title: Multimodal radiomics based on dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound for predicting cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma with Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to develop and validate a multimodal predictive model by integrating radiomic features from B-mode ultrasound (BMUS) and dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound (DCE-US) parametric imaging, as well as clinical and conventional ultrasound features, for preoperative prediction of cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) complicated with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). Methods A total of 191 patients with pathologically confirmed HT-complicated PTC were retrospectively enrolled between December 2023 and July 2025. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n=133) and a validation set (n=58) at a 7:3 ratio using a random number generator. Radiomic features were extracted from BMUS images and DCE-US peak enhancement parametric maps. Feature stability was assessed using intraclass and interclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Key features were selected through a sequential process including the Mann-Whitney U test, recursive feature elimination (RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by calculation of the radiomics score (Rad-score). Independent predictors of CLNM were identified using multivariate logistic regression incorporating clinical and ultrasound features. Three predictive models were constructed: a clinical-ultrasound model, a radiomics model, and a combined multi-modal model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis. Results TG-Ab, TR-Ab, extrathyroidal extension, filling defects, BMUS Rad-score, and DCE-US Rad-score were independent predictors of CLNM (P < 0.05). In the training and validation sets, the combined model achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.936 and 0.916, respectively, which were significantly higher than those of the radiomics model (AUC = 0.825, 0.876) and the clinical-ultrasound model (AUC = 0.760, 0.800; DeLong test, P < 0.05). Calibration curves showed good model fitting. DCA confirmed that the combined model provided greater clinical net benefit. NRI and IDI verified that the combined model significantly improved CLNM prediction performance. SHAP analysis revealed that DCE-US Rad-score was the most important predictor for CLNM. Conclusion A multi-modal predictive model combining dual-modality ultrasound radiomic scores (BMUS and DCE-US) with clinical and ultrasound features can effectively and robustly predict CLNM in patients with HT-complicated PTC and performs better than single-modal models. This model provides an objective reference for the formulation of individualized surgical strategies.

title: The feasibility of training nnU-Net to segment pediatric Wilms tumor with small datasets.
abstract: Introduction Segmentation of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can be used in the clinical care of patients with (suspected) Wilms tumor (WT). Manual segmentation, however, is time consuming and user dependent. Deep learning can be used to automate this, but is often associated with the need for large training datasets to be trained successfully, which is inherently challenging in pediatric populations. The aim of this study was to determine the effect of the number of training patients on automated WT segmentation. Methods 56 patients with a suspected WT were included in this retrospective study. The pre-operative MRI scans were divided in a training (n = 45) and test (n = 11) set. The segmentation was based on nnU-Net, an out-of-the-box framework for image segmentation. nnU-Net was trained on a random selection of five patients, and the resulting segmentation method was tested on a fixed test set of 11 patients. Next, patients were added to the training dataset with incremental steps of five patients, up to the full dataset of 45 patients. This process was repeated 5 times to account for random sampling. The Dice score was used as measure for segmentation performance. We pragmatically defined a Dice score of > 0.80 as a reference level for segmentation performance. Results The lowest median Dice score was obtained when using a subset of five training patients (0.38). The highest median Dice score was observed for training on 45 patients (0.91). An median Dice score of 0.80 was reached using a minimal subset of 10 training patients. The Dice score showed dependency on the random selection of the training patients, with the largest spread in performance observed in the training set of five patients. A large spread in performance between the 11 test set patients was observed. Discussion Using this specific training and test cohort, a median Dice score of 0.80 was reached with just 10 training patients, however, the results showed considerable variation in the individual test patients. The performance spread between the random subsampling of the training patients highlights the importance of clinically representable datasets when dealing with the small dataset sizes inherent to pediatric oncology.

The Dice score showed dependency on the random selection of the training patients, with the largest spread in performance observed in the training set of five patients. A large spread in performance between the 11 test set patients was observed.

Discussion

Using this specific training and test cohort, a median Dice score of 0.80 was reached with just 10 training patients, however, the results showed considerable variation in the individual test patients. The performance spread between the random subsampling of the training patients highlights the importance of clinically representable datasets when dealing with the small dataset sizes inherent to pediatric oncology.

title: Two case reports of small cell lung cancer: typical CT manifestations, with one case illustrating adjunctive CT-based diagnosis without pathological confirmation.
abstract: Background Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a highly malignant neuroendocrine tumor with rapid progression and poor prognosis. Pathological examination is the gold standard for its diagnosis, yet pathological sampling is unfeasible in some clinical scenarios due to various constraints, making imaging and tumor markers critical for clinical decision-making. This two-case report describes the typical computed tomography (CT) findings of SCLC and explores the clinical value of combining CT imaging with tumor markers in guiding the diagnosis and treatment of SCLC patients for whom pathological confirmation is not feasible. Case report We report two SCLC cases: Case 1 was a 56-year-old male with pathologically confirmed SCLC who presented typical imaging findings of hilar and mediastinal fused lymph nodes and achieved a partial response after combined chemoradiotherapy. Case 2 was a 67-year-old male with chest tightness and hemoptysis for 2 months, whose chest CT showed fused lymph nodes (a typical SCLC feature) and markedly elevated neuron-specific enolase (NSE: 221 ng/mL; reference range 1-16.2 ng/mL). Biopsy was unfeasible due to recent coronary stenting and ongoing antiplatelet therapy, and a clinical diagnosis of limited-stage SCLC was made via a combination of typical CT imaging features, significantly elevated NSE and clinical symptoms. The patient received timely EC regimen chemotherapy and subsequent standard chemoradiotherapy, which resulted in a clinical complete response (CR). Conclusions This case report details the typical CT manifestations of SCLC and demonstrates that the combined application of typical CT findings, tumor markers and clinical symptoms may provide a pragmatic basis for timely clinical diagnosis and treatment of SCLC patients when pathological sampling is not achievable. This approach may help avoid treatment delay and improve clinical outcomes for such patients, while emphasizing that pathological examination remains the gold standard for SCLC diagnosis.

title: IVIM-based habitat imaging for non-invasive assessment of Ki-67 proliferation status in cervical cancer.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate whether voxel-level IVIM-based habitat analysis supports exploratory pretreatment stratification of Ki-67 proliferation status in cervical cancer. Materials and methods Between January 2019 and June 2025, medical records of 149 patients with histopathologically confirmed cervical cancer were initially screened. Before image-quality assessment, 49 were excluded because IVIM MRI had been performed after chemoradiotherapy (n = 5), cervical biopsy sampling (n = 21), or lesion excision (n = 10), or because no pathological Ki-67 immunohistochemistry result was available (n = 13). Of the remaining 100 patients, 17 were excluded because of severe image artefacts (n = 11) or lesions too small for reliable ROI delineation (n = 6), leaving 83 patients for analysis. Patients were stratified into high Ki-67 (Ki-67 >70%, n = 38) and low/equal Ki-67 (Ki-67 ≤70%, n = 45) groups. Solid-tumour regions were analysed with patient-level K-means clustering using normalised D, f, and ADC features; D* was excluded from clustering because of voxel-level fitting instability. Habitat labels were harmonised according to quantitative parameter profiles and treated as image-defined phenotypes. Habitat-derived features, conventional ROI parameters, and logistic models were evaluated for Ki-67 stratification. Results Hab1 ADC was lower in the high- than in the low/equal-Ki-67 group (median [Q1-Q3], 0.947 [0.862-1.161] vs. 1.257 [1.113-1.455] × 10 -3 mm 2 /s; P < 0.001; BH q = 2.04×10 -6 ), whereas Hab3 volume proportion was higher (0.396 [0.341-0.488] vs. 0.279 [0.190-0.390]; P = 0.002; BH q = 0.006). Hab1 ADC outperformed conventional ROI ADC for identifying high Ki-67 status [AUC, 0.826 (95% CI, 0.726-0.909) vs. 0.563 (95% CI, 0.429-0.695); paired DeLong P < 0.001]. The combined Hab1 ADC and Hab3 volume proportion model showed the numerically highest discrimination (apparent AUC, 0.877; 95% CI, 0.794-0.938), but this numerical improvement over Hab1 ADC alone was not statistically significant (paired DeLong P = 0.056). Fixed-feature leave-one-out validation of the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.855 (95% CI, 0.771-0.923) and a Brier score of 0.157 (95% CI, 0.112-0.204). Conclusion IVIM-based habitat analysis showed exploratory potential for non-invasive Ki-67 stratification by isolating a low-diffusivity imaging compartment otherwise obscured by conventional whole-tumour averaging. The combined habitat model should be interpreted as a research-stage imaging biomarker, not a clinical decision tool, and requires prospective external validation before clinical translation.

title: A multimodal deep learning radiomics nomogram integrating clinicopathological features for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant therapy in triple-negative breast cancer: a multicenter retrospective study.
abstract: Background Accurate noninvasive estimation of pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) may support multidisciplinary discussions, but multimodal MRI-ultrasound evidence remains limited. We developed and externally validated a clinicopathological deep learning radiomics nomogram and explored its potential auxiliary value in a strictly hypothetical post-hoc surgical-planning scenario. Methods With institutional review-board approval and waived consent, this retrospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study included 436 biopsy-proven TNBC patients who underwent NAT and surgery: Center 1 training cohort (n = 268) and internal validation cohort (n = 86), plus historical cases from cooperating Centers 2-3 for external validation (n = 82). pCR was defined as ypT0/is ypN0. Pretreatment dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)/apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and B-mode ultrasound were analyzed. Intratumoral and 5-mm peritumoral ring radiomics features were extracted and selected by LASSO. DenseNet-121 extracted modality-specific deep features, fused using multi-head self-attention. Age, tumor size, Ki-67, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), cT/N stage, and histological grade were integrated with imaging scores in a logistic-regression nomogram. Parameters and thresholds were locked after Center 1 development and applied once to external data. No model output was used clinically. Feature standardization and ComBat harmonization parameters were strictly locked to the training cohort before application to validation data. Results pCR occurred in 182/436 patients (41.7%). The nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.917 (95% CI, 0.881-0.947) in training, 0.883 (0.814-0.937) in internal validation, and 0.856 (0.773-0.921) in external validation, exceeding clinical (external AUC, 0.721), radiomics (0.786), and deep learning (0.819) models. External sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy at the locked threshold were 0.765, 0.813, and 0.793, respectively. Calibration was acceptable (slope, 0.93; intercept, -0.06; Brier score, 0.16). Decision curve analysis showed net benefit for thresholds of 0.20-0.70. Multi-threshold analysis revealed that a high-specificity threshold (0.65) yielded a positive predictive value of 0.85, potentially identifying a subset of patients with very high confidence of achieving pCR. Compared with the clinical model, external reclassification improved (continuous net reclassification improvement [NRI], 0.34; integrated discrimination improvement [IDI], 0.11; P = 0.003 and P = 0.008, respectively). Conclusion Among the few multicenter TNBC studies combining MRI, ultrasound, intratumoral/peritumoral radiomics, and attention-based deep learning, this nomogram showed good retrospective accuracy for pCR prediction after NAT. The model is presented as an aid for pCR prediction and preoperative stratification rather than as direct support for surgical decision-making. Prospective validation and clinical-impact studies are required before implementation.

title: Case Report: Prolonged survival following multimodal treatment of leptomeningeal metastases in triple-negative glycogen-rich clear cell breast carcinoma.
abstract: Leptomeningeal metastases (LM) are a devastating complication of advanced breast cancer and confer an especially poor prognosis in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Therapeutic options for LM remain limited. Glycogen-rich clear cell (GRCC) carcinoma of the breast is an exceptionally rare histological subtype, with poorly defined metastatic patterns and optimal management strategies. This report presents a case of TNBC exhibiting GRCC characteristics, further complicated by LM. A 51-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage IV TNBC with GRCC morphology and concomitant axillary lymph node and liver metastases. Ten months after the initial diagnosis, LM was confirmed by brain magnetic resonance imaging and cerebrospinal fluid cytology. Marked clinical improvement was achieved following ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt placement and systemic treatment with sacituzumab govitecan (SG). The patient survived for 21 months since the diagnosis of LM and maintaining good functional status until the final month of her life. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of LM arising from GRCC carcinoma of the breast. This case suggests a potential therapeutic role for SG in LM associated with TNBC and raises the hypothesis that VP shunting may enhance treatment efficacy by altering drug exposure. Further studies are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Vascular habitat analysis using dynamic susceptibility contrast-enhanced perfusion MRI for differentiating glioblastoma from solitary brain metastases.
abstract: Objective To investigate tumor vascular habitat parameters based on dynamic susceptibility contrast-enhanced perfusion-weighted imaging (DSC-PWI) for differentiating glioblastoma (GBM) from solitary brain metastasis (SBM). Methods In this single-center retrospective study, imaging data from 141 patients with pathologically or clinically confirmed malignant brain tumors (74 GBM, 67 SBM) were analyzed. The hemodynamic tissue signature (HTS) method was used to segment the lesions and construct four tumor vascular habitats: high angiogenic tumor (HAT), low angiogenic tumor (LAT), potentially infiltrated peripheral edema (IPE), and vasogenic peripheral edema (VPE). Pearson correlation analysis was used to quantify the correlations among habitat hemodynamic parameters. Habitat characteristic parameters were calculated, and ROC were plotted to evaluate the diagnostic performance. A nomogram model was constructed using logistic regression. Results GBM exhibited significantly higher median relative cerebral blood volume (rCBV median ) and median relative cerebral blood flow (rCBF median ) than SBM across all four habitat regions (all p < 0.001). In terms of volumetric parameters, the ratio of IPE volume to peritumoral volume ( V (IPE) / V (P) ) was significantly higher in the GBM group ( p < 0.001). Among individual habitat parameters, LAT rCBF median showed the best diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.786 (95% CI: 0.709-0.850). In the GBM group, the perfusion parameters of the IPE and VPE were significantly positively correlated with those of the HAT, whereas no such correlation was found in the SBM group. A nomogram incorporating lesion location, enhancement pattern, and LAT-rCBF median yielded an AUC of 0.857 (95% CI: 0.79-0.92) for distinguishing GBM from SBM, with good calibration. Conclusion Tumor vascular habitat parameters based on DSC-PWI demonstrate significant differences between newly diagnosed GBM and SBM, and the nomogram shows certain value in differentiating between the two tumor types.

title: Artificial intelligence in image-guided cervical interventional radiotherapy: a systematic review.
abstract: Background Imaging-guided interventional radiotherapy (IG-IRT) is the standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer but remains time-consuming and operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to improve efficiency and reproducibility. Methods A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2010 and 2026 investigating AI-based imaging applications in cervical IRT. Eligible studies included original research evaluating segmentation (targets and organ at risk), planning, reconstruction, image registration and applicator selection. Results Fifty-two studies were included. Deep learning-based segmentation showed variable performance across anatomical structures and studies, with Dice coefficients approaching or exceeding 0.90 for some organs at risk and target volumes in the best-performing models. Individual studies reported shorter processing times, reduced contouring variability, accurate applicator reconstruction, and potential support for applicator selection. However, the substantial methodological and clinical heterogeneity precluded direct comparisons among AI approaches. Conclusions The available studies suggest that AI may support the automation of selected workflow steps and assist treatment-related decision-making in image-guided cervical interventional radiotherapy. While several applications have achieved high technical performance, most remain at the proof-of-concept stage, and robust external validation and prospective clinical evaluation are needed before routine clinical adoption.

title: Dosimetric benefits of deep inspiration breath-hold in postoperative radiotherapy for left-sided breast cancer after breast-conserving surgery: an anatomical parameter-based analysis.
abstract: Objective To investigate the dosimetric impact of deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH) technique on radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery for left-sided breast cancer, and to explore the relationship between patient anatomical characteristics and dosimetric benefits of DIBH, providing preliminary evidence for understanding individual differences in DIBH related dosimetric gains and their personalized application. Methods This retrospective study included 17 patients who underwent postoperative radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery for left-sided breast cancer. All patients underwent computed tomography (CT) simulation under both DIBH and free-breathing (FB) conditions, and intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) plans were generated from both image sets. With identical prescription doses and planning optimization objectives, dosimetric parameters for the left lung, heart, and cardiac substructures were compared between the two respiratory conditions. Correlations of the maximum cardiac margin distance (MCMD), cardiac displacement, cardiac displacement volume, heart-to-breast distance (HBD), and changes in lung volume with dosimetric parameters were also analyzed. Results Compared with FB, DIBH significantly reduced the mean dose (Dmean), V20, and V30 of the left lung, as well as the cardiac Dmean, V20, V30, and V40 (all P < 0.05). In addition, DIBH significantly reduced the mean doses to of the right ventricle (RV), left ventricle (LV), and left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) compared with FB (all P < 0.05). Correlation analysis demonstrated that MCMD under the DIBH condition was positively correlated with cardiac Dmean. The change in MCMD between DIBH and FB was negatively correlated with cardiac and ventricular dose parameters. Cardiac displacement volume between the two respiratory states was positively correlated with changes in mean heart dose. Further analysis revealed that changes in lung volume were positively correlated with cardiac displacement along the Z-axis and changes in HBD while negatively correlated with LAD Dmean under the DIBH condition. Conclusion DIBH can reduce radiation exposure to the left lung, heart, and selected cardiac substructures while satisfying target-dose requirements. Exploratory analyses indicated that cardiac geometric parameters and changes in lung volume were associated with selected dosimetric parameters, suggesting that dynamic anatomical changes during DIBH may help explain interindividual differences in dosimetric benefit. These findings require further validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

title: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumor of the kidney with prominent peritumoral adipose tissue: a case report radiologically mimicking angiomyolipoma with epithelial cysts.
abstract: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumor of the kidney (MEST) is a rare renal neoplasm with biphasic differentiation comprising epithelial and stromal components. It typically appears as a mixed cystic-solid mass on imaging, and the prognosis is favorable in the vast majority of cases. We report a case of MEST with a prominent fat component on imaging: a 54-year-old woman was admitted with a 1-month history of left flank distension and pain. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed a mixed cystic-solid mass at the lower pole of the left kidney, with a prominent low-attenuation fat-density area surrounding the mass. Preoperatively, the lesion was considered an unusual angiomyolipoma with epithelial cysts (AMLEC). Because the lesion was small, located at the lower pole, and relatively well circumscribed, the patient underwent laparoscopic left partial nephrectomy. Postoperative histopathologic examination confirmed that the left renal mass was benign; however, immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrated positivity for EMA and PCK in the epithelial component and for PR and ER in the stromal component, supporting a diagnosis of MEST. The adipose tissue submitted separately with the tumor was located around the tumor and could not be definitively confirmed as an intratumoral component. This case demonstrates that MEST may also exhibit prominent adipose tissue on imaging and illustrates the diagnostic pitfall in which fat-related imaging findings cause MEST to mimic AMLEC, making the early distinction between MEST and cystic change in fat-containing renal tumors challenging.

title: Retroauricular approach for carotid body tumor resection: a case report.
abstract: Introduction Carotid body tumors (CBTs) are rare and highly vascular paragangliomas arising at the carotid bifurcation. Surgical resection remains the standard treatment for CBTs. However, the conventional transcervical approach inevitably leaves a visible cervical scar, which may negatively affect quality of life in patients with cosmetic concerns. Case presentation A 27-year-old woman presented with a progressively enlarging right neck mass over a 6-month period. Ultrasonography demonstrated a hypervascular lesion surrounding the carotid arteries, and fine-needle aspiration was avoided because of the vascular nature of the tumor. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 4-cm enhancing mass at the carotid bifurcation, highly suggestive of a CBT. Because the patient expressed concern regarding a visible cervical scar, a retroauricular approach was selected after thorough discussion of its potential risks and benefits. The operation was performed by a head and neck surgeon with intraoperative assistance from a vascular surgeon. Complete tumor resection was successfully achieved despite the need for repair of two small arterial defects encountered during tumor mobilization. The operative time was 300 minutes, and the estimated blood loss was 900 mL. The postoperative course was uneventful, and no major complications or tumor recurrence were observed during 12 months of follow-up. The patient reported satisfaction with the cosmetic outcome, although no objective cosmetic assessment was performed. Conclusion In carefully selected patients with Shamblin type I or II CBT, the retroauricular approach may represent a feasible hidden-scar alternative to the conventional transcervical approach.

title: Ultrasonic manifestations of diffuse pericardial mesothelioma masquerading as pericardial effusion: a case report.
abstract: Background Primary pericardial mesothelioma (PPM) is an exceedingly rare, highly invasive cardiac neoplasm with insidious onset and non-specific clinical symptoms. Due to the lack of typical early manifestations and effective routine diagnostic methods, PPM is often misdiagnosed and missed, resulting in delayed treatment and poor prognosis. Case presentation A 42-year-old male presented with 6 months of recurrent chest tightness and pain, worsening over 2 months, and two prior admissions for unexplained pericardial effusion. On admission, he had tachycardia, distant heart sounds, bilateral lower extremity edema, and a 3×2 cm hard, fixed left supraclavicular lymph node. Imaging confirmed pericardial effusion with abnormal pericardial lesions. Ultrasound-guided pericardiocentesis yielded only a small amount of red jelly-like material, with cytology suggesting epithelioid neoplastic cells. Supraclavicular lymph node biopsy confirmed metastatic malignant mesothelioma. Nivolumab immunotherapy showed no improvement. Pericardial tumor resection revealed diffuse, fish-flesh-like tumor invading the myocardium and great vessels. Final pathology confirmed epithelioid-type PPM. Conclusion Patients with recurrent unexplained pericardial effusion and atypical sonographic features, such as flocculent echoes and irregular pericardial thickening, should raise suspicion for PPM. Early recognition of these signs and timely pathological confirmation are critical to avoid diagnostic delays and may improve outcomes.

title: Cardio-respiratory-gated proton pencil beam scanning for cardiac ablation: workflow and end-to-end validation.
abstract: Stereotactic Arrhythmia Radiotherapy (STAR) offers a non-invasive alternative for ventricular tachycardia ablation, yet motion management remains a critical challenge. While respiratory gating is established, cardiac gating requires a dedicated workflow and gating device. This study establishes and validates an end-to-end workflow for cardiorespiratory gated proton STAR in six healthy swine. Key innovations include a novel pencil-beam scanning (PBS) controller enabling mid-spot beam pausing and resumption, and the integration of CardioKit, an ultrasound-based image-guidance system for real-time soft-tissue tracking. The workflow was evaluated by comparing single-gated (respiratory only) and dual-gated (cardiorespiratory) delivery strategies, assessing system latency, dosimetric accuracy on dynamic phantoms, and motion tracking fidelity against 4D-CT benchmarks. The upgraded PBS system demonstrated a gate response latency of <550 µs, effectively mitigating interplay effects in dynamic phantom measurements through gated beam deliveries. CardioKit provided respiratory motion traces highly correlated with 4D-CT data (Pearson r > 0.97) and responded to arrhythmic events within 5 ms. In vivo, dual-gating restricted delivery to the diastolic window (70-100% R-R), which resulted in a reduction in the Internal Target Volume (ITV) expansion by a mean of 45% compared to single-gating (19% vs. 64%), thereby substantially sparing healthy myocardium. Although dual-gating increased total beam-on time, the mid-spot interrupt capability ensured robust dose accumulation without treatment aborts. The workflow for imaging, treatment planning, and cardiorespiratory-gated beam delivery was viable for treating all six subjects. The PBS system responded to gating commands < 550 µs and CardioKit responded to irregularities in heartbeat in <5 ms. Cardiorespiratory gating enabled an average 45% reduction in target expansion due to cardiac motion. Comparison of CardioKit respiratory motion traces with respiratory 4D-CT yielded differences of 1.1-1.4 mm in total motion amplitude and 0.97-0.99 Pearson correlation factor. These findings are valuable for establishing a workflow for cardiorespiratory-gated STAR treatment with CardioKit.

title: Radiologist-guided multimodal fusion network for differentiating parotid tumors on 3D non-contrast CT.
abstract: Objectives To improve the diagnostic accuracy of benign versus malignant parotid tumors using non-contrast CT. We propose a clinician-in-the-loop hybrid framework that mitigates low soft-tissue contrast by fusing semi-automated 3D visual features with expert semantic descriptors. Methods This multi-center retrospective study analyzed non-contrast CTs from 367 patients. We developed AttenNet, a semi-automated model. First, an nnU-Net module automates 3D tumor segmentation, eliminating manual bounding boxes. A 3D-ResNet backbone then extracts volumetric features, which are dynamically fused with radiologist-provided semantic labels via a Multi-Head Cross-Attention Fusion (MHAF) mechanism. This allows the network to query visual morphology based on expert priors. Diagnostic performance and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) interpretability were evaluated. Results The segmentation achieved a median Dice of 0.827. AttenNet (3D-ResNet) yielded an AUC of 0.908, significantly outperforming the image-only 3D-ResNet (AUC: 0.741) and expert-feature models (AUC: 0.821). External validation ( n = 20) reached an AUC of 0.560-0.910.However, given the extremely small sample size, these results must be interpreted strictly as an exploratory proof-of-concept rather than definitive confirmation of generalizability. Grad-CAM confirmed that AttenNet highlights clinically essential geometric indicators-specifically tumor margins and internal heterogeneity-for differentiating malignancy, whereas single-modality baselines focused on background artifacts. Conclusion This clinician-in-the-loop paradigm successfully integrates spatial imaging with expert reasoning. While multimodal fusion drove the primary performance gains, the MHAF mechanism provided enhanced spatial interpretability.

title: Non-invasive preoperative MRI-based deep transfer learning radiomics model for predicting meningioma brain invasion.
abstract: Background Current preoperative assessment of meningioma brain invasion (BI) demands imaging analytical frameworks that optimize computational efficiency while capturing multidimensional tumor-pathology correlations. Building upon the inherent advantages of 2.5D MRI in synthesizing multiplanar biological data with manageable processing loads, this study innovatively integrates deep transfer learning (DTL), a technique bridging pretrained network knowledge with target domain adaptation, to systematically identify tumor-invasive biological signatures and develop an optimized predictive system using preoperative contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI). Methods This retrospective study enrolled 674 patients with pathologically confirmed meningiomas, including 53 with BI and 621 without BI. The cohort was stratified into a training set and an independent test set. Tumor regions of interest (ROIs) were delineated on CE-T1WI, and radiomics and DTL features were extracted. Radiomics and DTL features were fused via early fusion, followed by feature selection. Within the training cohort, five-fold cross-validation was performed, with SMOTE applied exclusively to the training portion of each fold; validation folds and the independent test set retained their original class distributions. Results The effectiveness of the models was compared using the area under the ROC curve (AUC). In the training set, ComM achieved an AUC of 0.977, while in the test set, its AUC reached 0.935. ComM demonstrated the best performance (training set: AUCComM > AUCDTLRM > AUCRadM > AUCClinM > AUCDTLM; test set: AUCComM > AUCDTLRM > AUCRadM > AUCDTLM > AUCClinM), showing excellent preoperative predictive capability for meningioma BI. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated good model fit, and the calibration curve revealed that ComM was closest to the ideal curve. Conclusion ClinM, RadM, DTLM, DTLRM, and ComM based on 2.5D CE-T1WI all exhibited good performance in predicting meningioma BI. The clinical-radiomics-DTL fusion model (ComM) demonstrated the highest efficacy, suggesting that DTL provides additional features correlated with meningioma BI that differ from radiomics features. This model shows potential clinical utility for preoperative prediction; however, further external validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

title: Varying diffusion curvature, intravoxel incoherent motion, and conventional monoexponential diffusion models for evaluating Ki-67 expression in rectal carcinoma.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to systematically evaluate and compare the diagnostic performance of three diffusion models - varying diffusion curvature (VDC), intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM), and conventional monoexponential diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) - in predicting Ki-67 expression status in rectal adenocarcinoma. Methods A total of 84 patients with rectal carcinoma were enrolled, comprising 48 cases with high proliferative activity (Ki-67 > 50%) and 36 cases with low proliferative activity (Ki-67 ≤ 50%). All patients underwent pelvic MRI examinations. The following imaging parameters were calculated and compared: VDC-derived parameters (D 0 , D 1 ), IVIM-derived parameters (ADC slow , ADC fast , f), and the DWI-derived parameter (ADC). Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictive factors, and diagnostic performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), the DeLong test, and calibration curves. Results Compared with the low-proliferation group, the high-proliferation group of rectal carcinoma exhibited significantly higher D 1 and f values, along with markedly lower D 0 , ADC, and ADC slow values (all P < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis identified D 1 and ADC slow as independent predictors of Ki-67 status in rectal carcinoma. The combined diagnostic model incorporating D 1 and ADC slow yielded an AUC of 0.924, which was significantly superior to the individual parameters, including ADC (AUC = 0.780), ADC slow (AUC = 0.832), D 0 (AUC = 0.696), D 1 (AUC = 0.857), and f (AUC = 0.802) (all P < 0.05). The calibration curve demonstrated good stability and reliability of the combined diagnostic model. Conclusion Both VDC, IVIM, and DWI demonstrate efficacy in evaluating the Ki-67 expression status in rectal carcinoma. The combined parameters of D 1 and ADC slow may serve as a novel and reliable imaging biomarker for assessing the proliferative activity of rectal carcinoma.

title: Multiparametric MRI-based habitat and peritumoral radiomics integrating semi-automated segmentation for preoperative prediction of high-grade prostate cancer: a dual-center study.
abstract: Background This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning framework that combines semi-automated segmentation, intratumoral habitats derived from multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), and multiscale peritumoral radiomics to predict high-grade prostate cancer (HGPCa) before surgery. Methods This retrospective dual-center study involved 274 patients, comprising 208 from Center 1 for development and 66 from Center 2 for external test. The clinical and imaging variables included patient age, serum PSA, fPSA, PSAD, maximum tumor diameter, PI-RADS scores, and anatomical zone distribution (PZ vs. TZ). The development cohort was randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 145) and an internal validation cohort (n = 63). Intratumoral habitats were delineated using semi-automated segmentation and unsupervised K-means clustering, while peritumoral radiomic features were extracted from concentric 1-, 3-, and 5-mm shells. Predictive classifiers were optimized through machine learning algorithms, particularly a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for the habitat signature. A combined clinical-radiomics nomogram was constructed, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) employed to enhance model interpretability. Subgroup analyses were performed to assess the discriminative performance of the combined nomogram across the peripheral zone (PZ) and transition zone (TZ). Results The combined nomogram exhibited superior diagnostic performance, achieving AUCs of 0.914, 0.903, and 0.797 in the training cohort, internal validation cohort, and external test cohort, respectively. The MLP-based habitat model showed good discriminative performance, with AUCs of 0.896, 0.897, and 0.782 across the training cohort, internal validation cohort, and external test cohort, respectively. Among the peritumoral regions, the 5-mm shell demonstrated the best discriminative performance. SHAP analysis identified Habitat 1 Shape Sphericity as the most influential feature. Subgroup analysis demonstrated the discriminatory ability of the combined nomogram in both the PZ (AUC: 0.796) and TZ (AUC: 0.753) subgroups. Conclusion The integration of semi-automated segmentation-based habitat analysis and peritumoral radiomics provides a promising approach for preoperative risk stratification of prostate cancer.

title: Liquid biopsy using circulating miRNAs for the identification of recurrence-associated biomarkers in glioblastoma CNS WHO grade 4.
abstract: Introduction Glioblastoma CNS WHO Grade 4 (GBM) is associated with poor prognosis and high recurrence rates despite the current therapeutic approaches. Conventional imaging, in particular Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), is primarily used during follow-up to detect tumor recurrence but has limited ability to distinguish recurrence from therapy-related changes, such as tissue necrosis and postoperative scar tissue. Liquid biopsy using circulating tumor-specific serological biomarkers, such as miRNAs, provides a gene expression signature for early identification of GBM recurrence. This pilot "proof-of-concept" study investigated the potential of circulating tumor-derived miRNA in whole blood samples for early detection of tumor recurrence. Methods In a previous whole-transcriptome screening (NGS) study, whole-blood samples (n = 33) from seven patients and tumor biopsies (n = 4) were used to identify biomarkers. Corresponding to tumor surgery and recurrence, miRNA expression was examined in pre-surgical blood samples and tumor tissues. In whole blood, we investigated whether a pattern could be identified indicating post-surgery downregulation, consistent with reduced tumor burden, followed by a return to pre-surgery levels at recurrence. We identified 1-19 miRNA species per patient (a total of 72 miRNAs) showing this pattern. In this manuscript, we present the qRT-PCR validation results. The 45 most promising miRNAs identified by NGS study were selected and quantified using qRT-PCR. In addition, miR-21 was included as a promising candidate reported in the literature. To address challenges in miRNA normalization, five normalization strategies and unnormalized raw Ct values were compared. Results Two normalization approaches (median DCt normalization and unnormalized raw Ct values) showed no systematic bias. Depending on the normalization method, the agreement between NGS and qRT-PCR ranged from 23.6 to 27.9%. Although the concordance between NGS and qRT-PCR was low at the individual-patient level, qRT-PCR identified a common set of 24 miRNAs differentially regulated across patients. Notably, miR-424-3p and miR-362-5p were shared by five of seven patients, followed by miR-1307-3p and miR-22-5p , each shared by four patients. Interestingly, miR-21 did not show the predefined recurrence-associated pattern in any patient. Discussion Blood-based miRNA profiling may complement imaging in longitudinal monitoring of GBM patients, although clinical benefits have not been confirmed, and validation in a larger independent cohort is required.

title: Multiparametric MRI-based radiomics combined with deep learning for preoperative risk stratification of endometrial carcinoma.
abstract: Objective To develop and compare radiomics, deep learning, clinical, and combined models based on multiparametric MRI radiomics and 2.5D deep learning features for preoperative risk stratification of endometrial carcinoma (EC). Methods This retrospective study included 246 patients with pathologically confirmed EC, with preoperative clinical and imaging data collected. Clinical data, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) were collected. Radiomics and deep learning models were constructed based on T2WI, CE-T1WI, and their combination. A combined model integrating multiparametric radiomics features, deep learning features, and clinical parameters was subsequently developed. Model performance and clinical utility were evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and the DeLong test for pairwise model comparisons. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was employed to enhance model interpretability. Results Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis identified maximum tumor diameter, MR-DMI, BMI and ER status as independent predictive factors. Comparison of radiomics, deep learning, clinical, and combined models demonstrated that the multiparametric MRI model outperformed single-sequence models based on radiomics or deep learning, while the combined model exhibited the best predictive performance in the validation set, achieving an AUC of 0.891, accuracy of 0.86, sensitivity of 0.909, specificity of 0.765, and F1-score of 0.896. DeLong test results showed that, in the training set, the combined model had higher predictive performance than all other models, and the differences were statistically significant (P < 0.05). In the validation set, the combined model showed statistically significant improvements compared with the clinical model and the T2+CET1-Rad model (P<0.05). Decision curve analysis indicated that the combined model provided the highest clinical net benefit. Conclusion The combination of multiparametric MRI-based radiomics and 2.5D deep learning demonstrated favorable predictive performance in stratifying risk for EC, suggesting its potential utility as a non-invasive tool and offering a promising adjunctive approach to support personalized treatment planning and prognostic evaluation for EC patients in clinical practice.

title: Macroscopic versus rapid on-site evaluation for EUS-guided tissue acquisition of solid pancreatic masses: a systematic review, diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis, and network meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition (EUS-TA) is central to the pathological diagnosis of solid pancreatic masses, but the comparative value of rapid on-site cytologic evaluation (ROSE), macroscopic on-site evaluation (MOSE), and no on-site evaluation (NONE) may vary by needle type and remains uncertain. Methods We performed a PRISMA-DTA systematic review registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251241446). Potential cohort overlap and data dependency were assessed before quantitative synthesis. Diagnostic 2 × 2 data were synthesized with a bivariate binomial-normal random-effects model. Independent direct comparisons were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis for correct versus incorrect diagnosis, with complementary absolute differences in sensitivity and specificity. An exploratory three-node network meta-analysis (NMA) compared ROSE, MOSE, and NONE. Results Thirty-one eligible reports contributed 67 strategy-specific diagnostic datasets. After excluding 21 duplicate, nested, paired, or otherwise dependent datasets, 46 independent datasets representing 4,901 arm-level observations were included in the primary DTA. Pooled sensitivity was 0.94 (95% CI 0.92-0.95) and specificity was 1.00 (0.98-1.00); Deeks' asymmetry test was positive (P <0.001). In direct comparisons, ROSE improved composite diagnostic accuracy versus NONE in FNA studies (OR 5.56, 95% CI 1.76-17.62; k = 4), but not in FNB studies (OR 1.08, 0.42-2.79; k = 4); the FNA-versus-FNB interaction was exploratory (P = 0.012). MOSE versus NONE in FNB was uncertain (OR 1.31, 0.60-2.87; k = 4), as was MOSE versus ROSE (OR 1.53, 0.05-49.13; k = 3). The exploratory NMA did not identify a statistically clear difference for ROSE versus NONE (OR 1.67, 0.94-2.95), MOSE versus NONE (OR 1.89, 0.86-4.20), or MOSE versus ROSE (OR 1.14, 0.48-2.71). Conclusions EUS-TA showed high overall diagnostic performance. ROSE may add value in FNA-era workflows, whereas a clear incremental benefit was not detected with FNB. MOSE remains a plausible resource-sparing strategy, but comparative estimates are imprecise. The NMA should be regarded as hypothesis-generating because of sparse comparisons, methodological heterogeneity, small-study effects, and low-to-very-low certainty. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251241446.

title: Primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma with brain metastases in a male: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Background Primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma (PPC) is an exceptionally rare and highly aggressive extragonadal trophoblastic malignancy in males, with no established standard treatment. Cytotoxic chemotherapy alone generally yields limited therapeutic benefit, while the role of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains poorly defined. Case presentation Here, we report a 41-year-old man who presented with a six-month history of cough and was found to have a large right upper lobe pulmonary mass with multiple brain metastases. Histopathological examination revealed typical trophoblastic differentiation, and immunohistochemistry demonstrated diffuse positivity for HCG, CK7, GATA3, and SALL4, whereas TTF-1 and Napsin A were negative. Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-HCG) was markedly elevated (> 10, 000 mIU/mL), and no gonadal primary lesion was identified, confirming the diagnosis of primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma. Intervention/outcome The patient underwent multimodal treatment including radiotherapy, EMA/CO chemotherapy, EMA/EP combined with sintilimab, and third-line therapy consisting of nab-paclitaxel, bevacizumab, and penpulimab. Despite intensive treatment, the disease progressed rapidly with new intracranial and systemic metastases. Throughout the disease course, serial β-HCG measurements closely paralleled radiographic findings and provided timely guidance for therapeutic decision-making. In addition, we reviewed previously reported metastatic male PPC cases and performed an exploratory survival analysis, which suggested that patients receiving ICI-based therapy tended to have longer overall survival than those treated without immunotherapy. Conclusion Although these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size, this case highlights the highly aggressive nature of male PPC, emphasizes the diagnostic and monitoring value of dynamic β-HCG assessment, and supports further investigation of chemoimmunotherapy as a potential treatment strategy for this rare malignancy.

abstract: Introduction This study, through a meta-analysis, aimed to assess the predictive performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) for microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library were comprehensively searched from database inception to January 13, 2026. EndNote 21was employed for literature screening and data extraction. Meta-analysis was carried out on the extracted data using Stata 15, MetaDisc 1.4, and MedCalc. Results In total, 21 studies were included, involving 2,023 patients with HCC, of whom 890 were MVI+ and 1,133 were MVI-. In univariable analyses, both tumor-to-normal liver uptake ratio (TLR) (odds ratio [OR] = 2.577, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.446-4.593, P = 0.001) and maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) (OR = 1.272, 95% CI: 1.036-1.561, P = 0.021) were significantly associated with an increased MVI risk. After multivariable adjustment, SUVmax retained independent predictive value (OR = 2.140, 95% CI: 1.244-3.681, P = 0.006), whereas the multivariable evidence for TLR was derived from a single study and required further validation. AUC values for SUVmax and radiomics score (Rad-score) were 0.819 (95% CI: 0.739-0.899) and 0.809 (95% CI: 0.762-0.857), respectively, with relatively balanced values for sensitivity, specificity, and negative likelihood ratio. Conclusion The available evidence supports SUVmax as one of the metabolic markers for preoperative MVI risk assessment in HCC, with Rad-score similar to SUVmax in diagnostic discrimination. The complementary value of the two markers was not demonstrated by this Meta-analysis, but rather derived from inferences proposed by external studies. Moreover, because the included radiomics studies did not report a pooled effect size for the combined model integrating SUVmax and Rad-score, a Meta-analysis targeting this model is currently not feasible. Therefore, the complementarity of SUVmax and Rad-score should be regarded as a hypothesis to be tested. In the future, multicenter, prospective radiomics studies with rigorous external validation are warranted to further explore a combined prediction model based on SUVmax and Rad-score. On this basis, an integrated assessment workflow should be gradually established, by which preoperative decisions are guided. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261289724.

title: A prospective pilot study of urine microRNA as a biomarker of urinary radiation toxicity following MRI-guided prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy.
abstract: Introduction Urinary toxicities are common following prostate radiotherapy and can impair quality of life. New biomarkers are needed that can predict the risk of urinary toxicity following MRI guided stereotactic body radiotherapy (MR-SBRT) to assist with selection of the most appropriate radiotherapy treatment approach. We aimed to identify urine miRNA biomarkers of radiation-induced urinary toxicities. Methods Ten patients undergoing MR-SBRT were enrolled on a prospective biorepository protocol and urine specimens were collected before, at the final fraction and 2-4 months following radiotherapy. RNA was isolated and microRNA sequencing was performed followed by qPCR for confirmation of microRNA expression changes. Differences in microRNA expression were assessed with regard to timepoint, cancer risk category and urinary toxicity. Results Both sequencing and qPCR showed that expressions of miR-26a-5p and miR-95-3p decrease during MR-SBRT and increase during early follow up. miR-204-3p and miR-192-5p changed differently in patients with and without urinary radiation toxicity. Expression of miR-375-3p was lower in patients with higher risk category (NCCN unfavorable intermediate to high risk or recurrent/metastatic) at all timepoints and decreased during and after MR-SBRT, especially in patients with a lower risk category (NCCN low to favorable intermediate risk) of prostate cancer. Discussion Urine microRNA analysis is feasible and may identify biomarkers linked to radiation-induced urinary toxicity and prostate cancer severity. The findings of this pilot study are limited by the sample size and should be prospectively validated.

title: Relevance between patients' clinical factors and 4D-CT lung ventilation heterogeneity for evaluating the adoption of functional avoidance thoracic radiotherapy with a large patient database.
abstract: Objective Four-dimensional computed tomography (4D-CT)-guided functional-avoidance radiotherapy reduces radiation pneumonitis, but the lack of patient selection criteria limits its adoption. This study aimed to identify clinical predictors of lung ventilation heterogeneity and determine which patients derive the greatest dosimetric benefit from functional-avoidance planning. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 274 lung cancer patients. 4D-CT ventilation imaging was generated via deformable registration and a density-change algorithm, and the coefficient of variation (CoV) across six lung zones quantified heterogeneity. Clinical factors were assessed using Mann-Whitney U, Spearman, and multivariable logistic regression for three ventilation outcomes. Thirty-two patients were selected from CoV quartiles and re-planned with functional-avoidance plans; dosimetric parameters were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction applied to address multiple comparisons. Results Univariate analysis showed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and airway obstruction reduced bilateral mean ventilation, while central tumors impaired ipsilateral ventilation. Higher CoV was observed in stage III-IV versus I-II, central versus peripheral tumors, and patients with airway obstruction. Multivariable analysis identified airway obstruction as an independent predictor of elevated CoV (adjusted OR = 2.914, 95% CI: 1.315-6.454, P<0.05). Central location and advanced stage showed borderline significance, while COPD trended toward lower CoV. Dosimetrically, functional-avoidance plans reduced functional lung metrics in a heterogeneity-dependent manner. After FDR correction, key metrics (fMLD, fV10, fV20, fV30) remained significant in Group 1 (highest CoV; Q = 0.040-0.049), while significance diminished in lower CoV groups. Leave-one-out (LOO) sensitivity analysis confirmed fMLD and fV20 as robust endpoints. Furthermore, beam arrangement modifications were most frequent in Group 1 (5/8 patients) and absent in Group 4 (0/8), reflecting clinical optimization needs rather than confounding. Conclusions Ventilation heterogeneity is driven by tumor burden and airway patency. Patients with advanced stage, central tumors, or airway obstruction exhibit the strongest heterogeneity and may represent appropriate candidates for functional-avoidance radiotherapy in future prospective trials. However, as this replanning study lacked clinical follow-up for radiation pneumonitis, these findings reflect dosimetric rather than confirmed clinical patient-level benefit. Notably, CoV quartiles were derived from internal median splits within this cohort and require external validation. This study provides a dosimetric basis for hypothesis-generating patient selection.
