title: CBCT-based adaptive radiotherapy and automated radiotherapy decision-making systems: development and current status.
abstract: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-based adaptive radiotherapy (ART) has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing inter-fractional anatomical and physiological changes during treatment. By incorporating on-treatment imaging, ART enables treatment plans to be adapted to the anatomy of the day, with the potential to improve target coverage and reduce dose exposure to organs at risk (OARs). However, routine implementation remains constrained by the limited image quality of CBCT, uncertainties in dose calculation, labour-intensive workflows and the lack of reliable criteria for determining when adaptation is clinically necessary. This review summarises the development, current status and future prospects of CBCT-based ART, with particular emphasis on artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted automated delineation and automated radiotherapy decision-making systems. CBCT is widely available on modern linear accelerators and remains the most practical imaging basis for ART in many centres. Nevertheless, poor soft-tissue contrast, noise, artefacts, field-of-view truncation and unstable Hounsfield unit values limit its performance in target delineation and dose reconstruction. Recent advances in image-quality enhancement, deformable image registration and synthetic CT generation have partially addressed these limitations. AI-based auto-segmentation models, including convolutional neural networks, Transformers, generative adversarial networks and diffusion models, have demonstrated increasingly favourable geometric accuracy and workflow efficiency. Automated decision-making systems can advise clinicians whether treatment-plan adaptation is required and how it should be implemented according to each patient's circumstances, representing a prerequisite for more efficient ART. Current research has mainly focused on two approaches: adaptation triggered by predefined dosimetric thresholds, and artificial-intelligence-based models that learn from prior knowledge and predict potential dosimetric changes for the current patient based on previous experience. Both approaches have their respective strengths and limitations, but require further refinement, including the systematic exploration of decision thresholds. Moreover, the realisation of fully automated adaptive radiotherapy will require the integration of additional systems, including automated treatment planning and automated QA. Overall, CBCT-based ART assisted by AI is technically feasible and may improve dosimetric quality and treatment efficiency. Future progress requires improved CBCT-specific algorithms, integrated automated planning and QA, multicentre validation, standardised safety frameworks and stronger evidence of clinical benefit.

title: Multiple sclerosis relapse following gamma knife radiosurgery for meningioma in a patient treated with natalizumab: case report.
abstract: Objectives We describe a case of a patient with multiple sclerosis (MS) stable on natalizumab who developed widespread gadolinium-enhancing lesions and clinical relapse seven and eight months after gamma knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for left cerebellar convexity meningioma. We explore how increased blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability post-GKRS could potentially interfere with the lymphocyte anti-trafficking effect of natalizumab and result in new central nervous system (CNS) inflammation distant from the radiation site. Methods Comprehensive analysis of the patient's chart, brain and spine imaging, serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) profiles was conducted. We compiled a graphical representation of treatment changes, radiologic findings, and GKRS initiation within one timeframe. We conducted a structured literature review to support the discussion of this case and hypothesize possible pathophysiological mechanisms contributing to clinical and radiological findings. Results Seven months after GKRS, follow-up brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multiple gadolinium-enhancing lesions in both cerebral hemispheres, and repeat imaging one month later revealed new gadolinium-enhancing lesions, correlating with the patient's clinical relapse. Alternative causes of disease progression, including radiation-induced demyelination, radionecrosis, opportunistic infections, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), and development of anti-natalizumab antibodies, were explored and considered less likely. The patient was switched to ofatumumab with subsequent clinical and radiological stability. Discussion Given extensive new inflammatory lesions far from the GKRS site, it seems unlikely that the sole mechanism was radiation-induced neurotoxicity. We hypothesize that late delayed radiation side effects caused by GKRS may have enabled peripheral lymphocytes to enter the CNS, counteracting the effects of natalizumab on blocking lymphocyte trafficking through the BBB and possibly contributing to MS relapse.

title: Case Report: Long-term survival in FIGO stage IVB small cell carcinoma of the ovary, pulmonary type following complete cytoreduction and platinum re-challenge.
abstract: Background Small cell carcinoma of the ovary, pulmonary type (SCCOPT), is a rare and highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis. Long-term survival in advanced-stage disease has rarely been reported. Case presentation A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman presented with FIGO stage IVB SCCOPT accompanied by extensive peritoneal carcinomatosis and a solitary liver metastasis. No pulmonary lesion suggestive of primary lung malignancy was identified on CT, PET/CT, or chest radiography. She underwent aggressive primary cytoreductive surgery achieving complete macroscopic resection (R0), followed by four cycles of cisplatin and etoposide (EP). Sixteen months after diagnosis, isolated intracranial recurrence with multiple brain metastases were successfully treated with radiotherapy. Twenty-one months after diagnosis, systemic recurrence involving multiple liver metastases and a spinal metastasis was treated with six cycles of EP re-challenge, resulting in a marked radiologic response and subsequent durable disease control. The patient remained alive without clinical evidence of disease progression at the latest follow-up, 104 months after diagnosis. Conclusions This case suggests that prolonged survival may be achievable in selected patients with advanced SCCOPT through aggressive multimodal treatment. Complete cytoreductive surgery, platinum-based chemotherapy, including EP re-challenge following a prolonged platinum-free interval and previous response to platinum-based chemotherapy, and timely local treatment of metastatic lesions may contribute to durable disease control.

title: HSV-Net: hybrid state-space and self-supervised vision fusion with progressive contour learning for CT pulmonary nodule segmentation.
abstract: Accurate voxel-level segmentation of pulmonary nodules on chest CT is needed for diameter and volume measurement, growth tracking, and quantitative assessment in lung cancer screening. The task remains difficult: nodules vary in attenuation, size, and contact with vessels or pleura, and clinically relevant morphology often lies in a thin, ambiguous margin. Existing systems commonly trade contour fidelity for speed-large prompt-driven foundation models can be accurate but slow, whereas compact CNN or SSM decoders are efficient yet tend to smooth spiculated and ground-glass borders. We propose HSV-Net (Hybrid State-space-Vision Network), a dual-stream 3D network that is prompt-free after nodule localization: an SSM3D stream provides whole-patch context with linear-complexity state-space blocks, and an OrthoLoRA stream adapts frozen DINOv2 features on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. A Hybrid Gated Mixer (HGM) fuses the two streams before FPN decoding, and Progressive Contour Learning (PCL) supervises overlap, signed-distance-field geometry, and uncertainty-weighted contour refinement. On a 10-patient QIN Lung CT/QIN-LungCT-Seg development subset ( n = 12 tumors; nested patient-level 5-fold CV), HSV-Net obtained the highest mean Dice (90.1% ± 1.0%; 95% CI [88.9, 91.3]) and Boundary F1 (86.3% ± 1.3%) among the compared methods on 128 × 128 × 64 patches, with a latency of 58 ms. A standard full-volume nnU-Net v2 baseline reached 88.6% ± 1.0% Dice on the same QIN folds, still below HSV-Net. On an independent LIDC-IDRI benchmark with expert volumetric consensus masks (186 patients/294 nodules; patient-level 5-fold CV within LIDC, not QIN→LIDC transfer), HSV-Net achieved 87.8% ± 1.1% Dice and 83.6% ± 1.3% Boundary F1, outperforming full-volume nnU-Net (87.1% ± 1.0% Dice). LUNA16 was retained only as a proxy size/localization check with diameter-matched spherical references, not as contour external validation.

title: Case Report: Diagnostic pitfalls and individualized surgical management of borderline and malignant phyllodes tumors: a three-case series.
abstract: Phyllodes tumors (PTs) can overlap with fibroadenomas clinically and radiologically, and incomplete preoperative characterization can alter surgical planning. We describe three women with borderline or malignant PTs who declined preoperative core needle biopsy; clinical underestimation of malignancy also contributed to proceeding directly to excision. Case 1, a 36-year-old woman with long-standing bilateral masses, had a 63-mm malignant PT with heterologous chondroid and osseous differentiation and osteoclast-like giant cells; two contralateral lesions were fibroadenomas. An involved margin prompted re-excision, with no residual tumor and a final closest histological margin of 20 mm, permitting breast conservation. Case 2, a 68-year-old woman with a 75-mm malignant PT, had mildly prominent ipsilateral axillary nodes on mammography but no abnormal enlargement on axillary ultrasonography. Following malignant PT interpretation on frozen section, wide local excision was converted to total mastectomy; sentinel lymph node biopsy was negative (0/3), and the closest margin was the deep margin at 20 mm. The patient declined postoperative radiotherapy. Case 3, a 53-year-old woman with previous right breast fibroadenoma excision, had a right borderline PT involving the inked margin and contralateral pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia. Re-excision approximately 2 cm beyond the previous surgical margin found no residual tumor. All three patients had satisfactory postoperative wound healing, with no reported complications or recurrence during the reported 6-month follow-up. These cases highlight the need for preoperative tissue diagnosis, attention to discrepant axillary imaging, individualized margin-directed surgery, and long-term surveillance.

title: Low CT-derived vertebral attenuation as a prognostic factor in hepatocellular carcinoma patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
abstract: Background Computed tomography (CT)-derived vertebral attenuation has been recognized as an indicator of prognosis for patients undergoing tumor removal, liver transplant, or transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) therapy, but similar research has not been reported in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study aims to explore the prognostic value of CT-derived vertebral attenuation in HCC patients treated with ICIs. Methods This retrospective study included HCC patients who received ICI treatment at Wuhan Union Hospital between July 2020 and March 2024. CT-derived vertebral attenuation was assessed by measuring mean Hounsfield unit (HU) values in the center of the first lumbar vertebra (L1) on non-contrast CT scans. Based on the optimal cutoff value derived from X-tile software, patients were classified into the CT-derived L1 attenuation-low group (≤100 HU) and the CT-derived L1 attenuation-high group (>100 HU). A comparison of the baseline characteristics of the two groups was made, followed by a propensity score matching (PSM) analysis to balance the variables. The objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were calculated for both groups, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox regression models were used to analyze overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Results The cohort consisted of 357 patients, divided into the L1 attenuation-low group (n = 112) and the L1 attenuation-high group (n = 245). Among all patients, 30.0% (107/357) achieved complete or partial response. After PSM analysis, both groups contained 91 patients. The L1 attenuation-low group had shorter OS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15-2.60; P = 0.008) and PFS (HR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.04-2.08; P = 0.030) than the L1 attenuation-high group. Conclusion CT-derived L1 attenuation can stratify survival risk for HCC patients undergoing ICI treatment.

title: Boundary-aware geometric Mamba network for breast tumor segmentation in 3D MRI.
abstract: Introduction Accurate breast tumor segmentation in Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging (DCE-MRI) is important for reliable diagnosis and treatment planning. However, complex tumor morphology, diverse spatial structures, and indistinct boundaries remain challenging for existing segmentation methods. Convolutional neural network-based methods have limited ability to model long-range dependencies, while Transformer-based methods often introduce substantial computational overhead. Although Mamba-based approaches provide an efficient alternative, conventional scanning strategies may suffer from directional bias and insufficiently capture three-dimensional structural variations. Methods We propose a Boundary-Aware Geometric Mamba Network (BAGMNet) for three-dimensional breast tumor segmentation. BAGMNet establishes a structural representation learning framework that combines geometric modeling, multi-directional state-space propagation, and boundary-aware feature refinement. The Geometric Mamba Encoder constructs complementary spatial representations through multiple geometric transformations, while the Multi-directional Selective State Space module enhances three-dimensional dependency modeling and alleviates the directional bias of conventional Mamba scanning. The Gated State-space Fusion and Adaptive Skip Recalibration modules further integrate local structural details with global contextual information and enhance boundary-related representations during feature propagation. Results Extensive experiments were conducted on the ISPY1 and Yunnan breast MRI datasets. BAGMNet achieved Dice scores of 70.34% and 79.14%, with average surface distances of 9.79 mm and 8.96 mm on the ISPY1 and Yunnan datasets, respectively. Compared with representative convolutional neural network-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based methods, BAGMNet achieved competitive performance in both regional segmentation accuracy and boundary localization.

title: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma manifesting as a solitary metastasis to the skeletal muscle of the scapular region accompanied by invasion of the adjacent bone while on PD-1 inhibitor maintenance therapy: a case report.
abstract: Cervical cancer is a common malignancy in women worldwide, with distant metastases frequently occurring in the lungs, liver, bones, and lymph nodes. However, this case report presents an extremely rare isolated metastasis to the left scapular region,specifically located between the supraspinatus and the trapezius muscles, in a patient with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma who developed this lesion during maintenance therapy with a programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) inhibitor after completing concurrent chemoradiotherapy. The clinical presentation of this metastatic lesion was atypical and posed a significant diagnostic challenge; however, multimodal imaging (MRI, PET/CT) and histopathological examination ultimately confirmed the diagnosis of cervical cancer metastasis. This finding underscores the necessity of maintaining a high level of vigilance for metastases in atypical sites, even in the era of immunotherapy. To manage this rare presentation, a multidisciplinary team developed a comprehensive treatment strategy centered on surgical resection, followed by postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy administered concurrently with chemotherapy and anti-angiogenic therapy(Q3W) consisting of paclitaxel 135 mg/m², cisplatin 50 mg/m², and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg. The patient remained recurrence-free at 13 months, suggesting that a multimodal combined local and systemic strategy may be feasible for selected patients with solitary muscle metastasis. This case not only adds to the clinical understanding of rare metastases in cervical cancer but also demonstrates that tumors can still metastasize to atypical sites under immunotherapy. These findings highlight the need for vigilance regarding metastases at atypical sites during immunotherapy. Any underlying mechanism-including immune editing and clonal evolution-remains speculative in the absence of paired molecular data and requires further validation.

title: Case Report: Improvement in neurologic symptoms and remission following non-operative management of locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck following cemiplimab therapy: two cases.
abstract: Background Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma is a common skin malignancy in aging populations. Surgical resection and radiotherapy can result in significant morbidity, as well as functional and cosmetic impairments. PD-1 antibodies are promising treatments for locally advanced disease. Case presentation Two elderly men (aged 71 and 73) with locoregionally advanced head and neck tumors received neoadjuvant treatment with cemiplimab (350 mg IV every 3 weeks). Both patients presented with neurologic symptoms concerning for nerve involvement; however, perineural spread could not be identified radiographically or by limited biopsies. Both patients achieved a significant clinical response after only four doses of cemiplimab. After 4 additional doses, both patients underwent elective treatment discontinuation and surgery and radiotherapy were omitted. With over 12-month follow-up, both patients remained free of recurrence. Treatment was well-tolerated with only Grade 1 pruritus. Conclusion These observations are promising and suggest the feasibility of response-adapted management following cemiplimab therapy in selected patients with advanced squamous cell skin cancer with resolution of neurologic symptoms. This approach may allow for omission of surgery and radiotherapy in selected patients. Further investigation to define appropriate candidates for this approach appears warranted.

title: Cone-beam CT-based synthetic CT generation for adaptive radiotherapy: methodological paradigms, clinical reliability assessment, and translation.
abstract: Synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generated from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) has important applications in quantitative imaging, dose recalculation, and adaptive radiotherapy. Deep learning has improved image quality and Hounsfield unit accuracy, but its reliability for patient-specific dosimetry and routine clinical use remains uncertain. This narrative review examines deep learning methods for generating sCT from treatment CBCT in photon and proton radiotherapy, with emphasis on data requirements, generalizability, structural fidelity, dosimetric accuracy, and clinical feasibility. The literature search was last updated on 30 July 2026. Current methods mainly include supervised regression, adversarial networks, registrationguided approaches, and diffusion models. Available evidence demonstrates encouraging image and dosimetric performance, although no method consistently performs best across anatomical sites, imaging systems, and treatment modalities. Most studies are based on proof of concept or single-center validation and show considerable heterogeneity in datasets, acquisition protocols, reference images, registration methods, and evaluation criteria. External validation, prospective assessment, failure detection, and quality assurance remain limited. Future studies should emphasize multicenter validation, standardized and modality-specific evaluation criteria, uncertainty assessment, and prospective workflow testing. More rigorous and clinically relevant evidence is needed to support the reliable use of sCT in patient-specific adaptive radiotherapy.

title: Case Report: Bilateral vestibulopathy associated with leptomeningeal metastasis.
abstract: Introduction Bilateral vestibulopathy (BVP) presents with oscillopsia, unsteadiness, and imbalance. Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is a rare and underrecognized cause of BVP, with direct infiltration of the vestibulocochlear nerves representing a potential mechanism of bilateral vestibular dysfunction. We report a case of LM-related BVP documented by quantitative video head impulse test (vHIT) of all six semicircular canals. Case report A 61-year-old man presented with a six-month history of dizziness, tinnitus, oscillopsia, imbalance, and bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. vHIT showed reduced vestibulo-ocular reflex gain in all six semicircular canals. Contrast-enhanced MRI revealed leptomeningeal enhancement and enhancement of both vestibulocochlear nerves. CSF showed elevated protein, lymphocytic pleocytosis, and malignant cells. Serum anti-AQP4 antibodies were positive (1:320), but no other paraneoplastic antibodies were identified. He was diagnosed with LM from lung adenocarcinoma causing secondary BVP via direct infiltration of the vestibulocochlear nerves. Dizziness improved with intrathecal chemotherapy. However, he died approximately one year after discharge. Conclusion BVP may be the initial presentation of LM. It underscores the necessity of considering rare etiologies in patients with unexplained BVP. Early recognition and targeted therapy may improve neurological outcomes, although overall prognosis remains limited in the setting of disseminated malignancy.

title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics for preoperative prediction of tumor budding grade in rectal cancer.
abstract: Background Tumor budding (TB) is a histopathological marker of tumor aggressiveness and an established prognostic factor in colorectal cancer. In rectal cancer, however, TB is usually assessed on biopsy or resection material, and a reliable result may not be available when preoperative management is being considered. Purpose To develop and internally validate a radiomics model for preoperative discrimination of low-grade versus intermediate/high-grade TB in patients with rectal cancer who proceed to upfront surgery without neoadjuvant treatment. The primary model was selected according to the highest repeated cross-validation AUC, with alternative feature sets and algorithms evaluated exploratorily. Methods This retrospective study included 139 patients with pathologically confirmed rectal cancer who had received no neoadjuvant treatment. TB was assessed on postoperative resection specimens. T1WI, T2WI, arterial-phase contrast-enhanced T1WI, and DWI were analyzed. Radiomics features were extracted from the tumor core, a combined tumor-plus-2-mm expansion, and an isolated external 2-mm ring. Seven feature sets and four machine-learning algorithms were evaluated; the primary model was selected according to the highest repeated cross-validation AUC. Feature filtering, imputation, selection, and scaling were performed within the training portion of every split. Model performance was estimated using stratified five-fold cross-validation repeated five times and patient-level out-of-fold (OOF) probabilities. Results The primary core-ROI Elastic Net model achieved a repeated cross-validation AUC of 0.825 (range 0.809-0.839 across repetitions), with PR-AUC 0.781, sensitivity 0.604, specificity 0.851, and Brier score 0.173. Its patient-level mean OOF AUC was 0.829 (2,000 paired bootstrap replicates; 95% CI, 0.755-0.896). At a probability threshold of 0.50, patient-level sensitivity was 0.607 and specificity was 0.867. In conditional paired bootstrap comparisons, the core model showed higher AUCs than the clinical, peritumoral-ring, clinical-plus-expanded, clinical-plus-core, and clinical-plus-core-plus-ring models (BH-adjusted P = 0.004-0.005). The difference versus the expanded ROI was smaller and did not reach statistical significance after adjustment (P = 0.052). Conclusion Multiparametric MRI radiomics features from the tumor core showed promising internal discrimination of low-grade versus intermediate/high-grade TB among patients who underwent upfront surgery without neoadjuvant treatment. The model may support preoperative TB risk stratification in this population, but external validation is required before clinical use.

title: Identifying a novel variant in ELOC (TCEB1)-mutant renal cell carcinoma: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Background ELOC ( TCEB1 )-mutant renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a recently recognized molecular subtype formally included the 2022 World Health Organization (WHO) classification. Although morphologically overlapping with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), it remains clinically and radiographically indistinguishable from other RCC subtypes. Because few cases have been reported, we describe an ELOC (TCEB1) -mutant RCC harboring a novel somatic TCEB1 variant, c.227A>G (p.Y76C). Case presentation A 52-year-old male presented with an incidentally discovered left renal mass on routine ultrasound. Computed tomography (CT) revealed a round, slightly hypodense lesion, approximately 14×15 mm, in the left kidney. Following retroperitoneal laparoscopic partial nephrectomy, pathological examination and immunohistochemistry (IHC) established the diagnosis, and next-generation sequencing (NGS) identified a novel ELOC ( TCEB1 ) mutation, c.227A>G (p.Y76C). Conclusion We report a rare ELOC (TCEB1) -mutant RCC carrying one novel missense variant, c.227A>G (p.Y76C), and a frameshift variant, c.171_172insCC (p.N58Pfs*48), in trans. This case adds a newly identified TCEB1 variant to the known spectrum of ELOC -mutant RCC and may help clinicians recognize this rare subtype. We also review the clinicopathological features, immunophenotype, molecular genetic alterations, differential diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of this entity.

title: Sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma of the urethra with an unusual right ventricular metastasis: a case report and review of literature.
abstract: Primary urethral carcinoma is an uncommon malignancy, and cardiac metastasis represents a rare event (~4% of cases) that poses significant diagnostic challenges, particularly in distinguishing myocardial tumors from intracavitary thrombi. Here we report a 54-year-old male diagnosed with cT4N0M0 sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma of the bulbar urethra. Following neoadjuvant dose-dense MVAC and radical surgery (ypT2N0, PD-L1 TPS 20%), adjuvant nivolumab was initiated. Six months after surgery, he developed locoregional recurrence and an expanding right ventricular mass. Multimodality cardiac imaging-including contrast echocardiography, FDG PET-CT, cardiac CT, and cardiac MRI-demonstrated a solid myocardial lesion with intracavitary extension and adjacent myocardial infiltration, considered highly suspicious for cardiac metastasis in the context of concurrent extracardiac progression. Histological confirmation was not obtained because of the procedural risk associated with extensive right ventricular involvement. Treatment with enfortumab vedotin yielded relative stability of the cardiac and pulmonary metastases; however, relentless locoregional progression occurred, illustrating interlesional response heterogeneity. The patient subsequently received palliative radiotherapy, and best supportive care before passing away 17 months after initial diagnosis. This case underscores the vital role of multimodal imaging in the differential diagnosis of cardiac masses in oncological patients with concurrent thromboembolic risk and its interpretation in conjunction with the disease course when pathology confirmation cannot be obtained. Furthermore, it highlights the therapeutic complexity and dismal prognosis associated with sarcomatoid histology in advanced urethral carcinoma.

title: Clinical and radiological features of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome in children: a retrospective study.
abstract: Background Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is an uncommon but critical neurological emergency in children. Data on Chinese pediatric cohorts remain limited. Objective To analyze the clinical features, imaging findings, and treatment of PRES in children to improve early diagnosis and management. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 10 children diagnosed with PRES from March 2016 to January 2025. Results The patients included 7 males and 3 females, aged 3-13 years (mean 7.5 years). The main underlying diseases were acute lymphoblastic leukemia (3 cases) and nephrotic syndrome (3 cases). Eight children (80%) had hypertension, 6 (60%) had hypoalbuminemia, and 8 received glucocorticoids or immunosuppressants. The main symptoms were headache, seizures, impaired consciousness, and visual disturbances. Cranial MRI showed symmetrical long T1 and long T2 signals in bilateral posterior cerebral white matter. After comprehensive treatment including antihypertensive, anticonvulsant, and dehydration therapy, all symptoms resolved and lesions disappeared on follow-up imaging without sequelae. Conclusion Pediatric PRES is an acute reversible disorder associated with hypertension and immunosuppressive therapy. Early MRI diagnosis and prompt intervention can significantly improve prognosis.

title: An ultrasound-based nomogram for predicting early neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate an ultrasound-based nomogram prediction model for the early diagnosis of neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC). Methods This is a retrospective cohort study. A total of 500 preterm infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of our hospital from January 2023 to June 2024 were enrolled. They were stratified by NEC status and randomly assigned to a development cohort and a validation cohort at a ratio of 7:3. According to whether NEC occurred, infants were further categorized into an NEC group and a non-NEC group. General clinical data, including gestational age and birth weight, were collected. Laboratory inflammatory markers included C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and interleukin-6 (IL-6). Ultrasound parameters included bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, gastric antral area, gastric antral peristalsis, and bowel wall blood perfusion. Logistic regression analysis was performed in the development cohort to identify independent risk factors and construct a nomogram prediction model. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit in the development cohort. The validation cohort was used to verify model performance. Results Univariate analysis in the development cohort showed that gestational age, birth weight, CRP, PCT, IL-6, bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, gastric antral area, gastric antral peristalsis, and bowel wall blood perfusion differed significantly between groups ( P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression further identified gestational age, CRP, PCT, IL-6, bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, bowel wall blood perfusion, gastric antral area, and gastric antral peristalsis as independent factors associated with early NEC ( P < 0.05). On this basis, a nomogram prediction model was established. The areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) in the development and validation cohorts were 0.88 and 0.85, respectively, indicating good discriminative ability. The optimal risk cut-off of 0.18 was determined by Youden index solely from the development cohort. At this fixed threshold, sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV were 82.4%, 81.2%, 51.4%, and 95.0% for the development cohort; the corresponding performance in the validation cohort was 77.2%, 76.0%, 43.8%, and 92.4%. Goodness-of-fit testing of the calibration curves showed chi-square = 1.235 and P = 0.998 in the development cohort, and chi-square = 1.642 and P = 0.995 in the validation cohort, suggesting favorable agreement between predicted probabilities and observed risks. Decision curve analysis showed that when the risk threshold was greater than 0.05, the nomogram provided significant clinical net benefit. Conclusion The nomogram prediction model constructed from inflammatory and multiparametric ultrasound indicators demonstrates favorable predictive performance for the early diagnosis of neonatal NEC. It may provide clinicians with a noninvasive and repeatable auxiliary diagnostic tool, facilitating early intervention for NEC and improving prognosis.

title: Liveborn trisomy 22: a case report.
abstract: Introduction : Trisomy 22 is identified in 2%-5% of spontaneous abortions across various populations, making it the second most common trisomy in spontaneous abortions. Liveborn patients with complete trisomy 22 are rare and present with variable clinical findings. Methods A detailed clinical report of a term female neonate with complete trisomy 22 was compiled after obtaining informed consent from her mother. Results The neonate was born via spontaneous vaginal delivery, and resuscitation included intubation after multiple attempts. She presented with multiple congenital anomalies, including a single umbilical artery, microcephaly, dysmorphic facial features, absent red reflex, corneal haze, irregular pupil, microcornea, imperforated anus with rectovestibular fistula, bilateral clinodactyly of the fifth digits, and bilateral distal and proximal transverse palmar creases running parallel to each other. An echocardiogram showed Tetralogy of Fallot and hypoplasia of the transverse aortic arch. Abdominal ultrasound revealed small kidneys. The electroencephalogram showed diffuse cerebral dysfunction. Head ultrasound indicated absence of the septum pellucidum. Additional complications included pneumothorax, metabolic disturbances, sepsis, and persistent thrombocytopenia. The neonate's condition deteriorated, leading to demise on the seventh day of life. Chromosome analysis confirmed 47,XX,+22. Discussion : This case report contributes to the limited literature on complete trisomy 22, highlighting its prognosis, clinical heterogeneity, and management challenges. The constellation of anomalies observed underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and adaptability in providing optimal care. By better understanding its clinical presentation, we hope to facilitate early recognition, appropriate management, and counseling.

title: CT habitat and peritumoral radiomics for predicting progression after repeat TACE in hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicenter study.
abstract: Background This study developed and validated an machine-learning-based radiomics model integrating tumor habitat radiomics, peritumoral radiomics, and clinical features to predict progression-free survival (PFS) following repeat transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 270 patients with HCC. Patients from Center 1 were assigned to training (n = 94) and internal validation (n = 41) cohorts, while Centers 2 (n = 82) and 3 (n = 53) served as external validation cohorts. Tumor habitats and 5-mm peritumoral regions were generated from contrast-enhanced CT images. Radiomics features were selected using univariate Cox and LASSO-Cox regression. A fusion model and HPC risk score were constructed by integrating selected radiomics signatures and clinical variables. Performance was assessed using time-dependent ROC, C-index, calibration, decision curve analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analyses. Results The optimal habitat cluster number was K = 2. Eleven habitat features, three peritumoral features, and alpha-fetoprotein were retained in the fusion model. The model achieved AUCs of 0.923, 0.921, and 0.897 for 3-, 6-, and 9-month progression-free survival in the training cohort, and 0.932, 0.863, and 0.916 in the internal validation cohort, respectively; all external AUCs exceeded 0.82. The fusion model showed higher C-index values than the clinical model across cohorts. High-risk patients had significantly shorter PFS than low-risk patients (all P < 0.001). Calibration and decision curve analyses demonstrated good agreement and clinical utility. Conclusion The CT-based fusion model and HPC risk score effectively predicted progression risk in HCC.

title: Functional assessment of experimental lymphedema: a focused mini-review of animal models and measurement methods.
abstract: Lymphedema is a chronic progressive disease resulting from impaired lymphatic transport. A wide range of animal models has been developed to study their pathophysiology, yet how well lymphatic function is measured within these models has received comparatively little attention. This mini-review organizes assessment methodologies into three complementary tiers: Tier 1 covers morphological and indirect outcome measures, including volumetric quantification and histological assessment; Tier 2 covers imaging-based approaches, including near-infrared fluorescence lymphangiography, radionuclide lymphoscintigraphy, and magnetic resonance lymphangiography; and Tier 3 covers direct physiological measurement of physical quantities such as intraluminal pressure, lymphatic conductance, and albumin transport rate. Surveying primary studies across seven species, we identify a recurring mismatch between the species most commonly used for lymphedema modeling and those in which the most informative measurements are technically accessible. The most accessible endpoints tend to reflect late-stage tissue consequences rather than early pumping dysfunction, imaging readouts remain constrained to relative dye intensity rather than true physical flow quantities, and direct physiological measurement is sparse and limited to single time points. For acquired secondary lymphedema, the rat hindlimb model paired with quantitative longitudinal imaging and vessel-level analysis offers a balanced platform, whereas genetic mouse models remain preferable for congenital disease and large-animal models for microsurgical and clinical-scale intervention studies; a cross-tabulation by species and measurement tier is provided to guide model and assessment selection.

title: CuFormer U-Net: a transformer-enhanced multi-task network for cucumber leaf disease detection and segmentation.
abstract: Cucumber foliar symptoms reduce functional leaf area and complicate greenhouse scouting. This study presents CuFormer U-Net, a Transformer-enhanced multi-task network for three-class image-level classification on the 3,754-image Kaggle benchmark (healthy, powdery mildew, and downy mildew) and binary visible-symptom segmentation on a separate 400-image greenhouse cohort (200 healthy and 200 affected leaves). The greenhouse annotations comprise 2,705 rectangles (1,741 color-abnormality and 964 tissue-damage instances); rectangle-seeded lesion masks were manually refined for the dense-prediction experiments. The reported fixed-split point estimates were 96.7% accuracy, 96.3% macro precision, 95.8% macro recall, and 96.0% macro F1 for classification, and 92.4% mean image-wise Dice, 83.1% macro IoU, 93.2% foreground precision, and 91.7% foreground recall for segmentation. The complete internal-validation ablation configuration reached 93.1% Dice and 87.3% IoU. The available experiment archive does not contain independent-seed reruns, per-image predictions for inferential testing, annotator-level masks, quantitative results for the separate 100-image greenhouse stress-test cohort, or reproducible hardware profiling. Accordingly, all between-model differences are interpreted descriptively, the external cohort is not presented as formal external validation, and robustness and deployment claims have been moderated. CuFormer U-Net provides a technically motivated basis for joint recognition and spatial characterization, but confirmatory multi-run and multi-site evaluation is required. boundary refinement, cucumber leaf disease, multi-task learning, plant disease, precision agriculture, semantic segmentation, vision transformer.

title: Comprehensive artificial intelligence-assisted mental health program for university students in China (CAMPUS): study protocol for a multi-center prospective cohort with planned embedded randomized intervention trials.
abstract: University students face a rising prevalence of depression, anxiety, insomnia, and suicidal ideation that exceeds the capacity of conventional, resource-constrained campus support services. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted screening tools have emerged, many have evaluated selected modalities or isolated prediction tasks, and their integration with prospectively evaluated intervention pathways remains limited. This protocol describes the Comprehensive Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Mental Health Program for University Students in China (CAMPUS), a multi-center research program comprising a five-year prospective cohort, eight planned embedded randomized controlled trials, and exploratory multimodal AI and multi-omics studies across seven Chinese universities. Longitudinal cohort enrolment commenced at Henan Medical University in September 2025 and is planned to expand across seven participating universities. Multidimensional screening integrates psychological self-report (PHQ-9, GAD-7, ISI, BSI-CV, and others), physiological measurements (EEG, MRI, fNIRS, HRV, eye tracking, facial-expression analysis, ERP, voice acoustics), and an exploratory biospecimen component for multi-omics profiling, potentially including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and microbiome analyses, subject to the finalization and approval of layer-specific protocols. Students identified through cohort screening as potentially eligible for an intervention trial will undergo trial-specific eligibility assessment. Those who meet the eligibility criteria and provide trial-specific informed consent will be individually randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or its comparator within one of eight separate two-arm, multi-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trials. A Transformer-based multimodal AI framework with SHAP-based feature attribution will be developed and internally evaluated for questionnaire-defined risk stratification and exploratory treatment-response prediction. The initial Henan Medical University cohort recruitment and university-student mental-health assessment were approved by the Ethics Review Committee of Henan Medical University (XYLL-20250484), and written informed consent is obtained from participants before enrolment. Each additional participating center will obtain local ethics approval before study activation. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, scientific conferences, and policy briefs, providing evidence that may inform the design and prospective evaluation of youth mental-health programs in other university settings. Clinical trial registration The two clinical trials were registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR). The registration details and URLs are as follows: ChiCTR2500113527: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=298271; ChiCTR2500113613: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=298268.

title: Prediction of early developmental status using neonatal structural MRI radiomics.
abstract: Background Early identification of developmental vulnerability in high-risk neonates remains challenging because standardized developmental assessments, such as the Griffiths Development Scales-Chinese (GDS-C), are typically performed months after birth and cannot provide objective information during the neonatal period. Structural MRI provides quantitative information regarding neonatal brain development, and radiomics may capture imaging patterns beyond conventional visual assessment. This study aimed to investigate whether neonatal structural MRI radiomics combined with clinical variables could provide early estimates of developmental status during infancy. Methods This prospective cohort study included 93 neonates recruited from Xiamen Children's Hospital between November 2022 and August 2025. All participants underwent non-sedated brain MRI on a 3.0-T scanner during the neonatal period, and radiomic features were extracted from structural MRI. MRI radiomic features were integrated with prespecified clinical variables to develop machine learning models for estimating the Griffiths Development Scales-Chinese (GDS-C) general quotient (GQ) obtained during follow-up. Model development and performance evaluation were performed using a nested cross-validation framework involving all participants. A two-level stacking framework integrating predictions from ten regression algorithms was developed, and predictive performance was evaluated using the coefficient of determination (R 2 ), root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute error (MAE). Results Of the 93 neonates, 36 (38.7%) were female and 62 (66.7%) were preterm. The mean (SD) corrected age at GDS-C assessment was 7.13 (5.11) months, with a mean (SD) general quotient of 104.11 (19.77). The clinical-radiomics stacking model demonstrated moderate predictive performance under nested cross-validation, achieving an RMSE of 17.12, an MAE of 13.55, and an R 2 of 0.24. Compared with the clinical-only stacking model, incorporation of MRI radiomic features improved prediction performance. Exploratory analyses of GDS-C subdomains and hierarchical stacking approaches were additionally performed and should be interpreted as preliminary findings. Conclusions Neonatal MRI radiomics combined with clinical variables may provide complementary information for estimating developmental status during infancy among high-risk neonates undergoing clinically indicated MRI. These findings support the potential of quantitative imaging approaches as adjunctive tools for early developmental surveillance rather than replacements for standardized assessments. Larger multicenter studies with longitudinal follow-up are required to further evaluate clinical utility.

title: Deep learning prediction of overall survival in glioblastoma patients using pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data.
abstract: Purpose Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits variable treatment response and patients shown a median survival of 15 months. A major challenge lies in the difficulty of reliably assessing treatment response at an early stage, as it can usually only be evaluated on anatomical MRI performed up to three months after the start of treatment, when early interpretation may be complicated by the risk of pseudoprogression. Accurately predicting short-term and long-term survivors before radiotherapy and chemotherapy is therefore crucial. The objective of this study is to develop an AI model designed to predict survival outcomes based exclusively on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data. Material and methods A total of 1,575 retrospective T1-Gd brain images were obtained from 175 patients treated for GBM between 2018 and 2023. A ResNet-51Q model pretrained on ImageNet was fine-tuned on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI using transfer learning. To incorporate clinical data, deep hybrid learning (DHL) models were trained. Results At patient-level, the AI model achieved 81.08% (CI 95%: 67.57-91.89), 68.42% (CI 95%: 47.06-88.89) and 94.44% (CI 95%: 81.82-1.00) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively, for the classification of short-term and long-term survivors using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI. At patient-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 87.18% (CI 95%: 76.92- 97.44), 87.18% (CI 95%: 76.68-96.97), and 93.59% (CI 95%: 88.03-98.41) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively. In comparison at slice-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 81.77% (CI 95%: 70.66-91.45), 81.77% (CI 95%: 71.07-91.33), and 90.88% (CI 95%: 85.25-95.74) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively. In comparison the DHL model with clinical data achieved an accuracy of 84.62% (CI 95%: 71.79-94.87), a sensitivity of 84.62% (CI 95%: 72.54-95.24) and a specificity of 92.31% (CI 95%: 86.07-97.53) and 76.32% (CI 95%: 63.16-89.47), 76.11% (CI 95%: 61.63-88.75) and 92.06% (CI 95%: 87.51-96.23) for four overall survival classification. For multiclass tasks, metrics were calculated using a macro-averaged approach. Conclusion The combination of pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data using the DHL model for early survival prediction; however, adding clinical variables yielded comparable prognostic performance rather than a demonstrable enhancement over imaging features alone. The use of AI models to predict survival outcome in GBM from pre-chemoradiotherapy data may support pre-chemoradiotherapy prognostic stratification.

title: Q-rung orthopair fuzzy framework for multimodal MRI image fusion and U-Net-based segmentation for brain tumor detection.
abstract: Medical image analysis is a significant research domain in contemporary healthcare systems, which helps to accurately diagnose diseases and support clinical decision-making. This domain consists of important operations, including image enhancement, fusion, segmentation, morphological processing, and denoising, which assist in the effective understanding of complex biomedical information. Multimodal image fusion and segmentation are particularly important among these processes, as they enable the integration of complementary diagnostic information and the clear interpretation of clinically meaningful structures. However, medical images often consist of uncertainty, noise, and incomplete pixel information, creating major challenges for conventional analytical techniques. To address these challenges, the present study introduces a q-rung orthopair fuzzy set (qROFS)-based framework for multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) fusion, subsequently a U-Net-based segmentation architecture for brain tumor detection. To effectively handle uncertainty and preserve important image information, the fusion strategy is designed based on q-rung orthopair fuzzy Hamacher t-norm and t-conorm operators to integrate complementary information in four different MRI modalities, including T1, T1ce, T2, and Flair. The resultant fused images are subsequently processed through a U-Net architecture to obtain precise tumor segmentation. Experiments conducted on the BraTS 2020 benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Across the four MRI modalities (T1, T1ce, T2, and Flair), the proposed fusion framework attains the best quantitative performance when compared to state-of-the-art methods with an SSIM of 0.9271, an MSSIM of 0.9481, a PSNR of 24.7130 dB, a low AMBE of 6.6779, a Correlation coefficient of 0.9583, an MI of 1.4097, and a UQI of 0.9767. A comparative evaluation with existing fuzzy set-based fusion models further assures the effectiveness of the proposed qROFS-based framework for multimodal MRI image fusion. Furthermore, the U-Net-based segmentation model achieves excellent performance, with an accuracy of 98.96%, a precision of 98.95%, a sensitivity of 98.94%, and a specificity of 99.65%.

title: Prospective validation of multimodal risk stratification using clinical and quantitative imaging features for 12-month outcomes after minimally invasive surgery for lumbar disc herniation.
abstract: Background Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) is a common spinal disorder leading to chronic low back pain and radiating leg pain. Minimally invasive surgery is the preferred treatment, but postoperative recovery varies significantly, making accurate preoperative prognosis prediction a challenge. Methods This study developed and prospectively validated a multimodal risk-stratification framework integrating structured clinical variables, conventional imaging parameters, CT/MRI radiomics, and high-dimensional image-derived features. A total of 773 patients were analyzed, including 665 patients in the retrospective development cohort and 108 patients in an independent prospective validation cohort. The retrospective cohort was divided into a training cohort ( n = 532) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 133). Feature selection, parameter optimization, and classification-threshold determination were performed exclusively within the training cohort, and the finalized framework was subsequently evaluated in the internal and prospective validation cohorts. Results The integrated multimodal approach achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.937 (95% CI, 0.900-0.975) and a PR-AUC of 0.849 in the internal validation cohort, and an ROC-AUC of 0.976 (95% CI, 0.951-1.000) and a PR-AUC of 0.941 in the prospective validation cohort. Its discrimination was comparable to that achieved using structured clinical and conventional imaging information alone and was higher than that of isolated quantitative imaging approaches. At the prespecified training-derived classification threshold of 0.318, sensitivity, specificity, and balanced accuracy in the prospective cohort were 85.3%, 95.9%, and 90.6%, respectively. Calibration analysis demonstrated residual probability miscalibration despite strong discrimination, although training-derived logistic recalibration improved the Brier score. Conclusion Multimodal integration of clinical and quantitative imaging information demonstrated strong discrimination for 12-month postoperative outcome stratification in both internal and prospective validation cohorts. However, the incremental discriminative value beyond structured clinical and conventional imaging information was limited, and residual miscalibration remained in the prospective cohort. Further multicenter validation, standardized quantitative imaging workflows, and calibration assessment are warranted before clinical translation.

title: Temporal phase coverage and patient cohort size in deep learning-based cardiac cine computed tomography angiography segmentation.
abstract: Background Annotating all phases of cine computed tomography angiography (CTA) is burdensome. We evaluated how temporal phase coverage and patient cohort size affect deep learning-based cardiac segmentation. Methods Twelve 3D U-Net models were trained using a 110-patient single-phase CTA dataset or a 20-patient, 20-phase cine CTA dataset. Phase-coverage ablations used one, two, or 20 phases; patient-count ablations were performed within both datasets. One cine patient was used for validation and four independent patients were used for testing. Five cardiac structures were evaluated using Dice and the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95). Phase-wise and patient-level Dice consistency and structure-specific volumetric variability within and between subjects were assessed. Results Full cine training produced higher overall Dice (0.89 vs. 0.87) and lower overall HD95 (4.87 vs. 9.78 mm) than the single-phase reference (both p < 0.05). Right ventricular (RV) Dice was higher (0.91 vs. 0.84) and HD95 was lower (5.16 vs. 22.75 mm; both p < 0.05). The two-phase model achieved an overall Dice of 0.88 and an overall HD95 of 7.85 mm; neither metric differed significantly from the single-phase reference. HD95 generally increased with smaller cohorts, and both metrics deteriorated markedly in the five-patient configurations. Full cine training showed flatter phase-wise Dice profiles and lower across-phase variability. Between-subject volume differences exceeded phase-related within-subject differences for all structures (all p < 0.05). Conclusion In this cross-cohort comparison, full cine training showed higher overall Dice, lower overall HD95, and greater phase-wise consistency than single-phase training. The evaluated two-phase configuration may inform annotation-efficient cine CTA dataset design, but broader validation is needed.

title: Automated Nuchal Translucency analysis for early prenatal risk stratification.
abstract: Nuchal Translucency (NT) is a measurement taken from ultrasound images described as the gathering of fluid behind the fetus's neck, during 11-13 weeks. Increased Nuchal Translucency can lead to high risk of chromosomal abnormalities like Down Syndrome. The existing AI model may struggle to detect the subtle difference due to low resolution fetal movement, which can lead to errors in measurements and diagnosis. In addition, traditional NT measurement methods rely heavily on manual caliper placement, making the process operator-dependent and reducing consistency and automation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an Enhanced Multi-Scale Spatial Temporal Graph Attention Network (EMSSTGAN) to predict the risk of chromosomal abnormalities in NT. Initially, the input images of NT are pre-processed using feature refinement attention network (FRANet) for denoising and Multi-Scale Attention Retinex Network (MARN) for contrast enhancement. NT detection is then performed by localizing the nuchal translucency region using bounding box annotations, followed by U-Net-based segmentation for precise extraction of the NT area. The Active Contour Model (ACM) is subsequently applied to measure the NT thickness based on boundary geometry. The thickness when compared with threshold values is used to identify the risk of chromosomal abnormalities as low, medium and high. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 98.15%, an error of 1.85%, and a FDR of 2.44%, respectively.

title: Diffusion-augmented contrastive learning for diabetic retinopathy severity classification.
abstract: Automated diabetic retinopathy (DR) severity classification faces persistent challenges from limited annotated datasets, severe class imbalance across the five-level International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy (ICDR) scale, and domain shift between imaging environments. This paper presents an integrated deep learning framework that extends our earlier Fused Ensemble Convolutional Inception Network (93.2% accuracy) through three complementary innovations. First, a class-conditional latent denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) generates anatomically realistic synthetic fundus images for underrepresented DR severity levels, addressing data scarcity and class imbalance simultaneously. Second, a SimCLR contrastive self-supervised pre-training protocol, applied to the combined real-and-synthetic corpus, learns discriminative retinal representations prior to supervised fine-tuning. Third, a five-model ensemble (EfficientNet-B3, ResNet-50, VGG16, VGG19, and DenseNet-121) fused via a learned Pattern-Net achieves improved generalization through architectural diversity. Evaluated on the APTOS 2019 dataset under 5-fold stratified cross-validation, the integrated framework achieves 95.1% accuracy, 0.928 quadratic weighted kappa (QWK), 0.91 F1-score, and 0.97 AUC. Class-wise improvements over the EfficientNet-B3 baseline reach +23.8 percentage points for Severe DR (61.8 → 85.6%) and +17.7 for Mild DR (71.2 → 88.9%). Independent zero-shot validation on EyePACS yields 78.4% accuracy, 0.809 QWK, 0.738 macro F1, and 0.887 macro AUC, quantifying the expected performance reduction under domain shift. Fold-level variability and paired out-of-fold statistical analyses are additionally reported, and Grad-CAM visualization is included for qualitative model interpretability. These results demonstrate the synergistic benefit of generative augmentation with self-supervised representation learning for imbalanced medical image classification, with implications for scalable automated DR screening in resource-limited settings.

title: Mammography datasets and artificial intelligence for breast cancer detection: challenges, bias, and future directions.
abstract: Background Breast cancer is still one of the main causes of death in women from cancer worldwide, and early detection is crucial. Mammography is the primary imaging modality for breast cancer screening and recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have significantly enhanced automated breast cancer detection. This review takes a data-centered approach, examining key characteristics of public datasets, the contributions of mammography data to AI for breast cancer detection, and the implications for clinical generalizability. This review, however, takes a data-centered approach, critically analyzing characteristics of publicly available mammography datasets, and the role of mammography data to the development, performance and clinical generalization of AI models for the detection of breast cancer. The datasets are compared on the following aspects: dataset size, quality of the annotations, imaging modality, clinical metadata, dataset accessibility and demographic diversity. Analysis reveals that the quality, diversity and representativeness of the data used are critical for the performance and generalizability of AI models, ranging from the traditional machine learning era to the current era of deep learning, transformer-based systems, multimodal learning, explainable AI and privacy-preserving learning. Conclusion The results show that, apart from the development of AI model architectures, it is a necessity to have standardized, diverse and clinically representative datasets to make further progress in AI-assisted mammography. The review emphasizes the importance of establishing a comprehensive benchmark dataset for mammography that is large and diverse to enhance reproducibility, to fairly evaluate models, and to develop strong, clinically viable AI systems for breast cancer detection.

title: Beyond diagnostic accuracy: navigating the artificial intelligence data tsunami toward value-based implementation in gastroenterology.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy has evolved from its early application in simple edge detection to highly sophisticated technologies designed to improve detection of neoplastic and preneoplastic lesions and support clinical decision-making. However, this rapid technological evolution has generated a " data tsunami " or " datanami ": an overwhelming and continuously expanding volume of information that, frequently, exceeds the ability of clinicians and patients to process, interpret, and apply it effectively. Substantial investments in AI have been driven by expectations of improved efficiency and reduced healthcare costs. Nevertheless, the metrics used to justify the adoption of AI-assisted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies remain inadequately standardized, leaving the true cost-effectiveness of these technologies uncertain. Current AI research in gastroenterology has primarily focused on improving diagnostic performance rather than evaluating long-term clinical outcomes or economic value. To address this limitation, investigators employ stochastic microsimulation models, which simulate individual patient trajectories and enable more robust assessments of cost-effectiveness. As the field progresses from AI to extended intelligence and, ultimately, intelligent assistance, the role of humans becomes increasingly central. Rather than replacing clinical judgment, AI should augment human expertise, with healthcare professionals serving as the critical link between technological innovation and meaningful clinical benefit. This review examines whether AI applications in GI diseases can be implemented cost-effectively in routine clinical practice for diagnosis and treatment. It further explores the indispensable human dimension of AI adoption, emphasizing accountability, reliability, ethical oversight, and responsible implementation as essential safeguards for current and future clinical applications.

title: Segmentation of ovarian cancer tumors from CT images based on a two-stage neural network fusion system.
abstract: The detection of ovarian cancer using computed tomography images is making rapid progress, combining the strengths of different neural networks within a complex ensemble, a more effective model can be created to support medical decision-making in ovarian cancer cases. Various neural networks and ensemble models were tested on the TCGA OV database. Tumor regions were segmented using computer-assisted annotation masks, while molecular subtype labels were assigned at the patient level based on TCGA genomic classifications and mapped to tumors. As the main novelty, the proposed method involves a two-stage fusion system. The first stage combines several neural networks into four ensembles to capture diverse features, and the second stage integrates these results into a global system to enhance segmentation accuracy. The selected models demonstrated strong segmentation performance within the investigated experimental setting and were subsequently integrated into the proposed two-stage fusion framework. The neural networks for the first stage are Attention U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and ViT. The results show that the proposed two-stage fusion system achieved higher observed segmentation performance than the evaluated individual neural networks and first-stage ensemble configurations within the present TCGA-OV experimental setting. Across the five evaluated classes, the Global System achieved an average F1 score of 93.53%, recall of 93.38%, and precision of 93.68%, supporting the technical feasibility of the proposed two-stage fusion approach for ovarian tumor segmentation within the investigated dataset.

title: The "Sandwich" technique using a lateral locking plate and intramedullary reconstruction plate with bone cement for osteoporotic proximal humerus fractures: a case series.
abstract: Introduction Although lateral locking plate fixation is widely used for displaced proximal humerus fractures, fixation failure remains a major concern in elderly osteoporotic patients, particularly when medial column defects are present. Poor cancellous bone quality reduces screw purchase, while medial comminution and metaphyseal bone voids weaken the ability of the proximal humerus to resist varus and axial loading. Existing augmentation methods address only part of this problem. Fibular strut allografts can provide intramedullary and medial support but may be limited by graft availability, size matching, cost, and technical complexity, and they do not directly reinforce the screw-bone interface of all proximal screws. Cement augmentation can improve screw purchase, but cement alone does not create a defined intramedullary support structure or reconstruct medial column bone defects. Therefore, a composite fixation strategy is needed to simultaneously provide lateral fixation, intramedullary support, medial column stability, enhanced screw purchase, and bone defect reconstruction. To address this clinical gap, we developed the "Sandwich" technique, which combines a lateral locking plate, an intramedullary reconstruction plate, PMMA bone cement, and allogeneic cancellous bone graft to create a multidirectional support construct. Methods Five patients with osteoporotic proximal humerus fractures and medial column defects were treated using the "Sandwich" technique. This construct consisted of a lateral locking plate, an intramedullary reconstruction plate, PMMA bone cement, and allogeneic cancellous bone graft. The lateral locking plate provided lateral fixation, whereas the intramedullary reconstruction plate provided internal structural support. PMMA bone cement was placed between the two plates to reinforce screw purchase and construct stability, and allogeneic cancellous bone graft was used to fill the residual metaphyseal and medial column defects. Results The mean operative time was 123.0 ± 16.1 min, with an average blood loss of 206.0 ± 85.3 mL, hospital stay of 8.4 ± 1.1 days, and mean hospitalization cost of 56,258.4 ± 6,152.1 CNY. At 12 months postoperatively, all fractures achieved radiographic union without loss of reduction, screw penetration, or varus collapse. The mean CMS was 87.0 ± 6.0 and the mean Neer score was 86.0 ± 6.1. No cases of avascular necrosis or fixation failure were observed. Conclusion The "Sandwich" technique provides strong medial and intramedullary support, improves screw fixation, and enhances overall biomechanical stability in osteoporotic proximal humerus fractures. It achieved excellent healing and functional recovery with minimal complications, representing a promising surgical alternative to traditional fibular graft-assisted fixation.

title: Jejunal intussusception following distal gastrectomy with Billroth I anastomosis: a case report.
abstract: A 41-year-old male patient presented with acute persistent abdominal pain for 4 h and was admitted to our hospital in October 2023. The patient had a height of 178 cm and a weight of 55 kg, with a precisely calculated body mass index (BMI) of 17.4 kg/m² and a body surface area of 1.73 m². He was diagnosed with acute gastric perforation and underwent emergency distal gastrectomy combined with Billroth I gastroduodenal anastomosis and intraoperative jejunal feeding tube placement. On postoperative day (POD) 19, the patient developed aggravated abdominal distension and paroxysmal abdominal pain without fever, vomiting, or diarrhea. Laboratory tests showed slightly elevated inflammatory markers and normal serum lactate, while abdominal computed tomography (CT) revealed typical intestinal intussusception and partial intestinal obstruction. Emergency re-laparotomy confirmed antegrade jejunojejunal intussusception located approximately 20 cm distal to the Treitz ligament, with an intussusception length of approximately 40 cm. Manual reduction was successfully performed without intestinal resection or intraoperative complications. The patient achieved uneventful gastrointestinal function recovery and was discharged on POD 12 after reoperation. No recurrence of intussusception was observed during 6 months of outpatient follow-up. This study reports a rare case of late-onset antegrade jejunojejunal intussusception following Billroth I gastrectomy. Combined effects of low BMI-related loose mesentery, intra-abdominal postoperative adhesions, and indwelling jejunal feeding tube were identified as potential associative risk factors rather than definitive causal factors. We aim to summarize the clinical characteristics, diagnostic strategies, and standardized prevention and treatment protocols of this rare postoperative complication to supplement relevant clinical evidence.

title: When should a laparoscopic cholecystectomy be performed after ERCP for common bile duct stones combined with gallbladder stones? A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Background Gallstones combined with common bile duct stones are a common disease in biliary surgery. At present, for gallbladder stones with common bile duct stones, the globally recognized standard treatment is a step-by-step treatment of "endoscopy combined with surgery". First, more urgent and potentially life-threatening bile duct stones are treated, and then gallbladder stones are treated. However, after the common bile duct stones are successfully removed by ERCP, how long should laparoscopic cholecystectomy be performed at intervals? There is a dispute between "early" (defined as within 72 h after ERCP) and "delayed" (defined as 72 h after ERCP). The conclusion is not yet uniform. Objective To systematically analyze the efficacy and safety of early LC and delayed LC in patients with gallstones and common bile duct stones after ERCP, to provide current high-level evidence-based medical evidence for clinical decision-making, to help clinicians optimize the diagnosis and treatment process, to reduce the occurrence of adverse complications caused by treatment. Method PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, and other databases were searched to collect randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing early LC and delayed LC after ERCP from inception to December 2025. Two reviewers independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias of included studies using the Cochrane ROB evaluation tool. The RevMan 5.4 software was used to analyze the outcomes of each group. Unlike previous meta-analyses, this study only included randomized controlled trials and incorporated the latest ones. Moreover, the quality of each outcome indicator was evaluated using the GRADE method. Result This meta-analysis included 7 randomized controlled trials involving 593 patients (296 in the early LC group and 297 in the delayed LC group). Compared with the delayed LC group, the early LC group was associated with a significantly lower rate of conversion to open surgery ( RR = 0.35, 95 % CI : 0.17-0.68, P = 0.002), shorter operation time ( MD = -14.37 min, 95 % CI : -28.22 to -0.51, P = 0.04), shorter postoperative hospital stay ( MD = -0.81 days, 95 % CI : -1.20 to -0.42, P < 0.0001), and lower incidence of incision infection (RR = 0.21, 95 % CI : 0.07-0.61, P = 0.004). No significant difference was observed between the two groups in the incidence of bile leakage ( RD = -0.04, 95 % CI : -0.12-0.04, P = 0.30). Conclusion In conclusion, the available RCT evidence suggests that early LC following successful ERCP may provide clinical advantages over delayed LC, including lower conversion and infection rates and shorter operative and postoperative hospital stay. However, because of outcome-level heterogeneity, the limited number of included trials, and few bile-leakage events, these findings should be interpreted with caution and further verified in larger well-designed RCTs. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261395564, PROSPERO CRD420261395564.

title: Free flap selection strategies and advances in facial soft tissue defect reconstruction.
abstract: Reconstruction of facial soft tissue defects remains a demanding task in plastic, reconstructive, and head and neck surgery because the face combines aesthetic units with essential functions such as oral competence, speech, swallowing, breathing, eyelid protection, and facial expression. The severity, depth, and composition of the defect are the primary determinants of flap selection, especially when defects extend beyond skin and subcutaneous tissue to expose the oral cavity, pharynx, nasal cavity, skull base, or critical structures. This narrative review summarizes evidence and technical progress regarding free flap selection for facial soft tissue reconstruction. Literature was identified through PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using combinations of the terms "facial soft tissue defect," "free flap," "perforator flap," and "virtual surgical planning." Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical series, and studies published between 2019 and 2026, while classic microsurgical reports were retained when foundational. Free flap choice should be guided by an integrative three-dimensional matrix: defect characteristics×patient profile×institutional resources. The anterolateral thigh flap remains a workhorse for moderate to large defects because of its thickness, long pedicle, availability of fascia lata, and nerve harvest. The radial forearm free flap remains valuable for thin and pliable resurfacing of the lips, eyelids, nasal lining, and oral lining. The deep inferior epigastric perforator flap is useful for large-volume contour restoration. Additional soft tissue options-including the lateral arm, parascapular, and medial sural artery perforator flaps-should be considered when color match, donor-site morbidity, or body habitus makes traditional workhorse flaps suboptimal. Facial soft tissue reconstruction requires not only flap survival but also restoration of contour, sensation, oral competence, facial animation, donor-site acceptability, and patient-reported quality of life. Mature technologies such as CTA, selective ultrasound, virtual surgical planning, intraoperative indocyanine green angiography, and structured postoperative monitoring should be distinguished from evolving tools such as augmented reality, artificial intelligence decision support, robotic-assisted anastomosis, artificial vascular conduits, and allogeneic or xenogeneic transplantation. Future research should focus on multicenter registries, standardized outcome measures, cost-effectiveness analyses, and externally validated decision-support models.

title: Clinical outcomes of one-hole split endoscope versus unilateral biportal endoscopy for lumbar degenerative diseases.
abstract: Objective This study aims to compare the clinical efficacy and safety of the novel One-hole Split Endoscope (OSE) technique with the established Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy (UBE) technique for the treatment of lumbar degenerative diseases (LDD). Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted from January 2021 to December 2023, involving 116 patients with LDD. Patients were allocated to either the OSE group ( n = 60) or the UBE group ( n = 56). Perioperative outcomes (operative time, blood loss, hospital stay, incision length), clinical scores (VAS for back/leg pain, ODI), and complication rates were systematically compared between the two groups. Results Both groups demonstrated significant clinical improvement postoperatively. The OSE procedure required a longer operative time (135.8 ± 12.6 min vs. 102.4 ± 10.9 min, P < 0.001). However, the OSE group demonstrated advantages in several key perioperative metrics, including a significantly shorter hospital stay (3.9 ± 0.8 days vs. 5.4 ± 1.1 days, P < 0.001) and a smaller incision length (1.5 ± 0.2 cm vs. 2.7 ± 0.3 cm, P < 0.001). Intraoperative blood loss was minimal and comparable between the two groups ( P > 0.05). The OSE group also showed earlier and superior functional recovery, evidenced by significantly lower ODI scores at 1-week, 1-month, and final follow-up ( P < 0.05), whereas no significant differences were found in postoperative pain VAS scores or in the overall complication rate ( P = 0.127). Conclusion Both OSE and UBE techniques are effective and safe for treating LDD. Despite a longer operative time, the OSE technique offers distinct advantages in minimizing surgical trauma, promoting faster recovery, and achieving better early functional outcomes. OSE represents a valuable and innovative minimally invasive option in the spine surgeon's arsenal.
