title: Malignant Tracheal Stenosis: A Narrative Review of Current Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approaches.
abstract: Background: Malignant tracheal stenosis (MTS) is a rare, life-threatening condition caused by primary tracheal tumor, mainly adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), and more rarely other primary neoplasms such as lymphomas, or local extension/metastasis from adjacent malignancies (thyroid, esophageal, lung, or mediastinal cancers). Accounting for <0.1% of respiratory tumors, MTS presents with progressive respiratory failure, requiring urgent multidisciplinary care involving thoracic surgery, interventional pulmonology, oncology, and intensive care. Diagnosis relies on clinical evaluation, advanced imaging and endoscopy. Bronchoscopy (BC) remains the best investigation for direct visualization and biopsy or performing therapeutic maneuvers. Prognosis depends on histology, local extent, and achieving R0 resection. Tracheal resection with primary anastomosis remains the curative standard for resectable cases. Interventional procedures (debulking, laser, cryotherapy, stenting) are essential for palliative management and acute stabilization. Methods: A structured (non-systematic) search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science (1965-2025) was performed using MeSH/Emtree terms and free-text keywords. Studies were included if they evaluated adult patients with malignant central airway stenosis, primary tracheal tumors, or secondary invasion undergoing surgical, bronchoscopic, or multimodal interventions, including ECMO support. Results: Malignant tracheal stenosis (MTS)-predominantly adenoid cystic and squamous cell carcinomas-imposes a critical clinical burden despite its low incidence. Complete surgical resection with negative margins remains the curative treatment for resectable disease. In unresectable cases, multimodal palliative interventions (stenting, laser/electrocautery ablation, and mechanical debulking) provide rapid airway restoration and quality-of-life improvements, whereas ECMO is an established rescue or adjunctive support strategy in selected critical airway procedures performed in experienced centers. Three-dimensional bioprinting and tissue-engineered reconstruction remain experimental or early clinical, and bioresorbable stents and artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools remain investigational; none is currently part of routine MTS management. Conclusions: R0 resection for appropriately selected resectable disease and interventional airway management for unresectable symptomatic disease are the best-supported strategies, although the evidence derives mainly from retrospective series from specialized centers. Emerging technologies require prospective validation before clinical adoption. Management should be individualized, multidisciplinary and centralized in experienced airway centers.

title: Macular Holes Secondary to Macular Telangiectasia Type 2: Pathogenesis, Clinical Features, Imaging and Surgical Management.
abstract: Full-thickness macular holes (FTMHs) are a rare but recognized complication of macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel2). Unlike idiopathic FTMHs, which are primarily driven by vitreofoveal traction, MacTel2-associated holes appear to arise predominantly from progressive neurodegenerative changes. Müller cell dysfunction, intraretinal cavitation, and outer retinal atrophy progressively compromise foveal architecture, ultimately predisposing to tissue dehiscence and full-thickness defects. Although vitreofoveal traction may contribute in individual cases, it is unlikely to be the principal mechanism in most affected eyes. Surgical treatment remains challenging, as current evidence is limited to case reports and small case series. Internal limiting membrane (ILM) flap techniques and, in selected cases, retinal graft or amniotic membrane transplant procedures have yielded encouraging anatomical closure rates, whereas conventional ILM peeling alone appears less predictable. Importantly, restoration of foveal continuity does not necessarily result in meaningful visual improvement, particularly in eyes with established photoreceptor and outer retinal damage. The durability of anatomical repair may be further compromised by continued disease progression. Persistent Müller cell dysfunction, intraretinal cavitation, and progressive outer retinal atrophy can undermine foveal support and lead to recurrent architectural disruption, including reopening of a previously closed hole. Although late recurrence has been documented, its incidence and determinants remain poorly defined because of the limited size and heterogeneity of the available literature. Visual prognosis appears to be determined largely by the amount of structurally and functionally viable retinal tissue remaining at the time of intervention. Smaller defects, less extensive cavitation, and preservation of the external limiting membrane and ellipsoid zone are associated with greater potential for visual recovery. In contrast, extensive cavitation, advanced outer retinal atrophy, and substantial Müller cell or photoreceptor loss are associated with limited functional improvement and may compromise long-term anatomical stability. Overall, a FTMH secondary to MacTel2 should be regarded as a distinct form of macular hole in which surgical repair occurs against a background of ongoing macular neurodegeneration. Preoperative evaluation of hole dimensions, foveal cavitation, and outer retinal integrity may assist in prognostication and in identifying eyes with the greatest likelihood of achieving durable anatomical closure and meaningful visual recovery.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of GPT-5 in Detecting and Localizing Acute Ischemic Stroke on Isolated Diffusion-Weighted Imaging: A Retrospective Case-Control Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Multimodal large language models are emerging tools for medical image interpretation, but their performance on isolated diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) for acute ischemic stroke remains largely unexplored. We evaluated GPT-5 for stroke detection and vascular territory classification on preselected representative DWI images using a structured two-step prompting protocol. Methods: This single-center, retrospective, balanced case-control study included 220 cases (110 stroke patients and 110 stroke-negative controls). Four representative axial DWI slices per case were provided without apparent diffusion coefficient maps. Step 1 queried stroke presence and vascular territory; Step 2 queried the middle cerebral artery (MCA) segment-associated territory (M1-M4) following an MCA response. The reference standard was radiologist-neurologist consensus based on full multimodal magnetic resonance imaging, blinded to GPT-5 outputs. Diagnostic performance metrics and Cohen's kappa (κ) were calculated. Results: Stroke detection showed a sensitivity of 100% (95% confidence interval [CI], 96.6-100%), specificity of 83.6% (95% CI, 75.6-89.4%), accuracy of 91.8%, and κ = 0.836. Accuracy was 93.6% for anterior/posterior circulation (κ = 0.838) and 90.9% for vascular territory (κ = 0.799). Conditional MCA segment-associated territory accuracy was 71.6% (53/74; κ = 0.602); end-to-end accuracy was 66.3% (53/80). Exploratory analysis of the 18 false-positive cases identified four overlapping error categories: artifactual and physiologic signal misinterpretation (72.2%), chronic lesion misclassification (27.8%), terminological inconsistency or unsupported report statements (77.8%), and etiological scenarios or unhedged definitive diagnoses (38.9%). Conclusions: GPT-5 achieved high sensitivity and a specificity of 83.6% for stroke classification on preselected representative DWI images using a vascular territory-based diagnostic framework. However, the 16.4% false-positive rate indicates that positive findings require radiologist confirmation. These findings support further evaluation of GPT-5 as a potential clinician-assisted image-interpretation tool but do not establish a clinical decision-support role.

Exploratory analysis of the 18 false-positive cases identified four overlapping error categories: artifactual and physiologic signal misinterpretation (72.2%), chronic lesion misclassification (27.8%), terminological inconsistency or unsupported report statements (77.8%), and etiological scenarios or unhedged definitive diagnoses (38.9%). Conclusions: GPT-5 achieved high sensitivity and a specificity of 83.6% for stroke classification on preselected representative DWI images using a vascular territory-based diagnostic framework. However, the 16.4% false-positive rate indicates that positive findings require radiologist confirmation. These findings support further evaluation of GPT-5 as a potential clinician-assisted image-interpretation tool but do not establish a clinical decision-support role.

title: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Is Associated with Disease Progression in a Surveillance Cohort of Patients with Branch-Duct IPMN.
abstract: Background : A Branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (BD-IPMNs) are common pancreatic precursor lesions requiring varying duration of surveillance because of their potential for malignant transformation. Current risk stratification relies predominantly on imaging-based criteria defined by the Kyoto guidelines, while reliable blood-based biomarkers are lacking. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) has been associated with invasive IPMN in surgical resected cases, but its role in routine BD-IPMN surveillance has not been investigated. This study investigated the association between NLR and disease progression in a large surveillance cohort of patients with BD-IPMN. Methods : This retrospective two-center study included patients with image-based diagnosis of BD-IPMN who underwent at least one further follow-up endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) examination between 2006 and 2026 and had an available differential blood count. Disease progression was defined as the development of new worrisome features (WFs), high-risk stigmata (HRS), pancreatic resection for progressive disease, or IPMN-associated carcinoma. Results : A total of 285 patients undergoing 2207 EUS examinations were included, with a mean EUS surveillance duration of 4.8 years. During follow-up, 63 patients (22.1%) developed at least one WF, 4 (1.4%) developed HRS, 11 (3.9%) underwent pancreatic resection, and 2 (0.7%) developed IPMN-associated carcinoma. NLR was significantly elevated in patients who developed WFs ( p = 0.0023), HRS ( p < 0.0001), underwent pancreatic resection ( p = 0.0006), or had high-grade dysplasia ( p = 0.0002). Baseline continuous NLR showed no significant discriminatory ability for subsequent disease progression (AUC, 0.563; 95% CI, 0.482-0.635; p = 0.136). Patients with an NLR above the cohort median (>2.36) had approximately twofold higher odds of subsequent disease progression (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.02-3.98). Longitudinal analyses demonstrated significant increases in NLR preceding the development of WFs ( p < 0.0001), HRS ( p = 0.0265), and pancreatic resection ( p = 0.0272). Rising NLR was particularly associated with cyst growth, cyst size ≥30 mm, and main pancreatic duct dilation. Conclusions : Elevated and increasing NLR was associated with BD-IPMN progression and correlated with established markers of higher-risk disease. Longitudinal NLR assessment may represent a simple and widely available complementary biomarker for surveillance; however, its modest discriminatory performance warrants prospective validation before clinical implementation.

title: Orbital Fractures at a Level 1 Trauma Center: A Retrospective Epidemiological Analysis of 1489 Consecutive Fracture Records.
abstract: Objectives: Comprehensive epidemiological data on orbital fractures from large full-spectrum series remain scarce. We describe the demographics, mechanisms, fracture anatomy, CT-derived defect morphometry, and clinical findings at presentation of orbital fractures managed at a level 1 trauma center. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 1489 consecutive CT-confirmed orbital fracture records managed at Rambam Health Care Campus, Haifa, Israel, between September 2001 and November 2023. Demographics, mechanism, fracture location, laterality, CT-derived defect dimensions, orbital content herniation, inferior rectus muscle (IRM) involvement on CT, diplopia, concomitant facial fractures, and timing of repair were analyzed. The analysis was planned as descriptive; a single pre-specified comparison (age between sexes) was tested, and no inferential modelling of treatment decisions or outcomes was undertaken. Results: The cohort was 78.6% male (M:F 3.7:1), with a mean age of 36.5 ± 20.0 years; patients aged 18-29 years predominated (33.5%). Females were older than males (46.3 ± 24.6 vs. 33.9 ± 17.7 years; p < 0.001). Falls (33.0%) and assault (26.1%) were the principal mechanisms. The orbital floor was involved in 87.7% of fractures (isolated in 58.6%); mean sagittal and coronal defect diameters were 13.7 ± 6.1 and 13.3 ± 5.1 mm. Content herniation was present in 55.1%, IRM involvement on CT in 14.7%, and diplopia in 17.6%; concomitant facial fractures occurred in 27.9%, and 72.9% underwent repair, at a median of 2 days. Conclusions: In one of the largest single-center orbital fracture cohorts reported, a young-adult male, floor-dominant profile predominated. Herniation, radiological muscle involvement, diplopia, and associated facial fractures were common, indicating the functional and diagnostic complexity of this injury pattern. These descriptive findings characterize the population presenting to a level 1 center; they do not evaluate management strategies and should not be read as establishing surgical indications, thresholds, or optimal timing.

title: Preoperative High-Resolution Ultrasound-Guided Design of the Fibula Osteoseptocutaneous Flap: A Structured Surgeon-Performed Protocol.
abstract: Background/Objectives: The fibula osteoseptocutaneous flap is an established option for head and neck reconstruction. Preoperative planning requires assessment of donor-limb arterial anatomy and localization of cutaneous perforators. This study describes a structured surgeon-performed Conventional High-Frequency Ultrasound (CHFUS) protocol and evaluates its correlation with intraoperative findings. Methods: This retrospective study included patients undergoing reconstruction with a fibula osteoseptocutaneous free flap between January 2024 and December 2025. A standardized two-phase CHFUS workflow was used to assess infrapopliteal arterial anatomy and identify, characterize, and mark perforators at their deep fascial emergence. Preoperative findings were compared with intraoperative anatomy. Results: Ten patients underwent fibula flap reconstruction. Eighteen perforators were mapped, with a mean of 1.80 ± 0.63 per patient. The most common Kim-Lippert vascular pattern was type I (90%). Mean peroneal artery diameter at its origin was 2.83 ± 0.15 mm, and mean dominant perforator diameter at deep fascial emergence was 1.04 ± 0.14 mm. All 10 patients met the predefined anatomical agreement threshold of ≤1 cm (100%; exact two-sided 95% confidence interval, 69.2-100%). No flap required intraoperative redesign because of perforator anatomy. All flaps survived, without partial skin-paddle necrosis, donor-site ischemia, or vascular complications. Conclusions: This structured surgeon-performed CHFUS protocol was feasible and useful for fibula osteoseptocutaneous flap planning, enabling assessment of arterial anatomy, reliable perforator localization, and translation of preoperative findings into skin-paddle design. CHFUS should be considered complementary to CT angiography. Larger prospective studies are required to evaluate interoperator reproducibility and the diagnostic performance of CHFUS for clinically relevant arterial variants.

title: Serial Static Infrared Thermography for Intraoperative and Postoperative Surface-Temperature Monitoring of Free-Flap Skin Islands in Paediatric Craniofacial Reconstruction: A Technical Feasibility Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: This single-patient retrospective study evaluated the technical feasibility of serial infrared thermography (IRT) for intraoperative and postoperative surface-temperature documentation of free-flap skin islands and its descriptive concordance with clinical and vascular assessments. Methods: A 9-year-old boy with Nager syndrome undergoing bilateral temporomandibular joint reconstruction and soft-tissue reconstruction with an anterolateral thigh free flap divided into two skin islands was monitored intraoperatively and postoperatively. Thermograms were acquired using a FLIR T1020 camera (emissivity 0.98) under documented environmental conditions. Intraoperative and postoperative observations were interpreted separately, without normalisation between settings. Mean temperatures within manually delineated regions of interest and inter-island differences were analysed retrospectively and compared descriptively with documented clinical assessment, Doppler ultrasonography, and computed tomography angiography (CTA) findings. Results: Pallor prompted Doppler ultrasonography, followed by CTA; these showed absent right-perforator flow and non-visualisation of that perforator, respectively. The skin did not bleed after puncture. Thermography was performed after these tests and was not taken into account when making the decision about reoperation. IRT demonstrated temperature changes in both skin islands. At 49 h after the initial flap measurement, the mean surface temperature was 26.6 °C in the right skin island and 32.7 °C in the left (absolute difference, 6.1 °C). A focal area of relatively increased surface temperature "hot spot" was identified retrospectively within the viable left skin island; this qualitative observation was exploratory and was not based on a prespecified thermal threshold. Conclusions: Serial IRT was feasible and provided contactless thermal information retrospectively concordant with multimodal perfusion assessment. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish earlier detection, diagnostic accuracy, or a universal thermal threshold; larger prospective studies are required.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Ocular Surface Oncology: A Narrative Review of Multimodal Imaging, Smartphone-Based Screening, and Clinical Decision Support.
abstract: Ocular surface malignancies include ocular surface squamous neoplasia (OSSN), con-junctival melanoma, and conjunctival lymphoma. These rare disorders may threaten vi-sion and, in some cases, life. Early identification may be difficult because malignant le-sions can resemble benign ocular surface conditions. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a potential aid to detection, classi-fication, and referral. This structured narrative review, organized with reference to SANRA principles, synthesizes PubMed/MEDLINE literature on AI applications in ocular surface oncology available through 29 August 2026. We examine slit-lamp photography, anterior segment optical coherence tomography, in vivo confocal microscopy, ultrasound biomicroscopy, and smartphone imaging. Deep-learning models have shown promising performance in selected binary OSSN tasks, whereas multiclass studies report lower sen-sitivity for rare malignancies such as conjunctival melanoma and lymphoma. Smartphone-based screening has also been evaluated in a prospective referral pathway, although the reference standard and verification process limit interpretation of popula-tion-level sensitivity. Dataset imbalance, image-acquisition variability, limited external and prospective validation, explainability, and workflow integration remain barriers to implementation. Future work should prioritize multicenter datasets, standardized acquisition, calibrated thresholds, and prospective human-AI evaluations. Current evidence supports further evaluation of AI as an adjunct for detection and referral, not as a re-placement for specialist assessment or histopathology.

title: Heterogeneity in CT-Based Skeletal Muscle Mass Assessment and Sarcopenia Diagnosis Undermines Comparability in Hepatopancreatobiliary Surgery: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Sarcopenia has emerged as an important prognostic factor in patients undergoing hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) surgery. However, substantial heterogeneity in assessment methods and diagnostic thresholds limits comparability across studies. The aim of this review is to systematically characterize methodological variability in sarcopenia assessment within HPB surgical literature, quantify dispersion in reported cut-off values, and highlight key areas requiring standardization. Methods : A structured search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted to identify studies evaluating sarcopenia in adult patients undergoing surgery for benign or malignant HPB diseases. The included studies assessed skeletal muscle mass with computed tomography (CT)-based measures, rather than sarcopenia as defined in contemporary consensus definitions. Data were extracted regarding imaging modality, anatomical landmarks, muscle indices, normalization strategies and diagnostic thresholds. Between-study variability in skeletal muscle index (SMI) thresholds was quantified using the coefficient of variation (CV). Results : Fifty-three studies comprising 11,613 patients met the inclusion criteria. Thirty-four studies assessed CT-defined low skeletal muscle mass using total skeletal muscle area at the third lumbar vertebral level normalized for height, whereas the remaining studies employed heterogeneous methodologies, including psoas-only measurements and alternative vertebral levels. Reported SMI cut-off values ranged from 36.2 to 53.5 cm 2 /m 2 in males and 29.6 to 41.1 cm 2 /m 2 in females. The CV for male and female cut-offs was 10.9% and 7.6%, respectively. Descriptively, lower CV values were observed in Western cohorts (male 6.5%; female 4.2%) than in Eastern cohorts (male 11.0%; female 9.0%); these values were not formally compared statistically. Considerable dispersion persisted irrespective of the threshold source. Conclusions : Despite the predominance of CT-derived L3 SMI assessment, marked methodological heterogeneity remains in HPB sarcopenia research. Variability in anatomical landmarks, normalization methods, and cut-off values limits reproducibility and constrains meta-analytic synthesis. Harmonization of reporting and threshold selection is essential to clarify the prognostic role of sarcopenia in HPB surgery.

Descriptively, lower CV values were observed in Western cohorts (male 6.5%; female 4.2%) than in Eastern cohorts (male 11.0%; female 9.0%); these values were not formally compared statistically. Considerable dispersion persisted irrespective of the threshold source. Conclusions: Despite the predominance of CT-derived L3 SMI assessment, marked methodological heterogeneity remains in HPB sarcopenia research. Variability in anatomical landmarks, normalization methods, and cut-off values limits reproducibility and constrains meta-analytic synthesis. Harmonization of reporting and threshold selection is essential to clarify the prognostic role of sarcopenia in HPB surgery.

title: CT-Derived Adipose Tissue Biomarkers in Coronary and Carotid Atherosclerosis: A Systematic Review of Dual-Energy, Spectral, and Photon-Counting CT.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Advanced Computed Tomography (CT) enables multiparametric characterization of local perivascular and regional or systemic adipose tissue, potentially providing markers of vascular inflammation and cardiometabolic remodeling beyond conventional assessment of the vessel lumen and plaque. However, evidence remains fragmented across CT technologies, adipose depots and vascular territories. This systematic review evaluated human studies of adipose-tissue biomarkers derived from dual-layer spectral-detector CT (DLSCT), dual-source dual-energy CT (DS-DECT), rapid kVp-switching dual-energy CT (rsDECT), and photon-counting CT (PCCT) in coronary and carotid atherosclerosis. Methods : PubMed and Scopus were systematically searched for English-language human studies published from 1 January 2020, to 13 September 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching of eligible studies and reference-list screening of relevant reviews. Two reviewers independently performed study selection and risk-of-bias assessment. Because of clinical, technical, and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis. Results : Nineteen reports representing 15 likely independent study clusters met the inclusion criteria. DLSCT-derived pericoronary adipose-tissue attenuation; DECT-derived carotid perivascular adipose-tissue parameters; PCCT-derived adipose attenuation, volume, and radiomic features; and spectral measures of hepatic or visceral adiposity were associated with coronary artery disease, stenosis severity, high-risk plaque features, coronary calcification, or symptomatic carotid disease. Reported discrimination estimates were heterogeneous across populations, endpoints, and model structures and were predominantly derived from unvalidated development samples. Conclusions : Advanced CT-derived adipose-tissue biomarkers may complement conventional assessment of the vessel lumen and plaque by characterizing local vessel-adipose interactions and systemic cardiometabolic phenotype. However, current measurements are protocol- and platform-dependent, and clinical utility has not been established. Standardized measurement pipelines, biological validation, and prospective multicenter studies are required before routine clinical implementation.

title: Assessment of Liver Fibrosis Using the Coefficient of Variation on Gadoxetic Acid-Enhanced Hepatobiliary Phase MR Imaging: A Prospective Multicenter Study.
abstract: Background: Accurate non-invasive assessment of liver fibrosis is needed in patients with chronic liver disease. Gadoxetic acid (Gd-EOB-DTPA)-enhanced hepatobiliary phase (HBP) magnetic resonance (MR) imaging reflects hepatocyte function and parenchymal heterogeneity, and the coefficient of variation (CV), which quantifies pixel-level signal inhomogeneity, has been proposed as a quantitative imaging biomarker of liver fibrosis. However, previous studies were retrospective, single-center, and lacked direct pathological validation. Objectives: To investigate the factors associated with CV on HBP images, evaluate the correlation between CV and pathologically confirmed liver fibrosis stage, and compare the diagnostic performance of CV with serum biomarkers, including the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and fibrosis-4 (FIB-4), in a prospective multicenter setting. Methods: This prospective multicenter study was conducted between April 2017 and August 2020 at three medical centers. Ninety-nine participants who underwent Gd-EOB-DTPA-enhanced HBP T1-weighted MRI and liver biopsy or surgery were enrolled. CV was measured on HBP images, and the METAVIR fibrosis stage was used as the reference standard. Univariate and multivariable linear regression analyses, including an additional model adjusted for institution and pathology confirmation method, Welch's analysis of variance with the Games-Howell post hoc test, Spearman's rank correlation analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis with DeLong's method for AUROC comparison, and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) analyses were performed. Results: Ninety-nine participants (64 men and 35 women; mean age, 55.5 ± 15.1 years) were enrolled. In multivariable linear regression analysis adjusted for institution and pathology confirmation method, pathologic fibrosis stage (B = 0.468; 95% CI, 0.358-0.578; p < 0.001) and serum albumin level (B = -0.341; p = 0.015) were independently associated with CV. Spearman's correlation coefficient between CV and fibrosis stage was 0.74 ( p < 0.001). The AUROCs of CV for significant fibrosis (≥F2), advanced fibrosis (≥F3), and cirrhosis (F4) were 0.92, 0.88, and 0.86, respectively (all p < 0.001). CV outperformed APRI and FIB-4 across most fibrosis thresholds ( p < 0.001 to p = 0.045), except for FIB-4 in the diagnosis of ≥F2 fibrosis ( p = 0.09). The intra- and inter-observer ICC values were 0.94 and 0.84, respectively. Conclusions: In this prospective multicenter study with pathologically confirmed fibrosis stages, CV derived from Gd-EOB-DTPA-enhanced HBP MR images showed a strong correlation with liver fibrosis stage and higher diagnostic performance than APRI and FIB-4 across most fibrosis thresholds. Because CV can be calculated from routine clinical MRI acquisitions without additional hardware or blood tests, it may serve as a practical biomarker for non-invasive liver fibrosis assessment. However, because this study was conducted in a Korean cohort with predominantly hepatitis B virus-related liver disease, further validation in other ethnic groups and etiologies is needed.

title: Liver Function Assessment in Oncology: Current Tools for Evaluating Hepatic Reserve and Surgical Decision-Making.
abstract: Accurate assessment of hepatic functional reserve is essential in patients with primary or secondary liver malignancies undergoing liver resection, particularly in the presence of chronic liver disease, chemotherapy-associated liver injury, cholestasis, or portal hypertension. Conventional laboratory parameters and clinical scores, including Child-Pugh, MELD, ALBI, and the combined APRI/ALBI score, provide accessible measures of global hepatic status and risk stratification but do not directly quantify regional function or dynamic metabolic capacity. Complementary approaches include indocyanine green clearance, LiMAx testing, liver stiffness measurement, hepatobiliary scintigraphy, gadoxetic acid-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, and CT/MRI-based future liver remnant volumetry. This narrative review critically examines the strengths, limitations, and clinical applicability of these modalities in the context of contemporary evidence and recommendations. Building on, but extending beyond, the 2023 E-AHPBA-ESSO-ESSR Innsbruck consensus, we incorporate subsequent comparative evidence on blood-based scores and functional imaging and discuss emerging approaches including longitudinal assessment, radiomics, and artificial intelligence. Current evidence supports an individualized, multimodal strategy in which volumetry remains central to surgical planning, while additional functional and portal-hypertension assessment is selected according to the extent of resection, underlying parenchymal disease, previous treatment, and local expertise. No single modality or fixed combination can currently be considered universally superior, highlighting the need for prospective validation of integrated and cost-effective assessment strategies.

title: Association Between Ultrasonographic Evidence of Nerve Entrapment and Pain Outcomes After Nerve Decompression in Painful Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy.
abstract: Objective: To evaluate whether preoperative ultrasonographic evidence of nerve entrapment is associated with pain relief after lower-limb peripheral nerve decompression in patients with painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (PDPN). Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 110 consecutive patients with PDPN who underwent bilateral lower-limb peripheral nerve decompression between February 2023 and June 2024. After three patients were lost to follow-up, 107 were analyzed. Preoperative ultrasonography assessed the bilateral common peroneal and tibial nerves. Patients were classified as ultrasound-positive if at least one examined nerve met the specified focal entrapment criteria and as ultrasound-negative otherwise. Numeric rating scale (NRS) scores were recorded preoperatively and at 7 days, 6 months, and 12 months after surgery. A ≥50% reduction in NRS score at 12 months was defined as pain response. Analysis of covariance and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Results: Ultrasonographic evidence of focal entrapment in at least one examined common peroneal or tibial nerve was identified in 42 patients (39.3%). Mean NRS scores decreased from 7.9 preoperatively to 2.7, 2.5, and 2.7 at 7 days, 6 months, and 12 months, respectively (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). After adjustment for baseline NRS score, the ultrasound-positive group had lower NRS scores at 7 days and 12 months than the ultrasound-negative group; the between-group difference was not statistically significant at 6 months. At 12 months, 77 patients (72.0%) achieved pain response: 35 of 42 ultrasound-positive patients (83.3%) and 42 of 65 ultrasound-negative patients (64.6%). Ultrasound-positive status was associated with higher odds of pain response after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 3.69; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.28-10.67; p = 0.016). Firth bias-reduced logistic regression yielded a similar estimate (OR, 3.32; 95% profile-likelihood CI, 1.26-9.81; p = 0.015). Conclusions: Preoperative ultrasonographic evidence of nerve entrapment was associated with more favorable postoperative pain outcomes after nerve decompression in patients with PDPN. Its potential prognostic value requires prospective validation.

title: Current State of Adjuvant Hormone Therapy in Prostate Cancer and in the Management of Pelvic Nodal Recurrence: A Narrative Review.
abstract: In post-prostatectomy prostate cancer, combining androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with salvage radiotherapy (SRT) significantly improves clinical outcomes, though the absolute benefit varies based on baseline PSA, pathological risk, and treatment design. This review synthesizes findings from key randomized trials and contemporary meta-analyses-including RTOG 9601, SPPORT, GETUG-AFU 16, GETUG-AFU 22, and RADICALS-HD-evaluating the integration and duration of ADT with postoperative irradiation. While systemic therapy consistently enhances biochemical and clinical progression-free survival, a universal overall survival benefit remains uncertain or limited to high-risk cohorts with elevated pre-treatment PSA values. Concurrently, data from the prospective phase II OLIGOPELVIS (GETUG P07) and PEACE V-STORM trials are redefining the standard of care for pelvic nodal oligorecurrent disease detected via next-generation imaging (NGI). Transitioning away from exclusive lifelong ADT or isolated focal metastasis-directed therapy, emerging evidence strongly supports a multimodal paradigm: combining prostate bed RT, whole-pelvis elective nodal irradiation, and a high-dose boost to PET-positive nodes, complemented by a short course of systemic therapy. Ultimately, this narrative review provides clinicians with evidence-based guidance on integrating ADT to maximize regional disease control and delay systemic progression, while successfully sparing the majority of patients from the toxicities of continuous ADT.

title: Bedside Lung Ultrasound for Early Postoperative Risk Stratification for Prolonged Mechanical Ventilation After Liver Transplantation.
abstract: Objectives: Pulmonary complications remain a major determinant of postoperative morbidity following liver transplantation and frequently lead to prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV). This study aimed to evaluate the value of lung ultrasound (LUS) for early postoperative risk stratification of PMV and to develop a multivariable model integrating LUS with conventional clinical variables. Methods: In this prospective cohort study, 116 adults undergoing primary liver transplantation were enrolled. A standardized 12-zone LUS examination was performed within 1-3 h of ICU admission. PMV was defined as the need for mechanical ventilation for ≥24 h. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was constructed by sequentially incorporating perioperative variables and postoperative PaO 2 /FiO 2 , followed by LUS. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis. Results: PMV occurred in 39.7% ( n = 46) of the patients. Those requiring PMV had significantly higher early postoperative LUS scores than patients extubated within 24 h (median: 18.0 vs. 12.0, p < 0.001). LUS scores were inversely correlated with oxygenation (SpO 2 /FiO 2 ratio, ⍴ = -0.615, p < 0.001). LUS remained independently associated with PMV (OR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.27-1.83). LUS alone demonstrated good discrimination (AUC: 0.830). After postoperative PaO 2 /FiO 2 was included in the clinical model, incorporation of LUS significantly improved model discrimination (AUC: 0.935, 95% CI: 0.894-0.976) compared with the model without LUS (AUC: 0.862, DeLong p = 0.011). Decision curve analysis showed greater net benefit of the LUS-integrated model across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. Conclusions: Early postoperative LUS is independently associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation after liver transplantation. Integration of LUS into a multivariable framework provides incremental prognostic information beyond conventional postoperative respiratory assessment and may improve early postoperative risk stratification. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Staged Surgery for Synchronous Proximal Gastric Adenocarcinoma and Pancreatic Head Ductal Adenocarcinoma with an Early Favorable Outcome: A Case Report.
abstract: Background . Synchronous primary gastric cancer and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are uncommon, and published experience with their combined treatment is limited. Proximal gastric adenocarcinoma combined with pancreatic head PDAC presents a particular challenge because resection and reconstruction must address two anatomically separate primary tumors. Materials and Methods . A 62-year-old man with poorly differentiated proximal gastric adenocarcinoma (cT3N0M0) and pancreatic head PDAC (cT3N1M0) received six cycles of neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX. Preoperative ECOG performance status was 0. Treatment comprised proximal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy and double-tract reconstruction and, approximately 10 weeks later, pylorus-preserving pancreatoduodenectomy. Contrast-enhanced CT before the second stage showed no disease progression. Results . Intra-abdominal hemorrhage after proximal gastrectomy required relaparotomy. Histopathological examination confirmed microscopically negative resection margins (R0) for both tumors. Gastric tumor regression was Becker grade 3, indicating minimal or no regression; pancreatic regression was Modified Ryan score 3, indicating a poor or absent response. Six cycles of adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX were reported. At the last reported follow-up, 10 months after the second operation, the patient had no evidence of progression and an ECOG performance status of 0. Conclusions . This case documents the technical feasibility of staged gastric and pancreatic resection after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in a patient with preoperative ECOG performance status 0, with histologically negative resection margins and an early favorable outcome despite a postoperative complication. The reported R0 status describes the morphological assessment of resection margins. Longer follow-up is required to assess durable disease control.

title: Gallstone Ileus Presenting as Small Bowel Obstruction in an Elderly Patient: Diagnostic Approach and Surgical Management.
abstract: Background : Gallstone ileus is an uncommon cause of mechanical intestinal obstruction that predominantly affects older adults. It results from migration of a gallstone through a biliary-enteric fistula, most commonly a cholecystoduodenal fistula. Methods : An 84-year-old woman with hypertension and hypothyroidism presented with a four-day history of right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Laboratory investigations showed a marked inflammatory response and severe renal dysfunction with a substantial reversible acute component, most likely related to volume depletion and reduced renal perfusion. Computed tomography demonstrated an ectopic gallstone impacted in the distal small bowel, proximal bowel dilatation, pneumobilia, and a cholecystoduodenal fistula. Emergency laparotomy confirmed gallstone ileus. After assessment of the operative risk and local anatomy, a one-stage procedure was performed, comprising enterolithotomy, cholecystectomy, division of the fistula, and primary repair of the duodenal defect. Results: Postoperative management included continued monitoring of the admission renal dysfunction, together with treatment of postoperative tracheobronchitis, anemia, electrolyte disturbances, and transient elevation in pancreatic enzymes. These abnormalities were managed with supportive and multidisciplinary care. Renal function, inflammatory markers, and electrolyte concentrations improved substantially before discharge. Pancreatic amylase returned to its reference interval, whereas total α-amylase was below its stated reference interval at discharge, although anemia persisted. The patient was discharged in satisfactory condition on postoperative day 13. Conclusions : Computed tomography enabled preoperative diagnosis and characterization of the cholecystoduodenal fistula. Although a one-stage operation was feasible in this patient, this single outcome does not establish its superiority. Surgical management should be individualized according to the patient's physiological condition, comorbidities, and intraoperative findings.

title: An Overview of Cushing's Syndrome Caused by Ectopic Adrenocorticotropin Secretion.
abstract: Ectopic Cushing's syndrome (ECS) causes 10% to 20% of all cases of endogenous hypercortisolism. It is caused by the aberrant secretion of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) or corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) due to the presence of an ectopic tumor. The latter is usually a neuroendocrine (NEN) tumor (mostly thoracic NENs such as bronchial NEN neoplasms, thymic NEN neoplasms, small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC), or pancreatic NEN neoplasms). Clinical presentation is heterogeneous: an aggressive phenotype, typically driven by rapidly growing, poorly differentiated tumors such as small-cell lung carcinoma, manifests with severe symptoms of acute onset, predominant myopathy, resistant arterial hypertension, hypokalemia, and severe hyperpigmentation, usually without the centripetal obesity typical of Cushing's syndrome; conversely, an indolent phenotype, more often related to well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms such as bronchial carcinoids, may present with the classic centripetal fat distribution, facial plethora, and purple striae also seen in Cushing's disease, making clinical distinction between the two difficult. The diagnosis of ECS can be cumbersome and time-consuming. Once hypercortisolism is confirmed, the most critical step is to distinguish patients with an ectopic source of ACTH from those with pituitary adenoma. Dynamic endocrine tests such as the high-dose dexamethasone suppression test, CRH stimulation tests, desmopressin tests, and bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) can be helpful in the differential diagnosis. BIPSS is considered the gold standard for distinguishing a pituitary from a non-pituitary source of ACTH: the absence of a central-to-peripheral ACTH gradient supports, but does not by itself localize or confirm, an ectopic source. Tumor localization is achieved by a multimodality imaging protocol, including initial high-resolution computed tomography (CT) scans, followed by functional imaging, mainly Gallium-68-labeled somatostatin receptor positron emission tomography (PET)/CT scans. However, in 10-20% of these patients, the tumors cannot be localized. The treatment of ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism is two-fold: one is to immediately control hypercortisolism to prevent life-threatening complications (opportunistic infections and thromboembolism), and the second is to definitively treat the tumor. Medical treatment with steroidogenesis inhibitors, including metyrapone, ketoconazole, and osilodrostat, or surgical management (bilateral adrenalectomy) can be effective in immediately controlling hypercortisolism. Definitive surgical resection of the tumor is the hoped-for final treatment. The prognosis is variable, depending on the nature of the underlying neoplasm, ranging from excellent in patients with resected bronchial carcinoids to dismal in those with SCLC.

title: Outcome-Specific Performance of HALP, AIMS65, Glasgow-Blatchford, and Rockall Scores in Emergency Department Patients with Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives : The Hemoglobin-Albumin-Lymphocyte-Platelet (HALP) score integrates hematologic, nutritional, immune, and platelet parameters, but its prognostic value in acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) remains uncertain. We compared the performance of HALP with AIMS65, Glasgow-Blatchford Score (GBS), and Rockall scores. Methods : We retrospectively studied consecutive adults with endoscopy-confirmed UGIB presenting to the emergency department from January 2021 through December 2024. Outcomes were in-hospital mortality, packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion within 24 h, and composite severe UGIB, defined as ≥2 PRBC units transfused within 24 h or UGIB-related intensive care unit admission. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and areas under the curve (AUCs); pairwise comparisons used the correlated-sample DeLong test. Firth-penalized logistic regression assessed the adjusted association between HALP and in-hospital mortality. Results : Of 209 patients, 24 (11.5%) died and 36 (17.2%) had variceal bleeding. For mortality, AUCs were 0.580 for inverse HALP, 0.802 for AIMS65, 0.733 for GBS, and 0.731 for Rockall. For 24-h PRBC transfusion, AUCs were 0.629, 0.642, 0.814, and 0.511, respectively; for severe UGIB, they were 0.622, 0.594, 0.781, and 0.501. No statistically significant adjusted association between HALP and mortality was observed (aOR, 0.91 per 10-point increase; p = 0.571). Conclusions : HALP showed limited discrimination across the evaluated UGIB outcomes, and no statistically significant adjusted association with mortality was observed. AIMS65 had the highest observed AUC point estimate for mortality, although its AUC did not differ significantly from those of GBS or Rockall. GBS had the highest AUCs for PRBC transfusion and severe UGIB. These findings support outcome-specific selection of UGIB risk scores and do not support the use of HALP as a stand-alone risk-stratification tool without external validation.

title: Artificial Intelligence in 3D Aortic CTA Segmentation for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Management: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the reference imaging modality for diagnosis, endovascular planning, and surveillance of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs), but conventional assessment remains time-consuming, operator-dependent, and limited by complex anatomy. This narrative review examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in three-dimensional aortic CTA segmentation for AAA management. The narrative synthesis drew on literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and the Cochrane Library, with the original search covering January 2000 to July 2026. Ten primary studies from the existing bibliography were characterized in a study-level table, and reported Dice coefficients were displayed for nine studies. Current evidence indicates that AI-based segmentation, particularly using convolutional neural networks, U-Net-derived models, and nnU-Net frameworks, can improve the speed and reproducibility of aortic lumen, wall, thrombus, branch vessel, endograft, and aneurysm sac delineation. These techniques may support more accurate morphometric measurements, device sizing, procedural planning, quantitative surveillance, and the development of advanced imaging biomarkers. However, available studies remain heterogeneous in datasets, anatomical evaluation, imaging protocols, validation strategies, and reported performance metrics, limiting direct comparison and clinical generalizability. AI-assisted 3D segmentation represents a promising tool for transforming CTA from descriptive imaging into quantitative decision support, but robust multicenter validation, workflow integration, and expert supervision remain essential before widespread clinical adoption.

title: Variational Autoencoders for Medical Image Segmentation: A Review.
abstract: Medical image segmentation plays an important role in healthcare because it transforms raw scans into useful information for diagnosis and treatment planning. Despite the strong performance of deep learning, most supervised segmentation methods require large amounts of pixel-level annotations and may become less reliable when imaging modalities are incomplete or when prediction uncertainty is not properly considered. Variational autoencoders (VAEs) are deep learning models that were proposed to address some of these limitations, as they can learn probabilistic latent representations capable of capturing meaningful structure in medical images. This review provides a structured survey of how VAEs are applied to medical image segmentation and organizes them around five roles: generating synthetic samples for data augmentation, integrating variational representations into segmentation networks for representation learning and regularization, localizing pathology through reconstruction-based anomaly detection, fusing multiple modalities in a shared latent space for missing-modality segmentation, and learning anatomical shape priors for segmentation correction and quality control. In this work, the reviewed literature includes both approaches where the VAE directly contributes to the segmentation and related applications that support the segmentation pipeline, such as data generation, preprocessing or weak localization. We also summarize the main datasets and evaluation metrics used in the field and discuss current challenges, including blurry reconstructions, the use of hybrid architectures in several reviewed studies, the strong concentration of studies on brain MRI, the limited use of uncertainty, and the possible complementary roles of VAEs alongside diffusion and foundation models. Overall, the studies reviewed here suggest that VAEs can serve as parts of larger systems, where they provide structured representations and help handle missing modalities. Conditional models trained to predict masks can also generate multiple plausible segmentations, which may reflect variation among annotations when the training data capture it.

title: Vision-Language Models in Ultrasound Imaging: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Ultrasound vision-language models (US-VLMs) must interpret operator-dependent images and dynamic examinations while linking visual evidence to clinical language. This review synthesizes 32 formally published studies identified through a three-database search. We apply an operational three-axis taxonomy: the interaction axis identifies the primary image-text computation, the learning axis records ultrasound-specific training objectives, and grounding granularity specifies the finest documented visual-linguistic correspondence. Study-level assignments and rationales make these distinctions reproducible. We compare task-specific results without ranking models across incompatible cohorts, endpoints, and metrics. Dataset analysis separates acquisition volume from independent clinical diversity, and a seven-domain risk-of-bias appraisal identifies limitations in reporting of patient-level partitioning and development-test overlap. We also distinguish retrospective performance, including external-cohort results, from evidence that assistance improves clinical decisions or workflows. Current systems support diverse ultrasound tasks, but clinical claims require evidence grounding, uncertainty assessment, and validation matched to the intended use.

title: Hierarchical Reasoning Gates for Multimodal Large Language Models in Dental Image Interpretation: A Prompt-Level Protocol for Improving Accuracy.
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have been used to support dental image interpretation, but performance may depend on prompt structure. We proposed Hierarchical Reasoning Gates (HRG), a prompt-level protocol organizing image interpretation into sequential stages with validation before progression. Forty anonymized panoramic radiographs of impacted mandibular molars were analyzed using three prompt architectures: P1, zero-shot natural language; P2, a five-step structured workflow followed by a final internal-validation checkpoint; and P3, HRG with 10 macro-stages and 35 procedural control blocks. Outputs were compared with expert radiology reference reports using five predefined variables. Mean Total Score was 3.52 ± 0.85, 3.58 ± 0.71, and 4.35 ± 0.74 for P1, P2, and P3, respectively; Full Accuracy was 10.0%, 5.0%, and 50.0%. Reports with errors in three or more variables occurred in 12.5%, 7.5%, and 0%, respectively. Only Apparent Anatomical Relationship differed significantly across prompts after Holm adjustment. Test-retest repeatability was high for several variables but lower for Apparent Anatomical Relationship in P3. HRG was associated with higher image-interpretation performance and fewer complex error patterns, although higher performance did not uniformly translate into greater repeatability. These findings support gated prompt design for controlling dependent steps in MLLM-based image analysis, while clinical use still requires expert supervision.

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence Assistance on Radiologist Performance in CT-Based Pulmonary Nodule Detection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Detection Accuracy Studies.
abstract: Introduction Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related death; prompt detection and monitoring of pulmonary nodules through computed tomography (CT) is critical to prevent mortality. CT interpretation is time-intensive and can be prone to fatigue-related errors. The application of artificial intelligence (AI) may aid in the enhanced detection of pulmonary nodules when used in conjunction with radiologists. Thus, possibly decreasing interpretation time and enhancing diagnostic reliability. However, studies have reported uncertainty regarding the extent to which true positives are always diagnosed, as studies have indicated an increase in false positive rates with AI-assisted pulmonary nodule detection. This systematic review and meta-analysis focuses on the impact of AI assistance on sensitivity and false positive rates in comparison to unaided reading. Methodology Adhering to the PRISMA guidelines, an intensive literature search was carried out on Cochrane, PubMed, Medline and Embase. Research composed of studies that compared AI-assisted reading to unaided radiologists in the context of nodule detection, which also provided additional outcomes that were utilised in the secondary outcome analysis. ROBINS-1 tool was used to assess risk of bias and data quality. Risk ratios and risk differences with 95% CI were reported for dichotomous outcomes, whereas mean differences with 95% CI were utilised for continuous outcomes. Sensitivity analyses were performed for the imputation of missing standard deviations. Results Seven studies reported mean sensitivity in either second reader (SR) mode or concurrent reader (CR) mode. Five of the included studies implemented second reader designs; AI-assisted sensitivity ranged from 38% to 85.66%, whereas unassisted reading sensitivity ranged from 20.9% to 73.46%. Additionally, three studies reported concurrent reading, with AI-assisted reading ranging from 80% to 84%, while unassisted reading varied from 64% to 72%. According to our research, AI-assisted reading had a significantly higher sensitivity (RR of 1.39; CI 95% 1.08-1.79; p = 0.01; I 2 = 95%). Five studies reported false positives per scan. Four reported a numerical increase with AI assistance, but incomplete variance reporting and study heterogeneity precluded quantitative pooling. Reading time was increased under AI assistance as a second reader (MD 77.54; CI 95% -57.50 to 212.6, p = 0.132; I 2 = 64.9%) but did not yield significance. Additionally, AI-assisted reading under concurrent reading did not yield statistical significance for reading time (MD -11.39; 95% CI -498.7 to 476.0, p = 0.816; I 2 = 41.3%). Conclusions AI-assisted reading significantly improves sensitivity for pulmonary nodule detection compared to unaided reading, but the trade-offs with false positives and workflow disruption remain uncertain. Substantial heterogeneity and the limited number of studies preclude definitive clinical recommendations. These findings should be considered exploratory, and the implementation of AI in lung cancer screening requires prospective validation.

title: Renal Venous Anatomy in 192 Human Kidneys: Morphometry, Hilar Topography, and Anatomical Variants.
abstract: Renal venous anatomy is relevant to nephrectomy, living-donor evaluation, and retroperitoneal surgery. Classical descriptions often present a single renal vein on each side, whereas published series show that additional veins, retroaortic and circumaortic courses, and variable hilar tributaries are common. This study describes formation patterns, morphometry, and variants in four separate, non-overlapping methodological series of surgical specimens and imaging examinations, with particular attention to the termination of the posterior primary venous branch, the types of venous anastomosis, and the relation of the vein to the artery at the hilum. We examined 192 adult human kidneys (93 right, 99 left) in four separate methodological series, with no kidney examined by more than one technique: anatomical dissection of nephrectomy specimens ( n = 64), methacrylate injection and corrosion casting of nephrectomy specimens ( n = 93), contrast-enhanced CT angiography ( n = 23), and barium injection with radiography of nephrectomy specimens ( n = 12). The kidney was the unit of analysis. Because some right and left kidneys may have originated from the same individual and the pairing structure could not be reconstructed, right- and left-sided findings are reported descriptively, without inferential side comparisons. Each feature was analysed only in the kidneys in which it could be assessed. The four techniques differ in their ability to detect small tributaries and anastomoses, and frequencies pooled across methods are descriptive. Among 122 kidneys assessed for hilar formation, the renal vein was formed of two primary trunks in 76/122 (62.3%; 95% CI 53.4-70.4), three trunks in 34/122 (27.9%), and four trunks in 12/122 (9.8%). The confluence was assessed in 110 kidneys and was intrasinusal in 40/110 (36.4%), juxtahilar in 34/110 (30.9%), and extrarenal in 36/110 (32.7%). A posterior primary venous branch was present in 56/122 (45.9%): 19/50 right (38.0%) and 37/72 left (51.4%); it joined the already formed main trunk in 32/56 and took part in the confluence in 14/56. In 90 kidneys the main vein lay anterior to the artery in 42/90 (46.7%). In the descriptive morphometric summary of 78 veins, mean length was 6.9 cm on the left (range 4.8-12.5) and 2.9 cm on the right (range 1.5-5.5). At least one venous anastomosis was recorded in 77/192 kidneys (40.1%; 95% CI 33.4-47.2; pooled across methods): 45/93 right (48.4%; 95% CI 38.5-58.4) and 32/99 left (32.3%; 95% CI 23.9-42.0). Multiple renal veins were identified in 16/116 assessable kidneys (13.8%), including 14/52 right (26.9%) and 2/64 left (3.1%). A retroaortic left renal vein was seen in 2/42 assessed left veins (4.8%), and a complete circumaortic ring in one left specimen. The renal vein was often formed of more than one primary trunk, a posterior branch was present in about half of the kidneys assessed, and multiple veins predominated on the right, in line with previous surgical and imaging series. The more specific contributions of this material are the posterior-branch termination map, the classification of anastomosis types, and the vein-artery counts at the hilum. The study is anatomical and descriptive. It does not measure surgical outcomes and does not show that additional venous imaging is required in every patient.

title: Engineering a Multi-Dimensional Thermally Conductive Network to Enhance the Thermo-Mechanical Stability of Concrete.
abstract: Reliable thermo-mechanical performance is typically required in intensive thermal management applications, such as thermal energy storage systems and concrete-structured data centers; however, there is usually a trade-off between thermal conductivity and strength when designing thermally conductive concrete. To address the critical demand for concrete that combines high thermal conductivity with excellent structural stability after thermal loading, a novel multi-dimensional thermally conductive network was constructed by incorporating one-dimensional steel fibers and two-dimensional graphite-modified recycled aggregates to form a synergistic composite (SFRHCC). Results demonstrate that the thermal and mechanical stability of SFRHCC subjected to 200 °C was substantially improved compared with the unmodified reference. Specifically, after thermal treatment at 200 °C, SFRHCC restricted its thermal conductivity loss to only 7.6%, in stark contrast to the 28.2% reduction observed in ordinary recycled aggregate concrete (RAC). Furthermore, SFRHCC retained 92.0% and 91.3% of its reference compressive and splitting tensile strengths, vastly outperforming the unmodified reference (which retained only 75.0% and 72.4%, respectively). Both X-ray computed tomography (X-CT) and Euclidean distance transform (EDT) characterizations elucidate a high-density linear-planar overlapping network with an overall spatial connectivity of 9.94%, where the soft graphite coating layer accommodates thermal mismatch deformations and restricts volumetric fluctuations. This structural integrity effectively transforms the interfacial failure mode from simple weak-interface debonding to cohesive matrix tearing. These findings offer a promising materials design strategy for developing structural-functional integrated concrete for thermal management applications.

title: Cold-Welding and Over-Welding in Polyethylene Pipe Butt Fusion Joints: Formation Mechanisms, Structure-Property Degradation, and Emerging Microwave-Based Detection Strategies.
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) pipes are extensively used in gas- and water-distribution systems because of their corrosion resistance, toughness, and installation flexibility. However, the field reliability of PE pipeline systems often depends on the quality of butt fusion joints, whose integrity is highly sensitive to welding parameters and thermal history. Among process-induced defects, cold welding and over-welding are particularly critical because they are usually concealed, difficult to identify by visual inspection or short-term pressure testing, and strongly associated with long-term brittle failure. Existing reviews have discussed butt fusion joining or polymer non-destructive testing in a broad sense, yet a defect-oriented synthesis linking process deviation, interfacial evolution, material degradation, and microwave response remains limited. This review therefore focuses specifically on cold welding and over-welding as the two most safety-critical hidden defects in PE butt fusion joints. First, the paper summarises how insufficient heat input, poor wetting, and limited molecular-chain interdiffusion lead to weak interfacial healing and low effective entanglement density, whereas excessive heat input and unfavourable thermal history promote chain scission, thermo-oxidative degradation, abnormal recrystallisation, and microvoid formation. It then compares how these mechanisms influence tensile behaviour, slow crack growth resistance, and long-term service performance. On this basis, conventional radiography and ultrasonics, phased-array ultrasonics, nonlinear acoustics, and microwave non-destructive testing (MNDT) are critically compared. Particular emphasis is placed on the structure-property-signal pathway that links local perturbations in complex permittivity to changes in microwave scattering parameters, including |S11|, |S21|, phase drift, resonance shift, and quality-factor reduction. Finally, a hierarchical evaluation framework is proposed to connect microwave features with defect severity and engineering decisions, and the major barriers to wider engineering adoption-benchmark datasets, quantitative inversion, lift-off robustness, and standardisation-are discussed. By organising the field around a mechanism-based structure-property-signal framework, this review aims to provide a more rigorous basis for defect-oriented quality control and future intelligent inspection of PE butt fusion joints.

title: Temporal Change: Evaluation of Brain Atrophy in Patients with Radiologically Isolated Syndrome Using volBrain.
abstract: Background and Objective: Radiologically isolated syndrome (RIS) is characterized by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings suggestive of multiple sclerosis (MS) in individuals without a history of clinical demyelinating events. Increasing evidence indicates that structural brain abnormalities may be present in RIS before the development of overt neurological symptoms. However, most previous studies have employed cross-sectional designs, limiting the ability to characterize the temporal evolution of neurodegenerative changes. This study aimed to investigate longitudinal changes in global, regional, and lobar brain volumes in individuals with RIS using serial MRI examinations obtained at least six months apart. Methods: Patients with RIS who had undergone two 3 Tesla (3T) brain MRI examinations separated by an interval of at least six months were retrospectively identified. Three-dimensional (3D) T1-weighted MRI scans obtained at both time points were analyzed using the volBrain pipeline of the volBrain platform to quantify global, regional, and lobar brain volumes. Longitudinal volumetric changes were expressed as annualized percentage volume changes. The number of T2 lesions and total T2 lesion volume were additionally assessed, and their associations with longitudinal brain volume changes were investigated. Results: A total of 28 patients with RIS were included. After correction for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure, significant annual volume loss was observed in total brain volume ( p = 0.043), total cerebrum volume ( p = 0.033), right cerebrum volume ( p = 0.033), left cerebrum volume ( p = 0.044), total thalamic volume ( p = 0.033), right thalamic volume ( p = 0.047), and left thalamic volume ( p = 0.043). No significant associations were observed between annualized brain volume changes and follow-up duration, total or regional T2 lesion counts, or total T2 lesion volume. Similarly, annualized brain volume changes did not differ significantly between subgroups defined according to MRI progression, the presence of gadolinium-enhancing lesions, or the presence of spinal cord lesions. Conclusions: Longitudinal volumetric analysis demonstrated progressive brain volume loss involving both global and regional structures in patients with RIS. These findings provide further evidence of measurable longitudinal structural brain changes in RIS before the development of clinically overt demyelinating disease. Larger longitudinal studies incorporating appropriate control groups are warranted to further characterize the temporal trajectory of volumetric changes in RIS.

title: Supramalleolar Osteotomy for Varus Ankle Osteoarthritis: A Contemporary Narrative Review.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Varus ankle osteoarthritis (OA) is most commonly post-traumatic and is characterized by asymmetric degeneration and medial overload of the tibiotalar joint. Supramalleolar osteotomy (SMOT) is a joint-preserving procedure that aims to restore mechanical alignment, redistribute joint contact forces, and delay, or potentially avoid, total ankle replacement (TAR) or ankle arthrodesis (AA). However, the optimal choice of technique and amount of correction remain debated, particularly in complex multiplanar deformities. Materials and Methods: This narrative review summarizes current evidence on SMOT for varus ankle OA. Relevant clinical, radiographic, biomechanical, imaging, and surgical studies were selected and synthesized narratively, with particular emphasis on deformity classification, location of the center of rotation of angulation (CORA), joint congruency, surgical technique, clinical outcomes, complications, and treatment planning. Results: SMOT provides reliable pain relief and functional improvement in patients with Takakura-Tanaka stage 2-3A ankle OA, with reported mid-term survival rates of 88-93%. The choice of technique should be guided by the location of the deformity, the degree of talar tilt, and overall limb alignment. In selected cases, a concomitant fibular osteotomy improves talar reduction and medial unloading. Three-dimensional planning and patient-specific instrumentation may improve the accuracy of correction. Conclusions: SMOT is an effective joint-preserving treatment for varus ankle OA, provided that the deformity is accurately analyzed and patients are carefully selected. This review proposes a simplified, stepwise treatment algorithm, supported by illustrations, to help surgeons select the most appropriate osteotomy technique according to the deformity pattern.

title: Shear-Wave Elastography in Musculoskeletal Pain: Current Evidence and Clinical Applications for Tissue Stiffness Assessment.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Shear-wave elastography (SWE) is a quantitative ultrasound technique that estimates tissue stiffness based on the propagation velocity of shear waves. In musculoskeletal pain, it can provide biomechanical information that complements clinical examination and conventional ultrasound, although its relationship with pain has not been fully established. Materials and Methods : A narrative review was conducted of the literature indexed in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and PEDro on SWE and musculoskeletal pain. Priority was given to studies with the strongest evidence and the greatest clinical relevance. Results : SWE allows for the assessment of muscles, tendons, fascia and peripheral nerves, but its results depend on technical and biological factors, such as position, tension, muscle contraction, probe orientation and the equipment used. The evidence is more consistent in conditions with known tissue alterations, such as plantar fasciitis, Achilles or patellar tendinopathy and carpal tunnel syndrome, where it can support diagnosis and may contribute to clinical assessment and treatment monitoring. In other conditions, such as spinal pain and myofascial pain, where the structure causing the clinical symptoms is not so well defined, SWE findings are more heterogeneous. Currently, there are no fully accepted ultrasound parameters of clinical relevance, and comparisons between studies remain limited by methodological variability. Conclusions : SWE is a useful complementary tool in musculoskeletal pain, but not yet a standalone diagnostic modality or an objective measure of pain. Its clinical role will depend on standardized protocols, validated reference values, and higher-quality studies assessing its diagnostic, prognostic, and treatment-monitoring value.

title: Optimizing Indocyanine Green Fluorescence Cholangiography in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials on Dose, Timing, Route, Efficacy, and Safety.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Near-infrared fluorescence cholangiography with indocyanine green (ICG) has been proposed as an adjunct for improving biliary anatomy recognition during laparoscopic cholecystectomy. However, uncertainty remains regarding its comparative efficacy, operative value, safety, and optimal route, dose, and timing. Materials and Methods : A systematic review was conducted to identify randomized comparative and dose-finding studies evaluating ICG fluorescence cholangiography during laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Outcomes included visualization of the cystic duct, common hepatic duct, common bile duct, biliary junctions, operative time, time to critical anatomical identification, conversion or bailout procedures, length of stay, bile duct injury, bile leak, and ICG-related adverse events. Clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesized descriptively. Results : Eighteen studies were included. ICG improved visualization of selected biliary structures compared with white-light imaging, particularly before dissection, whereas differences versus radiographic intraoperative cholangiography were less pronounced. Operative effects were inconsistent: several studies reported shorter cholangiography duration or earlier anatomical identification, without consistent reductions in total operative time or length of stay. Bile duct injuries and bile leaks were infrequent, but event numbers were insufficient to establish a protective effect or comparative safety. Selected dose comparisons suggested reduced hepatic background fluorescence with lower doses, although findings depended on administration timing and imaging platform. Interpretation was limited by subjective visualization assessment, risk of bias, and heterogeneous patient populations. Conclusions : ICG fluorescence cholangiography improves visualization of selected biliary structures, but improved visualization should not be equated with demonstrated clinical benefit. Evidence remains insufficient to establish reductions in bile duct injury, conversion, or postoperative morbidity, or a universally optimal route, dose, or timing regimen.

title: Intraoperative Neurophysiological Monitoring During Continuous Radiofrequency Treatment of Morton's Neuroma: Complete Ablation.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Morton's neuroma is a compressive neuropathy of the common plantar digital nerve that most frequently affects the third intermetatarsal space. Continuous radiofrequency (RF) ablation has reported success rates of approximately 80-85%; however, recent histological evidence suggests that RF does not consistently achieve complete neural ablation. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring of sensory nerve action potentials (SNAPs) to optimize the outcomes of continuous RF ablation in the treatment of Morton's neuroma. Materials and Methods : This prospective case series included 22 patients (30 neuromas) treated with ultrasound-guided continuous RF ablation combined with intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring. SNAPs were recorded before, during, and after each RF application until complete abolition of sensory nerve conduction was confirmed. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the Foot Function Index (FFI), and the Giannini Interdigital Neuroma Clinical Evaluation Score at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Results : At the 12-month follow-up, satisfactory outcomes (Giannini score ≥60) were achieved in 86.7% of neuromas (26/30). The mean VAS pain score decreased from 8.67 preoperatively to 1.67 at 12 months. Among the seven neuromas with previous unsuccessful RF treatment, all achieved satisfactory outcomes following the monitored procedure. The four cases with poor outcomes were predominantly associated with a positive anesthetic suppression test, suggesting concomitant mechanical metatarsalgia rather than treatment failure. After excluding cases with likely diagnostic misclassification, the adjusted success rate increased to 96.3%. Conclusions : Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring enables real-time confirmation of complete sensory nerve ablation during continuous RF treatment. Its main potential value appears to lie in patients with previous unsuccessful conventional RF, all of whom achieved satisfactory outcomes in this series. Persistent postoperative symptoms appeared to be more closely related to concomitant forefoot pathology than to technical limitations of the RF procedure.

title: A Preliminary Novel CBCT-Based Staging System for Temporo-Mandibular Joint Disorders-A Systematic Review.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are heterogeneous conditions that may involve structural alterations of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). Although cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) enables detailed assessment of osseous structures, existing classifications mainly address clinical diagnosis, internal derangement, or isolated imaging findings. This review aimed to identify recurrent TMJ osseous changes and develop a practical CBCT-based staging system. Materials and Methods : The review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched, supplemented by citation and grey-literature searches. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and AMSTAR 2, while evidence certainty was evaluated using GRADE. Recurrent imaging findings, clinical correlations, prognostic implications, and therapeutic perspectives were synthesized to develop the proposed scale. Results : Sixty-seven peer-reviewed studies were included, while 12 grey-literature records were retained as complementary evidence. Frequently reported findings included condylar flattening, erosion, sclerosis, osteophytes, cortical alterations, subchondral cystic changes, joint-space abnormalities, remodeling, dimensional reduction, and deformation. Imaging-clinical correlations were heterogeneous. The synthesis supported a four-stage system ranging from preserved osseous morphology (Stage I), through early positional/adaptive changes (Stage II) and established remodeling (Stage III), to advanced structural degeneration with marked deformation and joint-space collapse (Stage IV). Conclusions : CBCT-detectable TMJ osseous changes can be organized into a four-stage severity framework intended to standardize structural assessment. The scale should complement, rather than replace, clinical diagnosis or MRI evaluation and requires external and longitudinal validation before routine clinical use.
